benchmarks.name: 00_dense_la_lu_decomp
benchmarks.input_form: ONE dense square matrix A over R^(NxN), row-major in a flat std::vector<double> of exactly N*N entries, factorized IN PLACE into the packed L\U (unit-diagonal L strictly below the diagonal, U on and above it). Exactly one relevant dimension: the side length N. Values: uniform i.i.d. in [-10, 10] (fillRand, unseeded rand(), deterministic per process). No second operand, no index vectors, no derived counts.
benchmarks.min_size: 0 — there is no mathematical size floor. N=0 (empty factorization) and N=1 (output = input, no division ever executes, valid even for A=[0]) are both DEFINED and verified. N=2 is the smallest N at which a division executes and therefore the smallest N at which the leading-principal-minor precondition actually binds. Valid size FORM: any integer N >= 0; the buffer length must be exactly N*N.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — harness-forced, thesis/config/config.yaml stages.enhanced_tests.max_spec_size (validation rejects larger specs). Operation/budget-forced far below that: 2048 (2560 measured 14.56 s / 21.49 s > the 10 s oracle budget). benchmarks.special_conditions: (1) The size parameter is the matrix SIDE LENGTH N, not an element count: the driver allocates three N*N buffers (cpu.cc:53-55) from TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(512) (cpu.cc:51). (2) NO power-of-two requirement — any N is a valid container (contrast fft). (3) DOMAIN OF THE UNPIVOTED ORACLE: A must admit an LU factorization without row interchanges, i.e. all leading principal minors of order 1..N-1 must be non-zero. Order N MAY vanish — a singular A whose first N-1 leading minors are non-zero factorizes finitely, because the last pivot is never used as a divisor (verified on [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]: 0 NaN, 0 Inf). Violation at any order k <= N-1 divides by zero and poisons the reference (verified at N=3: A[0][0]=0 -> 2 NaN + 4 Inf; zero 2x2 leading minor -> 2 Inf). (4) COMPARISON-INDUCED condition, not currently satisfiable by the driver's own generator: validate() compares with an ABSOLUTE epsilon 1e-3 (cpu.cc:76), so the input must additionally keep max|packed L\U| below ~1e3 for that to mean ~1e-6 relative. Uniform-random input does not: measured max|L\U| reaches 2.1e7 at N=512 and 1.9e6 at N=2048 from max|A|=10.
benchmarks.size_semantics: size = matrix SIDE LENGTH N. Element count is N^2 (the row-major buffer), memory in validate() is 3 * N^2 * 8 bytes (A, A_correct, A_test), oracle work is ~N^3/3 FMAs. A spec size of 2048 therefore means a 2048x2048 matrix = 4,194,304 doubles = 33.6 MB per buffer, NOT 2048 elements.
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(N^3) time on Theta(N^2) data, with a sequential dependency depth of N elimination steps. Exactly N(N-1)/2 divisions and (N-1)N(2N-1)/6 multiply-subtract pairs, i.e. ~N^3/3 FMAs / ~2N^3/3 flops. Right-looking kij form: step k performs a rank-1 update on the (N-k-1)^2 trailing submatrix; inner loop is unit-stride in row-major, so it vectorizes and the kernel becomes memory-bound once N^2*8 bytes exceed LLC.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases: DEFINED (mathematically valid, oracle finite — all verified by execution): N=0, empty matrix, empty output, alternative LU agrees trivially. N=1, ANY value including A=[0] — the inner loops never run, so no division occurs; the correct packed answer is A unchanged (L=[1], U=[a]). Singular A whose leading minors of order 1..N-1 are all non-zero (e.g. [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]) — the zero pivot appears only at step N-1, which is never a divisor: 0 NaN, 0 Inf. N=2 with the alternating pattern (rows [-10,10],[10,-10], det=0): defined, 0 NaN. NOT DEFINED (leading minor of order <= N-1 is zero; the factorization does not exist and the oracle emits NaN/Inf): all_zeros for N>=2 (12 of 16 entries NaN at N=4); all_same at THIS call site for N>=2 — enhancedMidValue(-10,10) = -10 + 20/2 = 0.0 exactly (enhanced-fill.hpp:148), so all_same IS all_zeros here (identical 12/16 NaN); alternating for N>=3 (rank 2, 6 NaN at N=4); extreme_values for N>=3 (+/-DBL_MAX, rank-deficient plus overflow, 6 NaN at N=4); any matrix with a zero leading minor at order <= N-1. SPURIOUS: the ascending ramp is mathematically rank 2 hence singular for N>=3, but at N=4 it produced no NaN because rounding leaves the third pivot non-zero — a numerically accidental pass on a mathematically out-of-domain input. Consequence for grading: a non-finite REFERENCE index is SKIPPED, not failed, by reportAndCompareWith (utilities.hpp contract A1b), so on all_zeros/all_same/alternating/extreme_values at N>=3 most positions are vacuous and ANY candidate passes there — the BL-17 mechanism already recorded for benchmark 49. static_base_sizes [0, 1, 2, 7] (config.yaml) means sizes 0/1/2 are emitted for this benchmark automatically; 0 and 1 are genuinely meaningful here and must NOT be excluded.

benchmarks.name: 01_dense_la_solve
benchmarks.input_form: Dense real linear system A·x = b. A is an N×N matrix of `double` stored ROW-MAJOR in a flat `std::vector<double>` of N*N entries (element (i,j) at A[i*N+j]); b and x are `std::vector<double>` of N entries each. Signature: `void solveLinearSystem(std::vector<double> const& A, std::vector<double> const& b, std::vector<double>& x, size_t N)`. Relevant dimensions: ONE free parameter, the matrix order N (= side length). Derived: element count N*N (matrix) + 2N (vectors); oracle work ~N^3/3 FMA; oracle memory 2·N^2·8 bytes (it copies A and b). The driver does not hand over a raw random matrix: it constructs a CONSISTENT system — A ~ U(-10,10)^{N×N}, x_true ~ U(-10,10)^N, then b := A·x_true, then x := 0 (cpu.cc:27-39). Nonsingularity and nonzero pivots hold with probability 1 because fillRand draws from a continuous distribution.
benchmarks.min_size: 1 (operational floor imposed by the ORACLE, not by the mathematics). N=0 is mathematically well defined (empty system, unique empty solution) but is OUT OF THE ORACLE'S DOMAIN: baseline.hpp:17 `for (size_t i = 0; i < N - 1; i++)` underflows to SIZE_MAX and indexes an empty vector. MEASURED: segfault, exit 139. N=1 is fully defined and correct (measured, 20000 trials).
benchmarks.max_size: Forced, by two independent caps. (a) HARNESS: `max_spec_size: 4096` (config.yaml:572, enforced in specs.py:293-294) rejects any spec with size > 4096. (b) BUDGET, which binds far earlier: the oracle at N=4096 measures a 77.34 s median (fastest single rep 59.58 s), 7.7x over the 10 s budget; N=3072 measures 38.25 s. The effective usable maximum for this benchmark is therefore ~2048, i.e. the harness cap of 4096 is unreachable here and must never be used as the domain maximum. A third, softer cap: the enhanced runner kills the whole driver process after `run_timeout_seconds: 60` (config.yaml:613), and validate() runs MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS=2 rounds of (oracle + candidate) at TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:78-92, utilities.hpp:25-26) — at N=2048 that is ~2×(4.1 s + candidate), leaving roughly 26 s per candidate solve.
benchmarks.special_conditions: (1) N >= 1 — oracle UB at N=0 (measured segfault), independently recorded in the repo as `baseline_incompatible` (baseline_selftest.jsonl). (2) NO structural size condition: any integer N >= 1 is a valid matrix order; no power of two, no minimum point count, no parity. (3) VALID MATRIX CONSTRUCTION (adopted domain decision for solve/LU): the oracle is Gaussian elimination WITHOUT pivoting, so its domain is matrices whose every leading principal submatrix is nonsingular — no exactly-zero pivot A_copy[i*N+i] for i<N-1 (baseline.hpp:19-24, else it returns early leaving x untouched) and A_copy[(N-1)*N+(N-1)] != 0 at back substitution (baseline.hpp:42, never checked → 1/0 = inf/nan). The driver's own generator satisfies this with probability 1 (fillRand is continuous, utilities.hpp:143-160). (4) SYSTEM CONSISTENCY is guaranteed by construction: b := A·x_true (cpu.cc:31-36), so a solution always exists. (5) Grading is an ABSOLUTE tolerance of 1e-4 (cpu.cc:96 → utilities.hpp:409-416, predicate `std::abs(x-y) > epsilon`) plus an explicit `isnan` guard on the candidate; entries of x_true live in [-10,10], so 1e-4 absolute ≈ 1e-5 relative. MEASURED that this is satisfiable over the whole chosen range: an algorithmically DIFFERENT correct solver (partial pivoting) deviates from the no-pivot oracle by at most 3.07e-7 at N=2048 and 2.4e-8 at N=64, 0 failures in ~92,000 trials across N ∈ {1,2,3,7,16,64,512,2048}. (6) NO ENHANCED_FILL INJECTION SITE: cpu.cc:28-29 calls `fillRand` directly, so the enhanced-tests pattern library cannot reach this benchmark at all — only the size axis varies the input (benchmark_shapes.json: `"fill_sites": 0`, `"explicit_values_supported": false`).
benchmarks.size_semantics: `size` = N = the SIDE LENGTH / matrix order of the square system, NOT an element count. The driver allocates A(N*N), b(N), x(N) from this one number (cpu.cc:53-55 for the timed context, cpu.cc:72-73 for validation) and `ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE` overrides exactly this N (cpu.cc:70, `ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(512)`; enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79). Consequence for the scale axis: work scales as N^3 and memory as N^2, so one doubling of the size number is 8x the runtime and 4x the footprint.
benchmarks.complexity: Oracle `correctSolveLinearSystem` (baseline.hpp:11-44): Gaussian elimination WITHOUT pivoting + back substitution. Time Θ(N^3) — exactly Σ_{i=0}^{N-2} (N-1-i)(N-i) ≈ N^3/3 multiply-subtract pairs in the elimination (baseline.hpp:27-33; the inner k-loop starts at k=i) plus ≈ N^2/2 in back substitution (baseline.hpp:37-43). Auxiliary space Θ(N^2): it copies A into A_copy and b into b_copy (baseline.hpp:13-14). Memory traffic Θ(N^3) bytes (≈ 16·N^3/3 = 4.6e10 B at N=2048), which is why the cost becomes bandwidth-bound once 8·N^2 exceeds the LLC.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
Derived from the operation, its complexity and the budget only — no candidate code was read or consulted.

OPERATION/COMPLEXITY: the oracle is unblocked Gaussian elimination without pivoting, ~N^3/3 multiply-subtract in the elimination plus ~N^2/2 in back substitution, over an O(N^2) working set that it copies (A_copy, b_copy — baseline.hpp:13-14). Because the working set is N^2 and the work is N^3, the operation traverses THREE distinct hardware regimes as N grows, and the scale axis is placed to hit one each. Host: i7-12700H, L1d 48 KiB, L2 1.25 MiB, L3 24 MiB.

SMALL = 64. A_copy = 32 KiB → L1-resident. Average inner-loop length is N/2 = 32, so loop/branch overhead and the O(N^2) back substitution (1/N of total work but no longer negligible) dominate; measured 1.6 GFLOP/s, the LOWEST of the three, i.e. the genuinely overhead-dominated regime. Still fully exercises the algorithm: 63 elimination steps, all trailing-submatrix updates, a full back substitution. For omp/mpi this is also the regime where parallel launch cost exceeds the work.

MEDIUM = 512. A_copy = 2 MiB, total footprint ~4 MiB → out of L2, comfortably inside L3. Measured 4.6 GFLOP/s, the PEAK of the three — the compute-bound, cache-resident regime. Independently it is the benchmark's own calibrated default validation size (cpu.cc:70, `ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(512)`), so medium coincides with the point the driver was written around; that coincidence is a check, not the derivation.

LARGE = 2048. A_copy = 32 MiB > L3 (24 MiB) → the trailing submatrix must be streamed from main memory on every elimination step; measured ~16 GB/s of traffic and 2.0 GFLOP/s, i.e. definitively memory-bandwidth-bound. It is also the LARGEST doubling step inside the 10 s serial-oracle budget: measured median 4.08 s (41 % of budget) versus 77.34 s at the next doubling 4096.

WHY A DOUBLING LADDER AND NOT THREE ARBITRARY NUMBERS: for an O(N^3) operation the meaningful scale unit is the side length, and each doubling is exactly 8x work / 4x footprint. 64 → 512 → 2048 gives 512x and 64x work steps and lands the footprint at 32 KiB / 2 MiB / 32 MiB — one point per cache level. Any non-ladder point (e.g. 1536, also measured at 1.78 s) would fit the budget too but would sit in the same regime as 2048 while sacrificing the clean 4x footprint spacing.

NOT DERIVED FROM: any observed model output, any generated spec file, or any strategy-switch threshold. The only repo artifacts consulted for sizing were the oracle's own complexity, the driver's allocation code, the config's caps, and my own timing measurements of the oracle.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no — not in the GENERATION prompt as the benchmark stands. The two hazards (N=0 crash, zero-pivot early return) are ORACLE-domain defects, not ambiguities the model could resolve: a correct candidate on N=0 simply does nothing, and on a zero-pivot matrix a pivoting candidate is right while the oracle is wrong. Restricting the generation prompt would neither prevent the crash nor change the verdict. The restriction belongs on the SPEC/SIZE domain instead (N >= 1), where it is already enforced by baseline_selftest marking size 0 `baseline_incompatible`. This answer FLIPS TO YES if the pending ENHANCED_FILL site is added to this driver (see pending_fix): structured matrices (all_zeros, all_same, extreme_values) then become injectable, the zero-pivot divergence becomes reachable, and the prompt would need this exact sentence: "A is nonsingular and every leading principal submatrix of A is nonsingular, so the system has a unique solution."
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: yes — three independent reasons. (1) The input is a CONSTRUCTED consistent system, not a filled buffer: A random, x_true random, b := A·x_true, x := 0 (cpu.cc:27-39). Any size-domain or edge-case harness must replicate `createRandomLinearSystem`, not just fill vectors, or it will feed an inconsistent b. (2) There is NO ENHANCED_FILL site in this driver (cpu.cc:28-29 calls `fillRand` directly), so the generic pattern machinery cannot touch this benchmark at all — the repo records this in benchmark_shapes.json ("fill_sites": 0, "no ENHANCED_FILL site; explicit_values disabled: nothing to fill"). Any input variation beyond N requires first adding a benchmark-specific injection point and then a benchmark-specific construction, because a pattern applied naively to A alone would silently break the b = A·x_true invariant. (3) Valid matrix construction is part of the domain (no zero pivots), which a generic filler cannot guarantee.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Own axis, independent of small/medium/large:
- **N = 0** — mathematically DEFINED (empty system; the unique solution is the empty vector). OUT OF THE ORACLE'S DOMAIN: `i < N - 1` underflows to SIZE_MAX (baseline.hpp:17) and dereferences an empty vector's data pointer. MEASURED: segfault, exit 139. The repo already records it: `{"size": 0, "status": "baseline_incompatible", "probe1": "crash", "benchmark": "dense_la/01_dense_la_solve"}` in baseline_selftest.jsonl, while sibling 00_dense_la_lu_decomp is "ok" at size 0. Note the config's static base set is [0,1,2,7] (config.yaml:562), i.e. size 0 IS requested for every parameterizable benchmark and is only neutralised at the gate — it must stay excluded here until the oracle is guarded.
- **N = 1** — DEFINED and correct: the elimination loop is empty, back substitution computes x[0] = b[0]/A[0]. MEASURED: 20,000 trials, x reproduces x_true exactly (max deviation from a pivoting reference 0.0). Degenerate sub-case: A[0] == 0 → 0/0 = nan, and no pivot check applies because the elimination loop never runs.
- **N = 2, 3, 7** — DEFINED, correct, repo-verified "ok" in baseline_selftest. MEASURED max deviation from an independent partial-pivoting solver over 20,000 trials each: 6.9e-12 / 4.8e-11 / 5.0e-10, all ~6 orders inside the 1e-4 tolerance. N = 3 is exactly the prompt's own worked example.
- **Exactly-zero pivot** (singular A, or a merely unlucky zero in a pivot position of a NONSINGULAR A) — the operation is defined for the nonsingular case and undefined/non-unique for the singular case, but the ORACLE does neither: baseline.hpp:22-24 `return`s from inside the elimination loop and leaves x exactly as the caller passed it. In validate() the caller passed all zeros (cpu.cc:82), so the reference becomes the zero vector. MEASURED at N=8 with A[0] forced to 0: oracle x = [0,0,0,0,…] while x_true = [-4.67, 0.795, -2.50, 5.20, …]. A correct pivoting candidate would be graded FAIL. Currently UNREACHABLE: fillRand is continuous (P(exact 0) = 0) and there is no ENHANCED_FILL site through which a structured matrix could be injected.
- **All values equal / all-zeros A** — singular, so it collapses into the zero-pivot case above (all-zeros additionally gives b = 0, for which every x is a solution). MEASURED at N=8 with A ≡ 0: oracle returns the untouched zero buffer. Also currently uninjectable here.
- **NOT degenerate, stated to prevent over-restriction**: N need not be a power of two, need not be even, and there is no minimum "enough elements for the operation to be defined" beyond N >= 1.

benchmarks.name: 02_dense_la_gemm
benchmarks.input_form: Two dense row-major matrices of `double` in flat `std::vector<double>`: A is M x K (row stride K), B is K x N (row stride N); output C is M x N (row stride N). Element (i,j) at buf[i*stride+j], 0-based, contiguous, unpadded. The PROMPT domain is general rectangular (M, K, N independent). The VALIDATED domain is square only: validate() calls the oracle and the candidate with M = K = N = TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:79, cpu.cc:82). The single relevant dimension for the enhanced-test size axis is therefore the side length n. Values: uniform in [-1.0, 1.0] at both fill sites (cpu.cc:70-71). Two fill sites (A and B), each n^2 elements — benchmark_shapes.json records elements_per_site ["n2","n2"], total_elements "n2 + n2", and explicit_values_supported=false for exactly that reason.
benchmarks.min_size: 0. GEMM imposes no lower bound: the empty product (M=K=N=0) is mathematically defined, and the driver realizes it without special-casing — all three vectors are empty, the oracle's loops do not execute, and reportAndCompare over two empty vectors returns true (total==0). Executed: N=0 runs clean, exit 0. There is no operation-derived size floor; 0 and 1 belong in degenerate_cases, not in a floor.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — a HARNESS cap, not an operation limit: thesis/config/config.yaml:572 sets max_spec_size 4096 and thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294 rejects any larger spec. The operation itself has no upper bound, and the comparator's absolute 1e-4 epsilon imposes none either in that range (measured reassociation deviation extrapolates to ~1e-12 at n=4096, 8 orders below the epsilon). The RUNTIME BUDGET binds far earlier: at 2*n^3 flops, 10 s is reached near n~1900 in the loaded host state (n=2048 measured 20.303 s there), so the effective ceiling for this benchmark is the chosen large=1536, well under the configured 4096.
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE on the size. No power-of-two requirement, no minimum element count, no structural/matrix-form precondition (contrast fft 05/07/08/09, or solve/LU). Any n >= 0 is a valid input, and any independent (M,K,N) is valid for the operation itself. The one genuine ORACLE precondition is on the OUTPUT buffer, not the size: correctGemm accumulates (`C[i*N+j] += ...`, baseline.hpp:15) and never zeroes C, so its semantics are C := C + A*B and it requires C to arrive zero-initialized. Every driver call site guarantees this (validate() std::fill 0 on `correct` and `test`, cpu.cc:72-73; reset() std::fill 0 on ctx->C, cpu.cc:29), so accumulate- and overwrite-style implementations are observationally identical under the driver protocol. A second, VALUE-axis (not size-axis) precondition was measured: the comparator epsilon is ABSOLUTE 1e-4 (cpu.cc:86 -> utilities.hpp:409-414, `std::abs(x-y) > epsilon`), while the output magnitude of this operation scales as R^2*sqrt(K) for a value range +/-R. Measured at n=500: a genuinely reassociated but correct implementation deviates by 7.1e-14 at R=1 (1.4e9x headroom), 7.1e-8 at R=1e3 (1.4e3x headroom), 7.0e-4 at R=1e5 (headroom 0.14 — ALREADY FAILING). Crossover ~ +/-3.8e4 at n=500, ~ +/-2e4 at n=1536. Enhanced specs must therefore not override value_range beyond about +/-1e4 for this benchmark; the call site's own [-1,1] is safe at every size up to the 4096 cap.
benchmarks.size_semantics: n is the SIDE LENGTH of a square matrix. validate() passes it as all three dimensions at once: M = K = N = n (cpu.cc:79/82). So one size number simultaneously sets the number of output elements (n^2), the number of input elements (2*n^2, split over two fill sites), and the accumulation length (K = n). Total memory touched by the oracle is 3*n^2 doubles, by validate() 4*n^2 doubles (32*n^2 bytes: 98 KiB at n=64, 8.0 MiB at n=500, 75.5 MiB at n=1536). Work is 2*n^3 flops. Note the asymmetry with the TIMED path, which is rectangular (M=P, K=P/4, N=P/2, cpu.cc:39-41) — the size axis of the enhanced stage only ever moves the square validation shape.
benchmarks.complexity: Time Theta(M*K*N) = Theta(n^3) for the square validation shape, exactly 2*n^3 flops (n^3 multiplies + n^3 adds), from the perfect ikj triple loop with no early exit (baseline.hpp:12-18). Space Theta(n^2): the oracle touches 3*n^2 doubles (A, B, C); validate() holds 4*n^2 (A, B, correct, test) = 32*n^2 bytes. Per-validate() cost is 2x the single-oracle cost, because MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS = 2 (cpu.cc:67 -> utilities.hpp:25-27) runs the trial loop twice, plus the candidate's own two runs.
benchmarks.domain_rationale: GEMM has no arithmetic preconditions, so the only structural axis available besides raw scale is the memory hierarchy — cubic work over quadratic data means the regime is set entirely by where the 3*n^2*8-byte working set lands. The container CPU (i7-12700H, measured in-image: L1d 48 KiB/core, L2 1.25 MiB/core, L3 24 MiB) fixes the three regimes, and the ladder is placed to BRACKET the already-validated default TEST_SIZE of 1024 rather than repeat it (1024 gives a 25.2 MiB working set, i.e. it sits exactly ON the L3 boundary and is already covered by the correctness stage). small = 64: 98 KiB working set — above L1d, comfortably inside L2. Fully cache-resident, pure arithmetic, no memory-hierarchy effect; K = 64 is already long enough for accumulation-order effects to exist (measured reassociation deviation 5.3e-15). 64 = 2^6 is the "clean" point: a multiple of every SIMD double width and every common block size, so no remainder handling is involved. medium = 500: 6.0 MiB — past L2, inside L3. 500 = 2^2*5^3 is deliberately NOT a power of two and NOT a multiple of 8/16/32/64, so an 8-wide (AVX-512) vector loop or any 16/32/64 block leaves a remainder in every dimension; its row stride of 4000 B is not even cache-line-aligned, so there is no systematic set aliasing. This is the point that covers the "arbitrary n" half of the specified domain — the operation places no power-of-two restriction, so a ladder made only of powers of two would leave most of the domain untouched. large = 1536: 56.6 MiB = 2.4x L3, firmly in the memory-traffic-dominated regime that the smaller two cannot reach; 1536 = 2^9*3 is again not a power of two, and its 12288 B row stride is 192 cache lines, congruent to 0 mod the 64 L1d sets, so rows alias into the same L1 sets — the classic stride pathology, deliberately placed at the top of the ladder. Together the three points cover aligned/cache-resident, unaligned-with-remainder/L3-resident, and aliased-stride/beyond-LLC. The static base sizes [0, 1, 2, 7] that the harness injects for every benchmark (config.yaml:562) already cover the tiny and tiny-prime end, which is why small is a genuine scale point at 64 rather than another near-zero value. No part of this reasoning uses observed candidate code: the regimes come from the operation's arithmetic intensity and the measured cache geometry, the non-power-of-two choice from the specified domain, and the ceiling from the runtime budget.

No derived counts, no structural construction, no validity retry loop. The only benchmark-specific handling already recorded elsewhere is that explicit_values is disabled because there are two fill sites (benchmark_shapes.json).

benchmarks.name: 03_dense_la_axpy
benchmarks.input_form: Scalar + two dense vectors -> one dense vector. alpha in R (double), x in R^N, y in R^N; output z in R^N, PRE-ALLOCATED to length N by the driver. Exactly ONE size dimension: N. Driver realisation: alpha is hard-wired to 2.0 (cpu.cc:36 perf path, cpu.cc:57 validate path) and is never varied; x and y are filled i.i.d. U[-1,1] by fillRand / ENHANCED_FILL (cpu.cc:26-27, 65-66; utilities.hpp:144-160). Two independent fill sites of n elements each (benchmark_shapes.json:28-37, elements_per_site ["n","n"], total_elements "n + n"). Grading: element-wise ABSOLUTE tolerance 1e-6 on z (cpu.cc:78 -> utilities.hpp:409-414), over MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS = 2 trials (utilities.hpp:25-27). Result magnitude is bounded by |alpha|*1 + 1 = 3, so 1e-6 absolute has ~10 orders of magnitude of headroom at every N.
benchmarks.min_size: 0. There is no size floor. correctAxpy is `for (size_t i = 0; i < x.size(); ++i)` (baseline.hpp:11) — well defined and a no-op at N=0; validate() builds four length-0 vectors and reportAndCompare over 0 elements returns true (utilities.hpp:356, 404). The spec validator accepts any non-negative int (specs.py:291) and the static base set already contains 0 (config.yaml:562). MEASURED: size 0 builds and runs, "Validation: PASS". The valid size form is "any integer N >= 0" — no power of two, no minimum point count, no matrix-validity condition.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — FORCED BY THE HARNESS, not by the operation. thesis/config/config.yaml:572 `max_spec_size: 4096`; enforced in thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294 ("size %s exceeds max_spec_size"). The operation itself has no upper bound. The MACHINE has one: measured, N = 2^27 (3.2 GB of arrays) is OOM-killed in the pareval-thesis container (exit 137; container total RAM 7 GB, ~4 GB available). Note the gap: the TIMED path runs at DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE = (1<<24) for serial/omp/mpi/mpi+omp (drivers/problem-sizes.json:29-33), i.e. 4096x above the enhanced-stage ceiling — the enhanced stage structurally cannot probe the DRAM-bound regime this kernel is benchmarked in.
benchmarks.special_conditions: Only one, and it is guaranteed by construction, never by the spec: |x| == |y| == |z|. The oracle reads y[i] and WRITES z[i] for all i < x.size() with no bounds check and no resize (baseline.hpp:11-13), so a shorter y or z is UB; the driver always builds all four vectors at TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:56), and the enhanced fill machinery fills both sites at the same n (benchmark_shapes.json elements_per_site ["n","n"]), so unequal lengths are unreachable through any spec. Secondary, on the CANDIDATE side: z must come back with length N — reportAndCompare fails a length mismatch outright (utilities.hpp:344-351, "SIZE_MISMATCH"), so a candidate that push_backs onto the pre-sized z fails. NOT required: powers of two, positivity, ordering, distinctness, minimum element count, any matrix form.
benchmarks.size_semantics: N = ELEMENT COUNT of each of x, y, z. Not a side length, not a derived nnz, not a matrix order. `const size_t TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)` (cpu.cc:54) then `std::vector<double> x(TEST_SIZE), y(TEST_SIZE), correct(TEST_SIZE), test(TEST_SIZE)` (cpu.cc:56). A spec size of n therefore costs n+n filled elements and a 4-vector validation footprint of 32*n bytes.
benchmarks.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) extra space. One fused multiply-add per element: 2 flops and 24 bytes of memory traffic (read x, read y, write z) per element — memory-bandwidth bound, not compute bound. MEASURED serial throughput with the pipeline flags: 5.2e8 elements/s at N = 2^24 (32.2 ms). Crucially there is NO accumulation: each output is one independent multiply-add, so numerical error does not grow with N and the absolute 1e-6 epsilon is equally safe at N=1 and at N=4093.
benchmarks.domain_rationale: min_size = 0 follows from the oracle's loop being defined at N=0 and from specs.py:291 accepting 0; there is nothing about axpy that needs a floor. No special condition beyond equal lengths follows, because axpy is a pure elementwise map: no reduction, no data dependence, no conditioning, no structural precondition. SCALE POINTS — derived from the operation, its complexity and the harness ceiling, never from any candidate. For an elementwise map with no reduction, exactly two things vary with N: (a) how many full SIMD/unroll BLOCKS the loop has versus its remainder — the only structural correctness hazard a map has; (b) how the work splits across the stage's fixed 4 threads / 4 ranks (config.yaml:603-604). Nothing numerical varies (see complexity). So the ladder samples one full block plus tail, the L1 boundary, and the harness ceiling, and every point is chosen ODD and non-power-of-two so that a nonzero remainder exists for every common blocking factor (2,4,8,16,32) and the 4-way split is always uneven. SMALL = 37: the smallest natural size past 32 (= 8 doubles of AVX-512 x 4-way unroll, the widest common block) — one full block for every blocking factor plus a 5-element tail; 37 is prime, so coprime to every unroll factor and every worker count (37 = 9*4+1). Footprint 37*32 B ~ 1.2 KB, L1-resident. MEDIUM = 1023: this benchmark's validation footprint is 32 B/element, so 1024 elements = 32 KiB = exactly one typical L1D — the L1 boundary is at N=1024, which is also the driver's own stock TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:54), i.e. the size the benchmark was authored for. 1023 = 3*11*31 sits on that boundary while breaking the power of two and the 4-way split (1023 mod 4 = 3). LARGE = 4093: the largest PRIME <= max_spec_size 4096 (config.yaml:572) — maximally uneven under every blocking factor and every worker count, ~128 KiB footprint (out of L1, into L2), and it exhausts the range the harness allows. 4093 is preferred over the literal ceiling 4096 precisely because 2^12 hides the one hazard this operation has. The three points are ~28x and ~4x apart; the ladder is compressed by the harness ceiling, not by the operation. Sizes 0/1/2/7 are deliberately NOT part of this ladder — they are the degenerate axis and are already the static base set (config.yaml:562).

Caveat: explicit_values (pattern 10) is DISABLED for this benchmark because it has 2 fill sites and the value-to-vector mapping would be ambiguous, so a hand-written surgical case (e.g. an exact-cancellation pair) cannot be expressed at all.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
MATHEMATICALLY DEFINED (and all EXECUTED against a correct candidate and against a deliberately wrong one that ignores alpha, to measure discriminating power; serial gate replica, g++ -O3 -DUSE_SERIAL -DDRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE=(1<<4) -DENHANCED_TEST_SIZE=n -DENHANCED_FILL_PATTERN=p -DMISMATCH_REPORT_MAX=3 over the real serial-driver.cc + cpu.cc):
- N = 0 (empty vectors): DEFINED, empty result. MEASURED: both candidates PASS -> VACUOUS. The compare loop never runs and utilities.hpp:404 returns true, so any non-crashing candidate passes. N=0 is in the static base set (config.yaml:562); it tests only "does not crash on an empty vector".
- N = 1: DEFINED. MEASURED: correct PASS, wrong FAIL (1/1 mismatch) -> fully discriminating. The smallest size that grades anything.
- N = 2 and N = 7 (rest of the static base set): DEFINED and discriminating (wrong candidate FAILs 2/2 and 7/7). N=2 additionally leaves 2 of the 4 ranks/threads idle, N=7 gives an uneven 4-way split.
- all_zeros (pattern 1) and all_same (pattern 2): DEFINED (z = 0). MEASURED at N=37: BOTH candidates PASS -> VACUOUS for any alpha error, since alpha*0 + 0 = 0 for every alpha. Note enhancedMidValue(-1,1) = 0.0 (enhanced-fill.hpp:148), so at the call-site range all_same is BIT-IDENTICAL to all_zeros for this benchmark — the two patterns are one case unless a spec overrides LO/HI.
- alternating (5) and ascending (3): DEFINED and discriminating (wrong candidate FAILs 37/37 and 36/37; the one matching index under `ascending` is the ramp's exact zero).
- extreme_values (6): mathematically defined in R, NOT representable in binary64. Both fill sites get lowest/max alternating, so z[i] = 2*(+-DBL_MAX) +- DBL_MAX = +-inf at EVERY index. MEASURED: "BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE: non_finite_reference", every index skipped, both candidates report PASS. Any such spec is discarded as baseline_incompatible before it grades anything (run_enhanced_tests.py:485-488; baseline_selftest.py:322).
- spike_at(k) (9): same overflow, one index only — both sites are spiked to DBL_MAX/2, so z[k] = 2*(DBL_MAX/2) + DBL_MAX/2 = +inf. MEASURED at N=37, k=3: marker emitted, index 3 skipped (wrong candidate FAILs 36 of 37, not 37). Also gated out as baseline_incompatible. The "arithmetic-surviving magnitude" comment at enhanced-fill.hpp:154 does NOT hold for this benchmark because alpha = 2 and both operands are spiked.
NOT REACHABLE as a degenerate case: alpha itself. alpha is hard-wired to 2.0 (cpu.cc:36, 57) and there is no ENHANCED_ hook for scalar parameters, so alpha = 0, 1, -1, NaN can never be tested at ANY size, and a candidate that hardcodes alpha = 2 passes the entire enhanced stage.
benchmarks.pending_fix: No pending semantics decision changes min_size, the special condition, or small/medium/large — those follow from the oracle and the harness bounds alone, and the row is NOT provisional on the size axis. Two grading-side caveats: (a) the degenerate-case verdicts above depend on UNCOMMITTED working-tree code — the A1b non-finite-reference contract in drivers/cpp/utilities.hpp:329 and the gate mapping in thesis/enhanced_tests/baseline_selftest.py:322 are both ' M' in git status; if that work were reverted, extreme_values and spike_at would silently PASS instead of being gated as baseline_incompatible, which would change what a spec at any size actually means. Both are orthogonal to the size ladder but cap what this row can buy.

Input built the way the driver's own generator builds it: srand(12345), x and y of length N filled by the repo's own fillRand(v, -1.0, 1.0) (utilities.hpp included, not reimplemented), alpha = 2.0, z pre-sized to N — mirroring cpu.cc:56-57,65-66. The result is consumed by a strided checksum so nothing can be dead-code-eliminated. Harness: <scratch>/domain/03_dense_la_axpy/harness.cpp.
FLAGS (pipeline-exact, no -DNDEBUG): g++ -std=c++17 -O3 -DUSE_SERIAL "-DDRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE=(1<<4)" -I /repo/drivers/cpp -I /repo/drivers/cpp/benchmarks/dense_la/03_dense_la_axpy harness.cpp -o h

BUDGET ADJUSTMENT: NONE. The first choice of LARGE was kept. The 10 s budget is a cap, and it is not the binding constraint here — max_spec_size = 4096 is. To document that the budget could never bind, the same harness was run up the full scale: N=2^20 -> 1.867e-03 s; N=2^24 (the timed DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE) -> 3.2245e-02 s; N=2^26 -> 8.353e-01 s median but wildly unstable (0.312 / 0.835 / 4.993 s — 1.5 GB of arrays against ~4 GB available, i.e. page-fault/swap noise); N=2^27 (3.2 GB) -> OOM-KILLED, exit 137. At the measured 5.2e8 elements/s, reaching 10 s would need ~5.2e9 elements = ~125 GB of arrays, which no host in this setup has. So for axpy the 10 s serial budget is physically unreachable, and I did NOT silently substitute another budget: LARGE is set by the harness cap (config.yaml:572), the cap is reported as max_size, and the resulting runtime is reported as measured.
NOT MEASURED: the omp and mpi enhanced runs (config.yaml:597 includes them, mpirun -np 4). benchmarks.name: 04_dense_la_gemv
benchmarks.input_form: Dense general matrix-vector product y = A·x over IEEE binary64. A: row-major dense matrix, M rows x N columns, held flat in std::vector<double> with M*N entries, addressed A[i*N+j] (baseline.hpp:15). x: dense vector of N doubles. y: OUTPUT vector, pre-sized to M doubles by the caller — the oracle writes y[i] without resizing, so y.size() >= M is a caller precondition (baseline.hpp:12-16). M and N are passed as separate size_t parameters. Relevant dimensions: M (rows / output length) and N (columns / input length); the two are mathematically independent. Values: uniform in [-10.0, 10.0] via fillRand (cpu.cc:69-70, utilities.hpp:144). CRITICAL: validate() collapses both dimensions onto ONE knob — A(TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE), x(TEST_SIZE), correct/test(TEST_SIZE), correctGemv(A,x,correct,TEST_SIZE,TEST_SIZE) — so every validated input is SQUARE, M = N = size (cpu.cc:59-61,75,78). The timed run, by contrast, is genuinely non-square: M = DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE/2 = 4096, N = DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE = 8192 (cpu.cc:37-38, drivers/problem-sizes.json "04_dense_la_gemv": (1<<13)).
benchmarks.min_size: 0. The operation imposes NO size floor: y = A·x is defined for every M >= 0, N >= 0 (N = 0 gives the empty sum, y = 0-vector of length M; M = 0 gives the empty y). The oracle's two loops simply do not execute and it returns cleanly — MEASURED at size 0 and size 1 (both < 1 microsecond, no fault). baseline.hpp carries no guard, no assertion and no minimum (baseline.hpp:11-17). The only preconditions are container-size contracts, not size floors: A.size() >= M*N, x.size() >= N, y.size() >= M. Consistent with this, the harness's own static base set already includes sizes 0 and 1 (config.yaml:562, static_base_sizes: [0, 1, 2, 7]).
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — FORCED BY THE HARNESS, not by the operation and not by the runtime budget. thesis/config/config.yaml:572 sets max_spec_size: 4096 and thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294 rejects any spec with size > max_size ("size %s exceeds max_spec_size %s"); specs.py:532-534 additionally clamps size mutations to that range. The operation itself has no upper bound. The physical ceiling on this host lies above the cap but below where the 10 s budget would bite: MEASURED, size 16384 (A = 2048 MB) took 216.2 s against a ~1.0 s Θ(size²) prediction — thrashing on an 8.15 GB Docker VM — and the same size under --memory=7g was OOM-Killed. 10 s of genuine arithmetic would need size ≈ 52,000–94,000, i.e. 21–70 GB for A, which is unreachable.
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE from the operation. GEMV requires no power of two, no positivity, no symmetry, no invertibility, no minimum point count, no structural property whatsoever — any real M x N matrix and any real N-vector are valid input. The only conditions are structural/contractual, and all three are guaranteed by the driver, not by the size choice: (1) A must hold exactly M*N entries in ROW-major order (baseline.hpp:15, A[i*N+j]); (2) x must hold N entries; (3) y must ALREADY hold M entries — the oracle overwrites (y[i] = 0 first, baseline.hpp:13) and never resizes. One harness-imposed condition that is NOT a property of the operation: validate() forces M == N == size (cpu.cc:59-61,75), so only the square diagonal of the (M,N) domain is ever exercised. Two additional non-conditions worth recording: the comparison tolerance is ABSOLUTE 1e-4 (cpu.cc:82 -> utilities.hpp:409, std::abs(x-y) > epsilon), which does not bind at any size the harness allows (worst-case reorder error at size 4095 with values in [-10,10] is ~1e-7, four orders under the tolerance; it would only approach 1e-4 near N ~ 2e6); and `correct`/`test` are allocated ONCE outside the MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS = 2 trial loop (cpu.cc:61 vs 67, utilities.hpp:26), so a candidate that accumulates into y instead of overwriting is caught on the second trial at ANY size, including size 1.
benchmarks.size_semantics: `size` (the spec field, compiled in as -DENHANCED_TEST_SIZE) is the SIDE LENGTH of a SQUARE matrix, not an element count and not a row count on its own: validate() sets M = N = size (cpu.cc:57-61,75). Derived counts at a given size: A holds size² doubles (8·size² bytes), x holds size, y holds size — benchmark_shapes.json records exactly this as elements_per_site ["n2","n"], total_elements "n2 + n", across 2 fill sites. Consequences worth stating: (a) the oracle's work grows QUADRATICALLY in the size number, so a size mutation of ×2 is a ×4 cost; (b) size is NOT the timed run's shape — the timed compute() uses M = 4096, N = 8192 from DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE = (1<<13), so the validation axis and the performance axis do not describe the same problem; (c) the default when no ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE is given is 1024 (cpu.cc:57), a 8 MB matrix; (d) explicit_values is disabled for this benchmark precisely because two fill sites would make the value-to-vector mapping ambiguous (benchmark_shapes.json notes field), so no size is expressible as a hand-written value list.
benchmarks.complexity: Oracle correctGemv: exactly M*N multiply-adds and M stores; time Θ(M·N) = Θ(size²) on the square validation axis, extra space Θ(1). Memory traffic is 8·M·N bytes for A streamed exactly once, against 2·M·N flops — 4 bytes moved per flop, i.e. the oracle is strictly MEMORY-BANDWIDTH-bound, not arithmetic-bound. This is the decisive fact for sizing: work and data grow at the same rate Θ(size²), so runtime is proportional to the matrix footprint and a 10 s runtime can only be bought with a ~70 GB matrix. MEASURED throughput confirms the linear-in-bytes behaviour while the matrix fits in RAM: 2.0 MB / 0.00053 s and 127.9 MB / 0.061 s are within ~15% of the same bytes-per-second.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
The scale axis for GEMV is set by three regimes of the SAME quantity — the row-major stream of A — plus the divisibility of the row count, because every parallel and every blocked implementation of y = A·x partitions rows (or the inner reduction) and the interesting failures are remainder chunks. Nothing about GEMV prefers round numbers: unlike the FFT family it has no power-of-two requirement, so the size choice is mathematically free and should be spent on the most discriminating values.

SMALL = 3. The smallest size at which the operation is STRUCTURALLY COMPLETE rather than degenerate: M >= 2 so that the per-row reset y[i] = 0 (baseline.hpp:13) is exercised across more than one row, N >= 2 so that the inner loop is a genuine accumulation rather than a single product, and — decisively — a NON-square-symmetric access pattern, since with random A the row-major read A[i*N+j] and the transposed read A[j*N+i] already give different answers at 3x3. 3 is also the smallest such value that is not a power of two, so any unroll or SIMD widening by 2, 4 or 8 leaves a scalar tail (3 mod 2 = 1, 3 mod 4 = 3, 3 mod 8 = 3). Finally, M = 3 is FEWER rows than any realistic OpenMP thread count or MPI rank count at the pilot's launch point, which exercises the "more workers than work items" path (idle ranks, empty chunks, negative/zero chunk sizes) that no larger size can reach. A is 9 doubles — fully hand-checkable. Matches the scale of the prompt's own documented example (a 2x3 gemv). MEASURED: below timer resolution (< 1 microsecond).

MEDIUM = 513 = 2^9 + 1. The regime where A (2.0 MB, MEASURED) no longer fits in a typical L2 (>= 1 MB) but still fits in L3, so blocking/tiling and cache-friendly reordering become live implementation strategies while the run stays sub-millisecond. The value is chosen one PAST a power of two so that 513 mod 2^k = 1 for every k = 1..9: a one-row/one-column remainder under every power-of-two row partition (2, 4, 8, 16, ... threads or ranks) and under every 2/4/8-wide vectorization of the inner reduction — the harshest possible tail, and the exact shape of bug that a divisible size masks. Row count 513 now comfortably EXCEEDS any thread/rank count, i.e. the opposite regime from SMALL. MEASURED oracle: 0.000533 s.

LARGE = 4095 = 2^12 - 1. The pure memory-streaming regime: A is 127.9 MB (MEASURED), an order of magnitude beyond any last-level cache, so the oracle and any candidate are bandwidth-bound and every chunked, strip-mined or MPI row-distributed decomposition must handle a final short chunk. 4095 is the LARGEST value under the harness's hard cap max_spec_size = 4096 (config.yaml:572, enforced at specs.py:293-294) that retains the remainder property — 4095 mod 2^k != 0 for all k >= 1 (4095 = 3^2·5·7·13, odd). Choosing 4095 over the cap value 4096 costs 0.05% of the data and buys the tail coverage; it additionally avoids the pathological power-of-two row stride (4096 doubles = exactly 32 KB), which is a cache-set-aliasing trap rather than a correctness signal — MEASURED side by side back-to-back on the same loaded host, 4096 ran 0.076 s vs 4095's 0.061 s, ~25% slower for identical arithmetic. Absolute tolerance 1e-4 is not endangered here: the worst-case summation-reorder error over 4095 terms of magnitude <= 100 is ~1e-7. Working set at LARGE is ~128 MB per validation process (A) — modest, but it multiplies if the enhanced runner uses parallel workers.

WHY THE 10 s BUDGET DOES NOT DECIDE THIS ROW. It is not the binding constraint and cannot be, for a mathematical reason specific to Θ(size²) work over Θ(size²) data. From the MEASURED LARGE point, reaching 10 s of arithmetic needs size ≈ 4095·sqrt(10/0.061) ≈ 52,000 (≈ 94,000 using the quiet-host 0.019 s measurement), i.e. 8·size² = 21–70 GB for A alone — physically impossible on this host (Docker VM total memory 8.15 GB, MEASURED via docker info). The memory wall is crossed far below that and far above the cap: MEASURED at size 16384 (A = 2048 MB) the oracle took 216.2 s, ~220x the ~1 s that its own Θ(size²) scaling predicts — that is page thrashing on a contended 8 GB VM, not arithmetic, and an earlier attempt under an explicit --memory=7g cap was OOM-Killed outright. So for GEMV the 10 s wall clock is reachable only through swapping, never through work. The genuine ceiling is the harness cap of 4096, and LARGE = 4095 sits directly beneath it.

NOT REUSED FROM A SIBLING ROW. 3 / 513 / 4095 follow from GEMV's own structure: 3 = minimum structurally complete square with an unroll tail and fewer rows than workers; 513 = first size past a power of two whose matrix leaves L2; 4095 = largest cap-legal size with a non-zero remainder under every power-of-two split. A benchmark with different complexity (e.g. the Θ(n) axpy at DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE 1<<24, or the Θ(n³) lu_decomp/gemm) lands on different numbers by the same reasoning.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no. GEMV has no mathematical precondition to communicate: y = A·x is defined for every M >= 0, N >= 0 and every real A, x. The prompt already pins the three things that are genuinely conventional and that the audit found to be the actual discriminators — the ROW-MAJOR layout of A, the shapes ("A is an MxN matrix stored in row-major, x has N elements, and y has M elements") and, via the worked 2x3 example, the y = A·x orientation rather than xᵀA. Nothing about small/medium/large needs to enter the prompt. The one real gap (M != N is specified but never validated) is a DRIVER defect, not a prompt defect — the prompt already states the general shape correctly; fixing it in the prompt would mean weakening a correct specification to match a narrow harness, which is the wrong direction.
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: yes — for the SPECIFIED domain: the prompt requires a general M x N matrix, but ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE is a single scalar that validate() feeds to BOTH dimensions (cpu.cc:59-61,75), so the entire M != N half of the domain is unreachable and a dimension-/stride-confused candidate passes; testing it needs a benchmark-specific rectangular construction (an (M,N) pair, not one size). For the SQUARE axis as it stands, no: the two standard ENHANCED_FILL sites (A with n² doubles, x with n) are sufficient and already declared in benchmark_shapes.json ("elements_per_site": ["n2","n"], "total_elements": "n2 + n").

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Mathematically DEFINED for y = A·x, and separately noted where the current driver cannot discriminate them:

DEFINED AND REACHABLE through the single size knob:
- size 0 (M = N = 0): A, x and y are all empty; y = A·x is the empty vector. Oracle handles it (MEASURED, < 1 us, no fault). BUT NON-DISCRIMINATING in the driver: correct and test are both empty, reportAndCompareWith loops zero times, total == 0 => PASS (utilities.hpp:337-408). Every candidate, including an empty function body, passes at size 0. Keep it as a crash/UB probe (out-of-bounds on empty vectors, division by M or N), not as a correctness probe.
- size 1 (1x1): y[0] = A[0]·x[0]. Fully defined and genuinely discriminating for basic indexing and for overwrite-vs-accumulate (the second trial reuses the same `test` vector, cpu.cc:61 vs :67), though it cannot separate row-major from column-major (both index element 0).
- size 2: smallest size where row-major and transposed access diverge; still a power of two, so no unroll tail.
- all-zeros A (or all-zeros x): y = 0-vector. Defined. Weak — the audit records all_zeros at tiny sizes as non-discriminating for this benchmark (thesis/docs/oracle-correctness-audit.md:541-546).
- all values equal (all_same): y[i] = N·a·b, the same constant in every row. Defined. Deliberately blind to any row-permutation or row/column-swap error, since all rows are identical — useful only as an accumulation-count check (it detects an off-by-one in the inner loop bound: the answer is exactly N·a·b).
- ascending / descending / alternating ramps over A: defined; ascending in particular makes each row's sum distinct, so it DOES separate row-major from column-major, unlike all_same.

DEFINED BUT UNREACHABLE with one size knob (they need an (M,N) pair):
- M = 0, N > 0: y is the empty vector. Defined.
- M > 0, N = 0: y is the M-vector of zeros (empty sum per row) — note this is the case that distinguishes an implementation which zeroes y from one which leaves it untouched.
- M != N generally (e.g. the prompt's own 2x3 example, and the timed 4096x8192 shape): defined and specified, never validated.

NOT degenerate — OUT OF DOMAIN for this benchmark (do not schedule as edge cases):
- extreme_values fill (±DBL_MAX alternating, enhanced-fill.hpp:129-141) and spike_at (DBL_MAX/2, enhanced-fill.hpp:152-162): products reach ~1e309 and overflow to ±inf, so the ORACLE ITSELF produces non-finite values; reportAndCompareWith then emits BASELINE_INCOMPATIBLE and SKIPS those indices (utilities.hpp:325-330, 355-365), turning the test vacuous. The audit records exactly this: "[F/documentation only] The enhanced-test spec 'extreme_values' (and all_zeros at tiny sizes) is non-discriminating for this benchmark" (thesis/docs/oracle-correctness-audit.md:541-546). These are a value-range failure, not a size degeneracy, and belong on neither the scale nor the degenerate axis.
benchmarks.pending_fix:
YES — this row is PROVISIONAL. Open, not-yet-implemented semantics decision, recorded in thesis/docs/oracle-correctness-audit.md (lines 121, 148, 503 and the per-benchmark section at 541-546) and classified there as "[F / should fix]": "validate() only ever tests a SQUARE matrix while the timed compute() runs a NON-SQUARE shape - a dimension-confused submission passes"; the prescribed remedy is stated as "Make validate() exercise the non-square shape the timed run uses." The same document quantifies the consequence at line 503: such a submission "gains a measured ~3x 'speedup' by touching half the data". The fix is NOT implemented — cpu.cc:59 still allocates A(TEST_SIZE * TEST_SIZE) and cpu.cc:75/78 still pass (TEST_SIZE, TEST_SIZE).

Impact on this row if the fix lands: `size` stops being one number. small/medium/large must be re-expressed as (M, N) PAIRS, benchmark_shapes.json's total_elements "n2 + n" becomes "M*N + N", the explicit_values element-count rule (specs.py:79-92, which knows only "n" and "n2") no longer computes the right count, and every existing size-based spec for this benchmark has to be re-derived. The scale REGIMES argued above (structurally complete + fewer rows than workers; past-L2 with a power-of-two-hostile remainder; beyond-LLC streaming under the 4096 cap) survive the change unaltered — only their encoding as a single integer does not.

Second, lower-severity open item from the same audit (classified "[B / no action]" and "[F / documentation only]", so it does not make the row provisional but is worth carrying): write-semantics divergence inside the dense_la family — correctGemm ACCUMULATES (C += A·B, never zeroes C) while correctGemv OVERWRITES (y[i] = 0 first, baseline.hpp:13), although all four dense_la prompts use the same "Store the results in ..." wording (oracle-correctness-audit.md:170-176). For 04 specifically the overwrite reading is the one the prompt implies and the one the oracle implements, so there is nothing to change here — but if the family is ever harmonised, 04 is in scope.

benchmarks.name: 05_fft_inverse_fft
benchmarks.input_form: One in-place vector `std::vector<std::complex<double>> x` of N elements. The driver builds it from two separate double vectors: `real` and `imag` are each filled independently with values in [-1.0, 1.0], then `x[j] = complex(real[j], imag[j])` (cpu.cc:63-64, 72-78; perf path identical at cpu.cc:30-39, 44-46). The ONLY dimension is N = x.size(); nothing is derived from it (no nnz, no side length, no second operand). Working set = 16*N bytes for x plus 8*N each for real/imag. benchmarks.min_size: No numeric floor — the constraint is a FORM constraint: N must be a power of two, N = 2^m. benchmarks.complexity: Theta(N log N) = Theta(2^m * m) for N = 2^m: m = log2(N) decimation-in-frequency stages of N/2 radix-2 butterflies each (baseline.hpp:19-33), plus an O(N) bit-reversal permutation (baseline.hpp:35-52) and three O(N) elementwise passes in correctIfft (conjugate, conjugate, scale by 1/N; baseline.hpp:62-72). benchmarks.domain_rationale:
The domain is fixed by the oracle's algorithm, not by any candidate. correctIfft = conj -> radix-2 DIF fft -> conj -> /N (baseline.hpp:61-73). The kernel halves its span (`k >>= 1`, baseline.hpp:20) and finishes with a bit-reversal driven by `m = log2(N)` (baseline.hpp:35, 45); both are only defined for N = 2^m. Hence the size axis is the exponent m, and m is ALSO the complexity parameter (work = Theta(2^m * m)) and the parallel depth. So the scale ladder is placed evenly in m.

Admissible range: m in [0, 12], because the harness rejects any spec size above max_spec_size = 4096 = 2^12 (config.yaml:572, specs.py:294). The bottom of that range is already occupied by the harness's own static base sizes {0, 1, 2} (config.yaml:562), which is the DEGENERATE axis, not the scale axis. Placing three points evenly in m strictly above the degenerate region and up to the cap gives m = 4, 8, 12 -> N = 16, 256, 4096.

Point-by-point:
- small = 16 (m=4): the smallest size at which every structural feature of the algorithm is simultaneously exercised — 4 stages, a non-trivial bit-reversal permutation, and a twiddle recurrence (T *= phiT) that runs over k = 8, 4, 2, 1 steps so accumulated twiddle rounding is real. It is strictly above the static base sizes {0,1,2}, so the scale axis adds information rather than duplicating the degenerate axis. It is deliberately NOT 8: N=8 is exactly the size of the worked input/output pair the prompt hands to the model, so anchoring the ladder there would test the one example the specification gives away. (That is a property of the specification, not of any observed candidate.)
- medium = 256 (m=8): the geometric midpoint in m. 32x more work than small; still fully L1-resident, so it isolates the algorithmic scaling from any memory effect.
- large = 4096 (m=12): the largest size the harness admits. 24x more work than medium.

Runtime budget: not binding here by five orders of magnitude (measured 198 us at N=4096 against a 10 s ceiling). I therefore ALSO derived and measured the budget-binding LARGE for the case that max_spec_size is ever raised: the first power of two whose 16*N-byte working set leaves a typical L3 is 2^22 = 4,194,304 (64 MiB), measured 3.012 s — inside budget; 2^23 measured 6.279 s (inside, but only 1.6x headroom); 2^24 measured 104.172 s (10x over — rejected). Nothing in this derivation refers to any model output.

Numerical headroom at LARGE: with the driver's actual input range [-1,1] the oracle agrees with a direct O(N^2) IDFT to 1.15e-09 at N=4096 (and that residual is dominated by the naive reference's own error, since my probe used magnitudes up to N). The driver's absolute epsilon is 1e-4 per component (cpu.cc:93), so there is ~5 orders of magnitude of numerical headroom at LARGE — no numerical reason to cap below 4096.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
MATHEMATICALLY DEFINED, keep (all measured by my own probe unless noted):
- N = 0 (empty vector): ifft of the empty sequence is the empty sequence. Oracle returns size 0, exit 0 (measured). CAVEAT: 0 is not a power of two, and validate()'s comparison loop runs zero iterations (cpu.cc:92), so any non-crashing candidate passes — this is a crash/robustness test, not a correctness test.
- N = 1 (= 2^0): ifft([z]) = [z]. Oracle exactly correct (measured max abs err 0.000e+00). Formal UB at baseline.hpp:45 (shift exponent 32); harmless in practice on x86 because the index is 0.
- N = 2 (= 2^1): smallest non-trivial transform, exact (measured 1.110e-16).
- all_zeros: ifft(0) = 0 exactly; catches candidates that produce NaN via 0/0 normalization.
- all_same (constant c): ifft = [c, 0, 0, ..., 0]. Exact, and a strong discriminator — it pins BOTH the 1/N normalization and the DC-bin placement.
- alternating (lo, hi, lo, hi, ...): output non-zero only in bins k = 0 and k = N/2. Defined and exact.
- ascending / descending ramps: generic, defined.
- duplicate_at(k), sorted_except_one(k): generic bounded inputs, defined (they carry no special meaning for a transform — a transform has no ordering or uniqueness structure).
NOT WELL-POSED for this operation, exclude:

benchmarks.name: 06_fft_dft
benchmarks.input_form: One real vector `x` of length N (`std::vector<double> const&`), output `std::vector<std::complex<double>>&` of length N. Single fill site, single dimension. The oracle is self-sizing: `int N = x.size()` (baseline.hpp:17) and `output.resize(N, 0)` (baseline.hpp:18), so N is fully determined by the input vector. Driver fill: uniform real values in [-1.0, 1.0] via `ENHANCED_FILL(x, -1.0, 1.0)` (cpu.cc:61), which defaults to `fillRand` (enhanced-fill.hpp:461, utilities.hpp:143-159). Relevant dimensions: N only (no matrix side length, no nnz, no point count).
benchmarks.min_size: 0 — no floor. The operation imposes no minimum: N=0 is vacuously defined (empty spectrum of the empty sequence), N=1 is the true minimal non-empty case (X[0] = x[0]). Both are placed on the degenerate axis, not used as a size floor. Verified by execution (check.cpp, this session): N=0 -> output.size()==0, no crash; N=1 -> DC error 0.0.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — forced by the HARNESS, not by the operation and not by the runtime budget: `max_spec_size: 4096` (thesis/config/config.yaml:572), enforced in `validate_spec` (thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294, "size %s exceeds max_spec_size %s"). Neither the operation (defined for all N) nor the 10 s budget binds here — the budget alone would allow N ~ 1.1e4-1.7e4 (measured extrapolation, see measurement_detail).
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE from the operation. Explicitly NO power-of-two requirement: the oracle is a direct O(N^2) double loop (baseline.hpp:20-28) with no radix-2 structure, no log2, no bit reversal, no divisibility use — it is mathematically correct for every N (adopted decision for 06; independently corroborated by thesis/docs/fft-family-consistency.md:12,546 and re-verified here at N = 3, 17, 255, 1023, 4093 via two oracle-independent invariants: X[0] == sum(x) exact to 0.0e+00, and conjugate symmetry X[N-k] == conj(X[k]) for real input to <= 1.25e-10). No divisibility-by-rank/thread requirement either. The ONE genuine precondition is a VALUE-domain one, not a size one: the inputs must be finite and N*max|x| must stay representable in double, since |X[k]| <= N*max|x|. The `extreme_values` pattern (+/-DBL_MAX, enhanced-fill.hpp:129-141) violates this — the pilot's gate already excluded the (7, extreme_values) spec for 06 as `numerically_unstable` (thesis/docs/fft-family-consistency.md:582,546). Not a power-of-two condition, not a minimum-count condition.
benchmarks.size_semantics: size == N == element count of the real input vector x == length of the complex output. Not a side length, not a nnz-generating parameter. `ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE` sets N directly: `const size_t TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)` (cpu.cc:50) sizes `x`, `correct` and `test` (cpu.cc:52-53). Confirmed by the derived shape record: `fft/06_fft_dft` -> `{"fill_sites": 1, "elements_per_site": ["n"], "total_elements": "n", "explicit_values_supported": true}` (thesis/enhanced_tests/benchmark_shapes.json), i.e. an explicit_values spec of size N ships exactly N numbers.
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(N^2) time, Theta(N) space. Exactly N^2 inner iterations (baseline.hpp:20-28), each performing one `cos` and one `sin` evaluation (baseline.hpp:23-24) plus one complex multiply-accumulate — i.e. 2*N^2 transcendental calls, which dominate the cost. `angle = 2*M_PI*n*k/N` is evaluated entirely in double (the leading `2 * M_PI` promotes the whole product), so there is no integer overflow of n*k at any N; the angle magnitude reaches ~2*pi*N and the argument-reduction cost grows mildly with N, which is why the measured cost is slightly super-quadratic (0.198 s @ N=2048 vs 1.30 s @ N=4093 in the same batch, ratio 6.6 against the pure-quadratic 4.0).
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
Operation: unnormalized forward DFT with negative exponent, X[k] = sum_n x[n]*exp(-2*pi*i*n*k/N), evaluated directly. It is total on N >= 0 and places NO structural constraint on N (baseline.hpp:20-28). Therefore the only structure the scale points must respect is (a) the quadratic cost law, (b) the harness cap 4096, (c) the 10 s serial-oracle budget.

Ladder construction (geometric in WORK, which is the right axis for a quadratic oracle): N steps by a factor ~15-16, so work steps by ~225-260x. Inner-iteration counts are 289 -> 65,025 -> 16,752,649, spanning ~4.8 decades of work from small to large — enough to expose an O(N^2)-vs-O(N log N) cost difference and to make the medium point a genuine intermediate rather than a rounding of the ends.

Why each point is NOT a power of two (this is derived from the operation, never from any candidate — no generated code was read for this row): 06 is the only member of the fft family whose oracle is valid for arbitrary N, and the single assumption the specification does *not* license is a radix-2 length. The base correctness stage already covers the "nice" case exhaustively — `validate()` defaults to TEST_SIZE 1024 (cpu.cc:50) and the perf driver runs DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE (1<<11) = 2048 (drivers/problem-sizes.json), both powers of two and both divisible by the pilot's launch widths (omp_threads 4 / mpi_ranks 4, config.yaml:603-604). The enhanced domain is therefore chosen to be complementary and to hold exactly the property the base stage cannot test.
- 17 = 2^4 + 1: prime, so no radix decomposition of any base exists; sits one ABOVE a power of two, so a pad-to-power-of-two implementation must pad by 15 and cannot hide it.
- 255 = 3*5*17 = 2^8 - 1: odd composite — mixed-radix is possible, radix-2 is not; separates "general mixed-radix" from "radix-2 only". Sits one BELOW a power of two, so a round-up-to-power-of-two implementation returns a wrong length or wrong values.
- 4093: the largest prime <= the harness cap 4096 (verified: 4094 = 2*23*89, 4095 = 3^2*5*7*13, 4096 = 2^12). Prime again at the top of the range, three below a power of two, and it exercises the cap.
All three are also indivisible by the launch widths (17,4093 = 1 mod 4; 255 = 3 mod 4), so the omp/mpi remainder path is exercised at every scale point — a consequence of the choice, stated deliberately rather than as an accident; the operation licenses no divisibility assumption either.

Numerical headroom at LARGE (checked, because an absolute 1e-4 epsilon must stay meaningful): the oracle's own accumulated error at N=4093 is <= 1.25e-10 (conjugate-symmetry residual, measured), ~6 orders of magnitude inside the driver's 1e-4 absolute tolerance (cpu.cc:74), so LARGE does not turn the test into a rounding contest.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
SIZE-degenerate, all mathematically DEFINED for this operation and all executed clean this session (check.cpp):
- N = 0: empty input -> empty output; the DFT of the empty sequence is the empty sequence. Oracle: both loops skipped, `output.resize(0)`. Defined, but GRADING-VACUOUS: cpu.cc:73 iterates `j < x.size()`, so at N=0 nothing is compared and every candidate passes unconditionally (the driver also never checks `test.size()`). Keep as a crash/robustness case, not as a correctness case.
- N = 1: X[0] = x[0] (angle = 0). Defined; catches implementations that divide by N-1 or assume N >= 2. Measured DC error 0.0.
- N = 2: X = [x0+x1, x0-x1], a purely real spectrum. Defined; the sign convention is INVISIBLE here (real output), so it cannot discriminate the open convention question.
- N = 3: smallest N with a genuinely complex spectrum and no radix-2 factorization — the exact size at which the rest of the fft family is silently wrong and 06 is correct. Measured conj-symmetry residual 1.35e-15.
VALUE-degenerate (independent of size):
- all_zeros -> X == 0 for every k; exact, trivially satisfied by any additive implementation (low discriminating power).
- all_same (constant c) -> X[0] = N*c, X[k] = 0 otherwise up to ~1e-13 rounding; a useful probe of the absolute 1e-4 tolerance, safe at all three scale points.
- extreme_values (+/-DBL_MAX) -> NOT defined in double: |X[k]| <= N*max|x| overflows, output becomes inf/NaN. Already excluded by the existing gate (numerically_unstable at N=7 in the pilot). Additionally hazardous for 06 specifically because its validate() uses a hand-rolled `abs(a-b) > 1e-4` (cpu.cc:74) which is NaN-blind — a NaN compares EQUAL.
- alternating (lo,hi,lo,hi) at ODD N (17, 255, 4093 are all odd) is not the pure Nyquist impulse it would be at even N — worth knowing when reading spec results, not a defect.

benchmarks.name: 07_fft_fft_conjugate
benchmarks.input_form: One in-place `std::vector<std::complex<double>> &x`. The only dimension is N = x.size(). The driver never builds complex values directly: it allocates two `std::vector<double>` (`real`, `imag`) of length TEST_SIZE, fills each with values uniform in [-1.0, 1.0], and zips them into x (cpu.cc:58-74). Output is written back into x (in place); the operation is "forward DFT, then complex-conjugate every bin". In the enhanced stage N is set by `-DENHANCED_TEST_SIZE=<n>` (enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79), which replaces the stock 1024 in `validate()`.
benchmarks.min_size: 0 — no size floor. N=0 (empty sequence) and N=1 (single sample) are both mathematically defined for "DFT then conjugate" and both baselines return without crashing (measured). They belong in degenerate_cases. The binding restriction on this benchmark is not a floor but a FORM: N must be a power of two. Within that form the smallest valid sizes are 1 and 2.
benchmarks.max_size: No harness-imposed maximum. Two operation-imposed ceilings: (a) `correctFft`'s bit-reversal packs the index into a 32-bit word and shifts by (32 - m) (baseline.hpp:38-42), so N <= 2^32 is structural; (b) on this host the practical ceiling is 2^24 — MEASURED 6.269 s median for the grading oracle with a MEASURED peak RSS of 1,048,392 KB (~1.0 GB), against ~3 GB available in the container VM.
benchmarks.special_conditions:
**N must be a power of two.** This is the adopted decision and it is forced by both baselines, not merely convention:
- `correctFft` (baseline.hpp:12-55) is an iterative radix-2 Rosetta kernel. The butterfly loop `for (a = l; a < N; a += n) { b = a + k; ... x[b] = ... }` (baseline.hpp:22-30) writes x[a+k] with no bound on a+k; at odd N the final level (k=1, n=2) reaches a = N-1 and writes x[N] — a heap out-of-bounds write. MEASURED: N=5 aborts rc=134 `free(): invalid size`, N=7 aborts rc=134 `double free or corruption (out)`. The bit-reversal decimation (baseline.hpp:33-42) with m = (unsigned)log2(N) is a permutation only when N = 2^m.
- `fftCooleyTookey` (baseline.hpp:57-85, the GRADING oracle) is memory-safe but splits into two N/2 halves (baseline.hpp:62-68), silently dropping x[N-1] at odd N.
MEASURED max deviation vs an independent O(N^2) conj(DFT^-) reference on an asymmetric complex input: N=3 -> 5.21 for BOTH functions (identical wrong output, so a differential test between them is blind there); N=6 -> 17.9 / 17.2. No non-power-of-two N is usable.
Second condition, currently unsatisfiable: within the powers of two, the grading oracle itself is only correct at N in {0, 2} (see pending_fix). This does not change the size ladder but does mean every scale point is provisional.
benchmarks.size_semantics: Element count: the size number IS N = the length of the complex vector (and of both double vectors that feed it). It is not a side length and nothing is derived from it. Memory per vector = 16*N bytes; `validate()` holds three of them (x, correct, test) plus the two double vectors.
benchmarks.complexity: Both baselines are Theta(N log N) in arithmetic. `correctFft` is the iterative in-place variant: log2(N) butterfly levels of N/2 butterflies plus an O(N) bit-reversal pass plus an O(N) conjugation pass; O(1) extra memory. `fftCooleyTookey` is the recursive variant: same Theta(N log N) arithmetic but it allocates two fresh `vector<complex<double>>` of size N/2 at every one of the 2N-1 recursion nodes (baseline.hpp:62-63), i.e. Theta(N log N) total allocated bytes and ~32*N bytes live at the deepest point. That allocation traffic is why the grading oracle is consistently ~2x slower than the perf reference in the measurements below. Sizing therefore follows the N log N curve: each 64x in N costs ~64*(1 + 6/log2(N)) in time.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
Derived only from the operation, its domain and the runtime budget — no candidate code was consulted.

**Form.** Radix-2 FFT: valid N are exactly the powers of two (see special_conditions, measured). The scale axis is therefore log2(N) = the number of butterfly stages, and the ladder must move in whole stages.

**Ladder = the three cache regimes of an FFT.** An FFT is a Theta(N log N) operation with Theta(1) arithmetic intensity per element per stage; what actually changes as N grows is not the arithmetic but where the 16*N-byte working set lives and how far the strided butterfly accesses and the bit-reversal permutation reach. The three regimes are the operation's own scale structure:
- SMALL = 2^10 = 1024 -> 16 KB working set, L1-resident, 10 butterfly stages. Fully compute/latency-bound, no memory traffic. This is also the driver's own stock validation size (cpu.cc:56, `ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)`), i.e. the benchmark's own definition of a representative valid FFT input — the small point is anchored in the benchmark, not chosen for convenience. Measured grading oracle: 0.131 ms.
- MEDIUM = 2^16 = 65536 -> 1 MB working set, past L1 (32-48 KB) and past typical L2 (0.5-1 MB), resident in L3; 16 stages. This is the regime where the butterfly stride pattern and the bit-reversal permutation start to dominate over the arithmetic. Measured grading oracle: 15.6 ms.
- LARGE = 2^22 = 4194304 -> 64 MB working set, beyond any L3, DRAM-bandwidth-bound; 22 stages. Measured grading oracle: 2.854 s.
The ladder is geometric in the structural parameter: 10 / 16 / 22 stages, equal steps of 6, i.e. 64x in N per step. That is the natural spacing for an N log N operation — equal ratios in N, near-equal ratios in cost (measured: 0.131 ms -> 15.6 ms -> 2.854 s, ratios 119x and 183x, the excess over 64x being exactly the log factor).

**LARGE from the budget.** The ceiling is 10 s for the serial reference. `validate()` calls the oracle MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS = 2 times (utilities.hpp:25-27, cpu.cc:64-65), so the call the enhanced stage actually makes costs 2x a single oracle run. At 2^22 that is 2 x 2.854 = 5.71 s measured — inside the ceiling with real margin on a shared host. See budget_adjustment for the two steps down from the first choice.

**Not derived from:** no model/candidate output was read, and no size was picked because an implementation might switch strategy there.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Which degenerate inputs are mathematically DEFINED for "DFT then conjugate" (all measured at a power-of-two N=16 unless the case is itself a size):

DEFINED and safe:
- **N = 0** (empty sequence): the DFT of the empty sequence is the empty sequence. Both baselines return an empty vector, no crash, no NaN (measured). A perfectly usable spec size.
- **N = 1** (single sample): DFT(x) = x, so the answer is conj(x[0]). Well defined. MEASURED: `correctFft` gets it right (dev 0 vs the O(N^2) reference); the GRADING oracle `fftCooleyTookey` returns x UNCONJUGATED (early return at baseline.hpp:59 skips the conjugation) — measured dev 1.8 on a complex input. So N=1 is a valid degenerate size that is currently ungradeable.
- **N = 2**: both baselines exact (measured dev 2.2e-16 vs reference).
- **all-zero input**: DFT(0) = 0, conj(0) = 0. Defined and both baselines agree — but with ZERO discriminative power (measured maxdev 0 between the correct function and the broken oracle). An all-zeros spec passes vacuously; it proves nothing.
- **constant / all-same input**: DFT = (N*c, 0, ..., 0). Defined and discriminative (measured maxdev 16 between the two baselines at N=16 — the oracle defect is visible here).
- **alternating +-1 real input**: defined; measured maxdev 0 between the two baselines — another accidental blind spot (the even/odd halves are constant, so the sub-transforms are real and the spurious inner conjugations are harmless).
- **purely real input**: defined, spectrum is conjugate-symmetric; discriminative (measured maxdev 19.1 at N=16 for a real ramp).

DEFINED mathematically but OUTSIDE the double-precision domain — must be excluded:
- **extreme_values (fill pattern 6, +-DBL_MAX)**: the very first butterfly x[a] + x[b] overflows to +-Inf and Inf - Inf produces NaN. MEASURED at N=16: BOTH baselines return non-finite output. Any spec using this pattern on this benchmark grades NaN against NaN.
- **spike_at (fill pattern 9, DBL_MAX/2)**: stays finite but the transform is pure catastrophic cancellation; MEASURED maxdev between the two baselines 1.27e+308 at N=16, i.e. the 1e-3 absolute tolerance at cpu.cc:88 is meaningless there.
