benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
DEFINED and legitimate (all executed against the real oracle, results measured):
- n = 0, empty vector: bins = [0 0 0 0]. A count over the empty multiset is 0 in every bin; unambiguous. Oracle measured [0 0 0 0]. In the static base set.
- n = 1: exactly one bin = 1, the other three 0. Measured x=[7.8] -> [0 0 0 1].
- n = 2 and n = 7 (rest of the static base set): defined; n < 4 cannot populate all bins, which is a correct consequence, not an error.
- all values integral (all_zeros pattern; also all_same at the [0,100] midpoint 50.0; also alternating with lo=0/hi=100): frac = 0 exactly -> bins = [n 0 0 0]. Measured [5 0 0 0], [5 0 0 0], [4 0 0 0]. Well-defined and a good single-bin stress.
- EXACT BIN BOUNDARIES frac in {0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75}: fully defined by the prompt's lower-closed half-open intervals, and 0.25/0.5/0.75 are exactly representable in binary64, so this is a decidable, high-value case. Measured x = [3.0, 3.25, 3.5, 3.75] -> [1 1 1 1], i.e. oracle and prompt agree.
- both documented prompt examples reproduce exactly: [7.8,4.2,9.1,7.6,0.27,1.5,3.8] -> [2 1 2 2] and [1.9,0.2,0.6,10.1,7.4] -> [2 1 1 1].
NOT DEFINED — degenerate inputs that must be excluded or resolved first (measured):
- any negative element: the four stated intervals contain no negative number, so under truncating frac such an element belongs to NO bin, yet the oracle's first test `frac < 0.25` catches all of them. x = [-1.3,-0.3,-2.5,-3.75] -> [4 0 0 0] (BL-08, class D, decision open).
- any |v| >= 2^31: `(int) val` is UB. 2147483648.0 -> [0 0 0 1] and 2^52 -> [0 0 0 1] although frac = 0 mathematically (should be bins[0]); DBL_MAX -> bins[3], DBL_LOWEST -> bins[0], DBL_MAX/2 -> bins[3]. The safe boundary was pinned exactly: 2147483647.0 -> [1 0 0 0] and 2147483647.5 -> [0 0 1 0] are both correct. This makes the shipped extreme_values (6) and spike_at (9) patterns out-of-domain for this benchmark.
- NaN / +-Inf elements: not producible by the current fill sites, and not defined for this operation (no bin contains NaN); not probed further.

benchmarks.name: 25_reduce_xor
benchmarks.input_form: One 1-D operand: `std::vector<bool> const& x` of length N (libstdc++ bit-packed specialisation, 64 elements per `_Bit_type` word). Value domain per element is {false,true}, enforced by the container type, not by any generator range. Output: a single `bool` = XOR/parity of all N elements (equivalently: (number of `true` entries) mod 2). Only ONE dimension exists: N. No second operand, no matrix shape, no derived nnz. Driver: `std::vector<bool> x (TEST_SIZE)` (cpu.cc:68), filled with `x[i] = rand() % 2` (cpu.cc:78).
benchmarks.min_size: 0. The XOR reduction over an empty vector is the identity element of XOR, i.e. `false`, and the oracle returns exactly that: `std::reduce(x.begin(), x.end(), false, a!=b)` returns the init value `false` for an empty range (baseline.hpp:11-15). There is no mathematical size floor and no structural precondition of any kind.
benchmarks.max_size: 2147483647 (INT_MAX) — FORCED BY THE HARNESS, not by the operation. (a) validate()'s fill loop is `for (int i = 0; i < TEST_SIZE; i += 1)` (cpu.cc:77); at TEST_SIZE >= 2^31 the signed counter overflows (UB). (b) The MPI path repeats the same `int i` pattern in bcastBools (cpu.cc:29, cpu.cc:33) and passes `vec.size()` into MPI_Bcast's `int` count parameter (utilities.hpp:115). The operation itself is defined for every N. A tighter PRACTICAL ceiling of ~2^28 follows from the driver's MPI path: bcastBools materialises a transient `std::vector<char> xChar(x.size())` — one BYTE per element, 8x the packed footprint — per rank (cpu.cc:28); at the enhanced stage's mpi_ranks: 4 (config.yaml:604) that is 4*N bytes of transient RAM, i.e. exactly 1 GiB at N = 2^28.
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE at the level of the operation. Any N >= 0 is a valid input: no power-of-two requirement, no minimum element count, no sortedness, no non-degeneracy, no matrix well-formedness. The only conditions in the row are harness-derived, not operation-derived: (1) N <= INT_MAX (cpu.cc:77, cpu.cc:29/33, utilities.hpp:115); (2) N should not be a multiple of 64, so that a word-wise implementation over the bit-packed `std::vector<bool>` must handle a partial final word — all three adopted sizes satisfy this (mod 64 = 61 / 37 / 57); (3) the reference answer at the size must not equal the reduction's identity (`false`) in every validation trial — see domain_rationale, this is the criterion that actually decided the exact values.
benchmarks.size_semantics: TEST_SIZE == N == the number of bool ELEMENTS of x. Not bytes, not a side length, nothing derived. `const size_t TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024);` (cpu.cc:66) is the vector length at cpu.cc:68, and ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE overrides it directly (enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79). Physical footprint = ceil(N/8) bytes because of the bit packing (confirmed by measurement: maxrss 36 MB at N=2^28-7, i.e. 32 MiB payload); word granularity is 64 elements.
benchmarks.small: 1021  (= 2^10 - 3; 128 B packed; mod 64 = 61; reference trials = (true, true); measured oracle 2 us)
benchmarks.medium: 1048549  (= 2^20 - 27; 128 KiB packed; mod 64 = 37; reference trials = (true, true); measured oracle 1.73 ms)
benchmarks.large: 268435449  (= 2^28 - 7; 32 MiB packed; mod 64 = 57; reference trials = (true, true); measured oracle median 0.670 s over 5 reps)
benchmarks.complexity: O(N) time, O(1) extra space. Exactly one bit-read and one XOR per element, zero arithmetic, single pass, no branching on data. The oracle is `std::reduce(first, last, false, op)` over `std::vector<bool>::const_iterator` with a user binary op — libstdc++ has no fast path for that, so it is a plain sequential per-bit loop (baseline.hpp:12-14). Measured throughput on this host: ~2.0 ns/element at N=1e3, ~1.65 ns/element at N=1e6, ~2.5 ns/element at N=2.7e8 — linear, degrading only through the memory hierarchy. Above the LLC the operation is purely memory-bandwidth bound; there is no algorithmic phase change anywhere in N.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
The operation has no preconditions, no conditioning and no algorithmic phase change, so the scale axis can only vary three things, and each fixes one of the three points.

(1) MAGNITUDE — memory hierarchy and decomposition width. Packed footprint is N/8 bytes; the measurement host (12th Gen i7-12700H, in-container lscpu) has L1d 48 KiB/core, L2 1.25 MiB/core, L3 24 MiB shared.
  - small ~10^3: 128 B packed, deeply L1-resident. Fewer elements than one cache line per worker at the enhanced stage's omp_threads: 4 / mpi_ranks: 4 (config.yaml:603-604), so the "more workers than work" chunking corner is the thing under test.
  - medium ~10^6: 128 KiB packed = 2.7x this host's L1d, resident in L2. >=10^6 elements means every decomposition is genuinely multi-chunk for any plausible thread/rank count, independent of host cache sizes.
  - large ~2^28: 32 MiB packed = 1.3x this host's 24 MiB L3, i.e. past the LLC and memory-bandwidth bound. The magnitude is capped from above by the driver, not by the 10 s budget: bcastBools allocates an N-byte `std::vector<char>` shadow copy per rank (cpu.cc:28), so at mpi_ranks 4 the transient cost is 4N bytes = exactly 1 GiB at 2^28 and 2 GiB at 2^29. 2^28 is the largest scale at which the three-execution-model enhanced sweep (config.yaml:596 [serial, omp, mpi]) stays affordable. INT_MAX (cpu.cc:77) is the hard ceiling above that.
  The ladder is 10^3 / 10^6 / 2.7*10^8 — three-plus decades for a strictly O(N) single-pass operation.

(2) TAIL WORD. The prompt's signature mandates `std::vector<bool>`, which libstdc++ packs 64 elements per word. A size that is a multiple of 64 lets a word-wise implementation skip remainder handling entirely. All three sizes are non-multiples of 64 (mod 64 = 61 / 37 / 57), so a partial final word exists at every scale. This follows from the container the operation is specified over, not from any observed implementation.

(3) NON-IDENTITY REFERENCE — the criterion that fixed the exact values. The codomain of this operation is a single bit whose identity element is `false`. A test whose reference answer is `false` in every validation trial cannot distinguish a correct implementation from `return false;` — it has zero discriminating power against the trivial implementation and against any bug class that collapses to the identity. This is derivable a priori from the operation; it is not candidate-adaptive. Because the driver fills from the deterministic UNSEEDED rand() stream (cpu.cc:78) after an init()/reset() offset of DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE draws (serial-driver.cc:45 then :48; cpu.cc:40-42; enhanced stage builds with -DDRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE=(1<<4), run_enhanced_tests.py:322), the reference answer is a DETERMINISTIC function of the size. I computed it directly from the driver's own stream for both trials (MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS = 2, utilities.hpp:25-26). Results: the plain magnitudes 2^28-1 (0,0), 2^28 (0,0), 2^28-19 (0,0), 2^20-7 (0,0) etc. are BLIND; the adopted 1021 / 1048549 / 268435449 all give (true, true), i.e. both trials discriminate, which also survives a future reduction of MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS to 1. This independently reproduces the blind spot the repo's own pilot analysis documents (pilot-001-corrected-numbers.md:94: sizes {0,1,2,7} pass a constant-false implementation, {3,4,6,8,...,1023,1024,2046} do not) — my probe returns (0,0) for N=0,1,2 and (1,0)/(0,1) for 1023/1024 at offset 16, matching it exactly. Note this makes the exact values (not the magnitudes) harness-dependent: see pending_fix.

Deliberately NOT reused from a sibling reduce benchmark: 26-29 are float reductions with fillRand value ranges and epsilon comparison; 25 is a 1-bit exact-equality parity over a bit-packed container with an inline rand()%2 generator and no fill site. Its sizes follow from packing granularity, the MPI byte-shadow copy and the identity-reference criterion, none of which exist for 26-29.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no. The operation is total on every N >= 0 (including 0 and 1), there is no power-of-two condition, no minimum element count and no structural precondition, so no size sentence needs to enter the prompt. The empty-input convention needs no sentence either: the identity of XOR is unambiguously `false` and the oracle agrees (baseline.hpp:12 init = false); thesis/docs/benchmark-example-consistency.md:85 already records prompt/oracle/example as consistent for this benchmark. The MPI prompt's "Every rank has a complete copy of x. Return the result on all ranks." is the wording under which the observed even-np cancellation class was already adjudicated a REAL model defect (pilot-001-corrected-numbers.md:88), so it is not re-opened here.
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: yes. validate() fills inline with `x[i] = rand() % 2` (cpu.cc:78) — there is NO ENHANCED_FILL call site anywhere in this driver, unlike its siblings 26-29 (which call ENHANCED_FILL at cpu.cc:61/63/64-65). thesis/enhanced_tests/benchmark_shapes.json:225-231 records this as `fill_sites: 0`, `explicit_values_supported: false`. Consequence: every fill pattern is a compile-time no-op here, so pattern-distinct specs at the same size are byte-identical tests (confirmed empirically in the pilot: validation-report.md:410 — reduce/25's (7,all_same), (7,alternating) and (7,random) show the identical status vector). Only N can currently be varied. Every degenerate case below except plain size variation therefore needs a benchmark-specific fill site — and it must be bool-specific: enhancedFillPattern is written for floating/integral/complex DType (enhanced-fill.hpp:105-226) and `std::vector<bool>`'s proxy reference plus the two-valued domain (all_zeros == all_same == alternating collapse pathologically on bools) need their own construction, e.g. all-false / all-true(N even) / all-true(N odd) / exactly-one-true(k) / exactly-two-true.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Mathematically DEFINED for this operation (the identity of XOR is `false`, and the oracle's `std::reduce(..., false, ...)` realises it, so nothing here is out of domain):
- N = 0 — empty vector; result = false (identity). Defined. Currently BLIND: reference is (false,false) in both trials, so a `return false;` stub passes (verified by direct computation over the driver's stream; matches pilot-001-corrected-numbers.md:94).
- N = 1 — result = x[0]. Defined. Currently blind for the same reason ((false,false) at offset 16).
- N = 2 — result = x[0] != x[1]. Defined. Currently (false,false), blind.
- all elements false, any N — result = false. Defined. THE case that separates a correct XOR from any "return true if non-empty" error. Needs a fill site.
- all elements true, N even — result = false; all elements true, N odd — result = true. Defined, and the single sharpest discriminator in this benchmark: it separates XOR/parity from OR/any_of, which agree on almost every random input. Needs a fill site.
- exactly one true (at index 0, at N-1, at an interior index) — result = true regardless of N and position. Defined. Separates XOR from AND and from "first/last element" errors.
- exactly two trues — result = false. Defined. Separates XOR from OR.
- N a multiple of 64 vs N = 64k+1 — full final word vs a 1-bit final word; the two extremes of the bit-packing tail. Defined; a pure size case, constructible today.
NOT degenerate for this operation (no such notion exists here): duplicates, sortedness, all-values-equal in a numeric sense, extreme/NaN values, near-singular structure. The value domain is {false,true}, so `all_zeros`, `all_same` and `extreme_values` collapse onto "all false" / "all true", and `ascending`/`descending`/`sorted_except_one` are meaningless.
Of the eight cases above, only the two pure-size ones and N in {0,1,2} are constructible with today's driver; the rest are blocked on the missing fill site.

benchmarks.name: 26_reduce_product_of_inverses
benchmarks.input_form: One 1-D dense vector `std::vector<double> x` of length N. Relevant dimension: N = element count only (no second dimension, no derived nnz, no matrix structure). The operation is P(x) = prod_{i even} x_i * prod_{i odd} (1/x_i), i.e. a length-N multiplicative reduction whose per-element transform depends on the GLOBAL index parity. Return value is a single scalar double.
benchmarks.min_size: 0. The empty product is mathematically defined and the oracle returns exactly 1.0 for N=0 (std::reduce with init 1.0, baseline.hpp:16) — MEASURED: `empty (n=0) product=1 finite=1`. There is no mathematical size floor and no valid-size FORM restriction: every N >= 0 is valid, odd N included (the prompt's own example has N=5).
benchmarks.max_size: 16418 for the enhanced stage, forced by the OPERATION (not by the harness): sigma(log10|P|) = 0.38445*sqrt(N) must keep the +/-308-decade double exponent range at >= 6 sigma, i.e. sqrt(N) <= 308/(6*0.38445) = 133.5 -> N <= ~17800. Measured confirmation of the ceiling: N=32770 consumes 189.8 of 308 decades on one driver draw; N=1048576 and N=4194304 return inf. (No harness-imposed max: TEST_SIZE is a free compile define, enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79.)
benchmarks.special_conditions:
(1) VALUE domain, hard: x_i != 0 for every ODD index i. 1/0 = +inf and the product then evaluates to inf or (with a zero also at an even index) NaN — MEASURED: `zero at ODD index (n=2) product=inf finite=0`, `pattern all_zeros n=15 product=-nan finite=0`. The driver generator guarantees this (fillRand(x, 1.0, 100.0) -> x_i in [1,100], strictly positive, utilities.hpp:144-159 + cpu.cc:26/61).
(2) REPRESENTABILITY, the binding size constraint: log10|P| is a mean-zero random walk with per-element sigma_log10 = 0.38445 (Var[ln U(1,100)] = 0.78362), so sigma(log10|P|) = 0.38445*sqrt(N). The reference is finite only while the walk AND its running partial products stay inside the double exponent range (+/-308 decades). Criterion adopted: keep 308 decades at >= 6 sigma. N=16418 -> sigma = 49.3 decades = 6.25 sigma (safe); N=32770 -> 4.42 sigma and a MEASURED running excursion of +189.8 decades on one of two driver draws (62% of the range consumed) -> rejected; N=1048576 -> MEASURED product = inf on both driver draws.
(3) NO power-of-two, divisibility, minimum-point-count or matrix-form condition of any kind.
(4) Chosen additionally (operation-derived, not candidate-derived): medium and large satisfy N === 2 (mod 32), so an equal split into 2, 4, 8 or 16 contiguous parts has an ODD leading chunk length and therefore at least one sub-range that BEGINS at an odd global index — the only structural case that distinguishes global-index parity from sub-range-local parity. small is odd, so the trailing element is unpaired (8 non-inverted vs 7 inverted factors).
benchmarks.size_semantics: Element count of the single input vector x. TEST_SIZE / ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE / DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE is used directly as `std::vector<double> x(TEST_SIZE)` (cpu.cc:52) and `ctx->x.resize(DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE)` (cpu.cc:33) — not a side length, not a nnz seed, nothing derived from it. N/2 of the elements (rounded down) are inverted; for odd N there is one extra non-inverted factor.
benchmarks.complexity: Time O(N), one multiplication (and N/2 divisions) per element; oracle also O(N) AUXILIARY SPACE — baseline.hpp:13-15 materializes a full transformed copy via push_back before std::reduce, so its measured cost is allocation/page-fault dominated, not FLOP dominated.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
GENERATOR (as requested, verbatim behaviour, MEASURED): the only fill site is cpu.cc:61 `ENHANCED_FILL(x, 1.0, 100.0)`, which without ENHANCED_* defines is fillRand(x, 1.0, 100.0) = `(rand()/(double)RAND_MAX)*(100.0-1.0)+1.0` (utilities.hpp:144-159). Value range: [1.0, 100.0] closed, i.i.d. uniform, drawn from UNSEEDED rand() (utilities.hpp:242, "as if srand(1)"), so the input is DETERMINISTIC per (size, call order); init() consumes DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE draws first, then validate() runs MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS = 2 trials (utilities.hpp:26).
SIGN CHANGES / CANCELLATION: NONE in the additive sense. All x_i > 0, so every factor is positive and P > 0 always; there is no subtraction anywhere in the oracle. The cancellation is purely MULTIPLICATIVE (log-space): even-index factors lie in [1,100] (log10 in [0,2]), odd-index factors are inverses in [0.01,1] (log10 in [-2,0]), and the two streams cancel in expectation, leaving a mean-zero log-space random walk with sigma_log10 = 0.38445 per element.
LARGEST N OF THE PROPOSED SIZES = 16418. At N=16418 the theoretical spread is sigma(log10|P|) = 49.3 decades; MEASURED on the driver's own deterministic stream: trial 0 P = 1.02281e-36, trial 1 P = 8.9588e-62; running partial-product extremes log10 in [-95.98, +26.85]. For calibration at the other sizes: N=514 -> 6.83782e+09 / 4.71057e+08; N=15 -> 0.450123 / 677.899; and at the CURRENT default TEST_SIZE 1024 -> 2.85321 / 94734.3 with a running excursion up to 1e+15.7. => Any ABSOLUTE tolerance is meaningless here; the tolerance must be RELATIVE. Ingredients for the tolerance task: reassociation error of an N-term product is ~sqrt(N)*u typical / N*u worst case with u = 1.11e-16, i.e. 1.4e-14 typical and 1.8e-12 worst case at N=16418; a log-domain (sum-of-logs then exp) implementation, which is mathematically legitimate, carries rel err ~ u*|ln P| ~ 1.1e-16 * 113 = 1.3e-14 plus its own summation error, so a relative tolerance in the 1e-9 range covers both without hiding logic errors.
SCALE AXIS: the sizes span 15 -> 514 -> 16418 (34x, 32x — geometric), all far inside the representable domain. small = 15: odd, so the last element sits at an even index and stays un-inverted (8 vs 7 factors); at the pipeline's enhanced launch (4 threads / 4 ranks) the split is ragged (4/4/4/3) so sub-ranges differ in length parity; small enough that the structured fill patterns are still informative (alternating(1,100) -> 1e-14, representable; MEASURED). medium = 514 = 2*257 and large = 16418 = 2*8209, both === 2 (mod 32): N/2, ceil(N/4), ceil(N/8), ceil(N/16) are all ODD, forcing at least one sub-range to start at an odd global index — the structural case that separates a correct global-parity implementation from one that re-derives parity locally per chunk. large is the largest size the DOMAIN admits (see special_conditions (2)), not the largest the time budget admits.

The operation is defined for every N >= 0, odd N included (the prompt already demonstrates an odd-length input, [4,2,10,4,5] -> 25, and the oracle reproduces exactly 25 — MEASURED), and there is no power-of-two, divisibility or minimum-length condition. The only real precondition (x_i != 0 at odd indices) is a property of the INPUT the harness supplies, not something a candidate can be blamed for, so it belongs in the enhanced-test spec (exclude the all_zeros and spike_at fill patterns), not in the prompt.

benchmarks.name: 27_reduce_average
benchmarks.input_form: One flat `std::vector<double> x` of length n; values drawn uniform in [0.0, 100.0] by the generic fill site. Exactly ONE dimension: n. Return value is a single `double` (the arithmetic mean). Signature `double average(std::vector<double> const& x)` identical across serial/omp/mpi; the mpi prompt additionally specifies that every rank holds a complete copy of x and that the average must be returned on ALL ranks (Allreduce, not Reduce). No structure, no ordering, no matrix/graph/point-set precondition. `benchmark_shapes.json` records this as `fill_sites: 1`, `elements_per_site: ["n"]`, `total_elements: "n"`, `explicit_values_supported: true`.
benchmarks.min_size: 1. The arithmetic mean is defined for any non-empty multiset, so n=1 is the smallest MATHEMATICALLY DEFINED and smallest INFORMATIVE size (measured: a candidate returning a constant is caught at n=1). n=0 is accepted by the spec schema (specs.py:290 rejects only size < 0) and by the driver, but the oracle evaluates 0.0/0 = NaN — measured, harness printed `avg=-nan` — so it belongs on the degenerate axis, not on the scale axis. No floor above 1 is imposed by the operation.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — FORCED BY THE HARNESS, not by the operation or the budget. thesis/config/config.yaml:572 `max_spec_size: 4096`, actually enforced in thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294 ("size %s exceeds max_spec_size %s"), which rejects the spec outright; the mutation operator's `size*2` is filtered by the same bound (specs.py:534). Secondary hard ceiling far above it: fillRand indexes with `int i` (utilities.hpp:146), so n >= 2^31 is undefined behaviour. Neither the operation (total for every n) nor the 10 s budget (~4.9e9 elements) binds.
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE on the size axis. No power-of-two requirement, no minimum point count, no valid-matrix construction, no sortedness/uniqueness precondition. Any n >= 0 and any finite real values form a valid input. The only genuine preconditions are VALUE-RANGE conditions imposed by the comparator, not by the operation: cpu.cc:74 compares with an ABSOLUTE epsilon of 1e-4 on the returned scalar, so (a) a value_range that pushes |average| far above 1e4 silently converts the check into bit-exact equality (spike_at: sum is exactly DBL_MAX/2 because the [0,100] terms are wholly absorbed — ulp at 1e307 is ~1e291 — and the average ~1e304 must then match to the last bit), and (b) extreme_values (alternating DBL lowest/max) can drive the REFERENCE itself to +/-inf or NaN, which the working-tree A1b/A1f contract turns into a non-finite-reference exclusion. Computed corollary that matters for sizing: with the default [0,100] range the average is ~50, so 1e-4 absolute is ~2e-6 RELATIVE, while worst-case naive-summation error at the harness ceiling n=4096 is 4096*2^-53 ~ 4.5e-13 relative (~2.3e-11 absolute). Reassociation between the serial oracle (std::reduce, which is itself permitted to reorder) and a 4-way OMP/MPI tree reduction therefore CANNOT trip the tolerance anywhere in the legal size range — the scale axis for this benchmark probes loop/decomposition structure, never numerical accumulation.
benchmarks.size_semantics: size == ELEMENT COUNT of x, 1:1, with no derivation. cpu.cc:52-54 reads `const size_t TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024); std::vector<double> x(TEST_SIZE);` — so -DENHANCED_TEST_SIZE=N gives literally N doubles = 8N bytes. Not a side length, not an nnz derivation, not a point count. benchmarks.domain_rationale:
min_size=1 follows from the operation: the mean of a non-empty multiset is defined, the mean of the empty multiset is not (oracle: 0.0/0 = NaN, measured). max_size=4096 is NOT chosen — it is forced by the harness (config.yaml:572 max_spec_size, enforced at specs.py:293-294). The three scale points span the only usable dynamic range this cap leaves (~2 decades above the degenerate region) and each marks a distinct regime of a flat O(n) reduction under the pipeline's FIXED 4-way decomposition (config.yaml:602-604 omp_threads: 4, mpi_ranks: 4):
- SMALL = 33: the smallest size at which a vectorized/unrolled steady-state loop body genuinely exists AND leaves a non-trivial tail. 33 = 4 full 8-double blocks (4-lane AVX2 double vector x 2 unroll) + 1 leftover element, and it splits 4 ways as 9/8/8/8 — so it exercises simultaneously the SIMD scalar tail and the uneven rank/thread chunk (n/size + remainder), the two classic off-by-one sites of a hand-written reduction. Measured to sit clearly in the pre-asymptotic regime (3.0-3.5 ns/elem vs the 0.5 ns/elem asymptote), i.e. it is genuinely "small" for this loop rather than merely a small number. It is deliberately NOT one of the static base sizes (0,1,2,7), which cover n below/just above the worker count on the degenerate axis.
- MEDIUM = 1024: the steady-state, evenly divisible counterpart. Measured at the asymptotic per-element cost (0.51-0.56 ns/elem), 8 KB and comfortably L1-resident, and it divides exactly by 4 (256 per worker) so the clean-decomposition path is represented alongside SMALL's ragged one. It is additionally the driver's OWN authored validation size (cpu.cc:52 default 1024) — the size at which this benchmark was written and has always been validated — which anchors the axis to the benchmark's own reference point instead of an arbitrary round number.
- LARGE = 4096: the harness ceiling itself, i.e. the largest input the enhanced stage will ever accept for any benchmark. It maximises the accumulation depth (and hence the reassociation freedom a parallel candidate has), it is exactly 32768 bytes = the classic 32 KB L1d boundary, and it again divides cleanly by 4. Going beyond it is not a budget question but a rejected-spec question.
The 10 s serial-oracle budget is NOT the binding constraint here and never comes close: measured 1.7e-6 s at LARGE, six orders of magnitude under. Measured headroom (2.06 ns/elem at 67.1M elements) says 10 s would buy ~4.9e9 elements ~ 39 GB — beyond both the container's memory and the `int i` loop counter in fillRand (utilities.hpp:146, UB at n >= 2^31). The budget is satisfied trivially; the harness cap binds. Per the instructions this is not a "budget inappropriate, stop" case — the budget is a ceiling and it is met with enormous margin; it is simply not what selects LARGE.
Explicitly NOT used in any of this: no observed candidate/model code was consulted; the sizes follow from the mean's definition, the O(n) single-pass structure, the fixed 4-way launch config, the cache hierarchy, and the harness cap alone.

benchmarks.name: 28_reduce_smallest_odd_number
benchmarks.input_form: One std::vector<int> x of length n. Exactly one dimension (n) and exactly one fill site — thesis/enhanced_tests/benchmark_shapes.json:250-258 records fill_sites 1, total_elements "n", explicit_values_supported true. Output: a single int, compared by EXACT integer equality (cpu.cc:74 -> utilities.hpp:483-485), no epsilon, no ordering, no canonicalisation. Driver value domain: integers in [0,100]. The generator call is fillRand(x, 0.0, 100.0) (cpu.cc:28 and cpu.cc:63) — DType deduces to double from the literals even though the container is vector<int>, so the floating branch runs (utilities.hpp:148-149, val = rand()/RAND_MAX*100.0) and the double is truncated on assignment into the int slot: each of 0..99 with probability ~1/100, value 100 with probability ~4.7e-10. Mathematically the operation is defined on any std::vector<int>. MPI form: the prompt states every rank holds a COMPLETE copy of x and the result must be returned on all ranks, i.e. the input is replicated, not distributed — n is identical on every rank (generation-prompts-thesis.json, mpi entry at :605-609; cpu.cc:29/:64 BCAST(x, INT)).
benchmarks.min_size: 0 — there is no size floor. n=0 is constructed, run and graded: config.yaml:562 puts sizes [0,1,2,7] into the static base set for every parameterizable benchmark, and cpu.cc:52 makes this benchmark parameterizable (ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT, checked at run_enhanced_tests.py:874). The oracle terminates on n=0 and returns its std::reduce init value INT_MAX (MEASURED). The only spec-level size constraints in the whole harness are size >= 0 and size <= max_spec_size (specs.py:290-295); no per-benchmark floor exists. n=0 and n=1 are VALUE questions (what should be returned when no odd exists), not size violations, and are therefore listed under degenerate_cases, not as a floor.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — HARNESS-FORCED. thesis/config/config.yaml:571-572 `max_spec_size: 4096`, enforced for every spec source (static base, LLM seeds, mutations) in thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-295 ("size %s exceeds max_spec_size %s") via validate_spec, called from build_spec_set at specs.py:580 and :593. The OPERATION imposes no upper bound at all: the oracle at 4096 costs 6.0e-5 s and even at 2^28 = 268,435,456 elements it stays inside the 10 s budget (5.63 s measured). The cap, not the runtime budget, is what bounds this row.
benchmarks.special_conditions: No condition on the SIZE: no power of two, no minimum element count, no matrix/point-set/graph form, no derived nnz. n may be any non-negative integer. The genuine preconditions are VALUE conditions, and none of them is stated in the prompt — all three verified by running the real oracle: (1) x must contain at least one odd element, otherwise "the smallest odd number" does not exist and the oracle silently returns its INT_MAX fold identity (measured: {}, {2}, {0,2,4,6} -> 2147483647). (2) Every element must be non-negative for the oracle to agree with the prompt's plain reading: baseline.hpp:16-24 tests `a % 2 == 1`, which is FALSE for negative odd numbers in C++ (-3 % 2 == -1), so the oracle treats negative odds as even (measured: {-3,-1,-5} -> INT_MAX; {-3,5,-1,7,3} -> 3, not -3). (3) INT_MAX must not occur in x: it is simultaneously a legal odd input and the fold identity (baseline.hpp:15), so "INT_MAX is the smallest odd" and "there is no odd at all" are indistinguishable (measured: {2,4,INT_MAX} -> 2147483647). The driver's own generator satisfies (1)-(3) with overwhelming probability for n >= 8 because it only emits [0,100]; the enhanced fill patterns do NOT (see degenerate_cases). Positive property worth recording: under the oracle's own parity predicate the binary op is associative and commutative with INT_MAX as identity, so the reduction is order-independent — a parallel candidate may reorder freely and the exact-equality comparison is sound (no epsilon needed, unlike the float reduce siblings).
benchmarks.size_semantics: size = the element count n of the single input vector x. It is NOT a side length, not a point count, and nothing is derived from it (no nnz, no n*n). ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE overrides TEST_SIZE at cpu.cc:52 and is used directly as the vector length at cpu.cc:54; benchmark_shapes.json:250-258 confirms total_elements = "n" over 1 fill site. Under MPI the same n is materialised on every rank (replicated input), so wall-clock memory is n*4 bytes per rank.
benchmarks.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space. baseline.hpp:15 is a single std::reduce with NO execution policy, i.e. one sequential fold over n elements applying a constant-work binary op (two comparisons + two modulo operations). Measured throughput 12-22 ns per element (1.4e-5 s at n=1024, 4.9e-5 s at n=4093, 0.371 s at n=2^24, 5.63 s at n=2^28) — the per-element cost is dominated by the data-dependent branches in the lambda, not by memory bandwidth.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
The operation is a single-pass conditional min-reduction over ints: a per-element parity predicate plus an associative/commutative min with INT_MAX as identity. Scale therefore introduces NO new mathematical cases — every mathematical case is a VALUE case (see degenerate_cases). What scale does introduce is decomposition structure, and that is the only axis on which small/medium/large can carry information for this operation. The three points are chosen to span that axis, plus a measured statistical property of the driver's own value domain.

SMALL = 17. Smallest prime strictly greater than 16, the widest common int32 SIMD lane count (AVX-512 = 16, AVX2 = 8). 17 = 1x16 + 1 = 2x8 + 1, so for BOTH common widths the input is exactly one full vector body plus a single-element scalar tail — the minimal non-empty remainder. Being prime, it is divisible by no plausible thread or rank count (the enhanced stage launches omp_threads=4 / mpi_ranks=4, config.yaml enhanced_launch), so every chunked decomposition is uneven. It is also strictly above the largest static base size (7, config.yaml:562), so it adds a scale point rather than duplicating one. Independently justified by a MEASURED property: at n=17 the driver's random fill still discriminates — three consecutive draws produced oracle answers 19, 1, 29 — because P(value 1 present) = 1 - 0.99^17 = 15.7%.

MEDIUM = 1024. The benchmark's OWN configured validation size (cpu.cc:52, ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)), so enhanced verdicts at this point are directly comparable with the stage-1 base verdict on identical input geometry. Structurally it is the exact complement of small: 2^10 divides evenly by every SIMD width (8/16) and every plausible thread/rank count (2,4,8,16,32,64), so there is no remainder anywhere and the decomposition is perfectly balanced. 4 KiB of ints, fully L1-resident, so the reduction is compute-bound.

LARGE = 4093. Largest prime <= max_spec_size (4096), i.e. the largest scale the harness admits (config.yaml:572, specs.py:293-295), carrying the remainder property at maximum scale: with 4 ranks it splits 1024/1023/1023/1023, so a SIMD tail, a chunk tail and a rank tail all occur simultaneously — a combination no smaller size can produce, because at n=17 there is no chunk level at all. 4096 itself was deliberately REJECTED as large: it is 2^12 and therefore structurally identical to medium (perfectly divisible at every level), so the pair (1024, 4096) would differ only by a factor of 4 in scale and carry one structural fact between them. The 3-element sacrifice costs nothing (measured 4.9e-5 s vs 6.0e-5 s). One transparency note: explicit_values fills cyclically and is capped at 64 values (config.yaml:576), and 64 divides 4096 but not 4093, so a 64-value cycle is truncated mid-cycle at large — this changes the input, never the correctness of the oracle's answer on it.

MEASURED domain fact that constrains what large can be used FOR: because the driver's value range is [0,100], P(the minimum odd value 1 is absent) = 0.99^n, which is 15.7% at n=17 but 3.4e-5 at n=1024 and 1.2e-18 at n=4093. The random pattern therefore returns the constant 1 at medium and large — confirmed in every timed repetition at 1024, 4093, 4096 and 2^24. Medium and large are consequently decomposition/scale probes only; their discriminating power must come from structured or benchmark-specific fills, never from `random`.

Spacing note: the geometric spread (17 -> 1024 -> 4093) is compressed at the top because of the 4096 harness cap, not because of the operation. Absent that cap the operation-derived large would be the benchmark's own DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE 1<<24 = 16,777,216 (drivers/problem-sizes.json:254-258), 64 MiB, i.e. the first point that exceeds a typical last-level cache and makes the pass memory-bound — measured at 0.371 s, still 27x inside the budget. Under the current cap every enhanced input is <= 16 KiB and hence L1-resident, so the enhanced size axis structurally cannot reach the memory-bandwidth regime in which the benchmark's speedup is measured. That is a limitation of the row, stated rather than papered over.

No part of this sizing was derived from any candidate or model code; the inputs to the decision were the prompt, the oracle, the driver generator, the asymptotic complexity, the harness cap and the runtime budget.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Which degenerate inputs are mathematically DEFINED for this operation (all verified against the real oracle):

DEFINED, and the oracle is right:
- All elements odd, or at least one odd present: the answer is the minimum odd value. Measured {7,7,7,7} -> 7 (all-identical-odd exercises the a>=b branch where both arguments are equal and odd).
- Odd value larger than every even value: {9,2,4} must give 9, not 2 — the operation is a min over a FILTERED subset, not a global min.
- n=1 with an odd element: measured {3} -> 3.
- Ascending/descending ramps: measured {0,14,28,42,57,71,85,100} -> 57 in both directions (order-independence confirmed).

NOT mathematically defined by the prompt — the oracle nonetheless returns a value:
- n=0 (empty vector): min over the empty set does not exist. Oracle returns 2147483647 = its std::reduce init (measured). GRADED in every run (static base size 0, config.yaml:562).
- n=1 with an even element: measured {2} -> 2147483647. GRADED (static base size 1).
- Any n with no odd element at all: measured {0,2,4,6} -> 2147483647. This is not exotic — THREE of the eleven offered fill patterns land here at EVERY size, because the call site's range is [0,100]: all_zeros -> all 0, all_same -> all 50 (midpoint), alternating -> 0/100. All three measured -> INT_MAX. Between them they carry one bit of information about the operation.

MATHEMATICALLY DEFINED but the oracle CONTRADICTS the prompt:
- Negative odd values. -3 is odd; the oracle's `a % 2 == 1` (baseline.hpp:16-24) is false for it. Measured {-3,-1,-5} -> INT_MAX and {-3,5,-1,7,3} -> 3 (not -3). Already scheduled and gate-passed in the pilot spec set (thesis/results/cache/enhanced/specs.jsonl:138 and :141, both explicit_values with negative odds).
- Input containing INT_MAX. Mathematically INT_MAX is odd, so it is a legal answer; but it is also the fold identity, so "INT_MAX is the smallest odd" is indistinguishable from "there is no odd". Measured {2,4,INT_MAX} -> 2147483647.

NOT A WELL-DEFINED INPUT AT ALL (harness defect surfaced here, verified with UBSan):
- extreme_values (pattern 6) and spike_at (pattern 9). ENHANCED_FILL is invoked with the double literals 0.0/100.0 (cpu.cc:63), so DType deduces to double while the container is vector<int>; enhanced-fill.hpp:200 assigns +/-DBL_MAX (and enhanced-fill.hpp:212 assigns DBL_MAX/2) into an int slot. That is an out-of-range floating-to-integer conversion = undefined behaviour, and it is OPTIMIZATION-LEVEL DEPENDENT in practice: at -O3 pattern 6 produced alternating -2147483648 / 2147483647, at -O0 it produced ALL -2147483648, with UBSan reporting "drivers/cpp/enhanced-fill.hpp:200:81 runtime error: -1.79769e+308 is outside the range of representable values of type 'int'". Pattern 9 planted 2147483647 (i.e. the fold identity itself) at the spike index at -O3. specs.jsonl:142 schedules extreme_values at size 2 with the stated intent "INT_MIN (even) and INT_MAX (odd)" — that intent is only accidentally realised, and only at -O3. These two patterns cannot serve as reproducible inputs for this benchmark as the call site currently stands.

benchmarks.name: 29_reduce_sum_of_min_of_pairs
benchmarks.input_form: Two dense vectors of `double` of EQUAL length N, passed as `std::vector<double> const& x, std::vector<double> const& y`; return value is a single `double`. Relevant dimension: exactly one — N = the common length. Driver values are drawn i.i.d. uniform from [0.0, 100.0] for both vectors independently (`fillRand`). Operation: s = sum_{i=0}^{N-1} min(x_i, y_i).
benchmarks.min_size: 0. Size 0 is mathematically defined (empty sum = 0) and executes cleanly: MEASURED `N=0 -> oracle=0`. Size 1 is likewise defined (`N=1 -> oracle=2.5` for x=[3.5], y=[2.5]). The operation imposes NO floor. The only floor anywhere in the stack is a harness one and applies to three fill patterns only: the k-parameterised patterns 7/8/9 need size >= 2 (enhanced-fill.hpp:22-24).
benchmarks.max_size:
yes, forced — three independent ceilings, the lowest binding.
(1) OPERATION + COMPARATOR (binding): with the driver's [0,100] range, a correct re-ordered (parallel) summation exceeds the 1e-4 absolute epsilon at N = 2^23 = 8,388,608 (MEASURED 9.996e-5, exactly at the wall) and clearly at 2^24 (1.86e-4). Practical ceiling with a >=10x margin: ~2.5e6. This ceiling scales with the SUM magnitude, i.e. with N * E[min(x,y)] — a spec that widens the value range lowers it proportionally.
(2) HARNESS, generator: fillRand uses an `int` loop counter (utilities.hpp:146), so any size >= 2^31 is undefined behaviour in the input generator itself.
(3) HARNESS, memory: the oracle allocates a third N-vector (baseline.hpp:15) -> 24 B/element. MEASURED OOM-kill (exit 137) at N = 6.7e7 in the pipeline container (7 GiB total).
(4) HARNESS, current config: `max_spec_size: 4096` (thesis/config/config.yaml:570-572) — enhanced-test spec validation REJECTS any size above 4096 today. Under the config as it stands, MEDIUM (65,536) and LARGE (2,097,151) are unreachable; both would require raising that cap. Flagged rather than silently accommodated, because collapsing the scale axis to <=4096 (32 KiB, entirely L1/L2) would leave the memory-bandwidth regime and the accumulation-error regime completely untested for this benchmark.
benchmarks.special_conditions: (1) |y| >= |x| — the oracle iterates x.begin()..x.end() and reads y through the second input iterator (baseline.hpp:16); the driver always allocates both at exactly TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:55), so in practice |x| == |y| == N. This is the only structural precondition. (2) NO power-of-two, sortedness, positivity, distinctness or minimum-count condition exists. (3) The real, non-obvious condition is NUMERIC and couples size to the value range: validation is `reportAndCompareScalar(correct, test, 1e-4)` with an ABSOLUTE epsilon (cpu.cc:77) applied to a scalar whose magnitude grows as N * E[min(x,y)] (= 100/3 * N for the driver's own [0,100] range). Because the oracle fixes ONE summation order (std::reduce over z, libstdc++ = sequential left-to-right, baseline.hpp:19) while the omp/mpi prompts explicitly ask for a parallel sum, the admissible N is bounded by when a legitimately re-ordered summation still lands inside 1e-4 absolute. MEASURED (max over block counts p in {2,4,8,16,64,1024}): N=1023 -> 7.3e-12; N=65,536 -> 5.6e-9; N=2,097,151 -> 7.8e-6 (12.9x margin); N=4,194,304 -> 2.9e-5 (3.5x margin); N=8,388,608 -> 1.00e-4 (AT the epsilon); N=16,777,216 -> 1.86e-4 (EXCEEDS — a correct 2-block parallel reduction FAILS). (4) Consequence of the same absolute epsilon at the other end: if a spec's value range pushes |sum| to ~1e8 or above, the 1e-4 absolute tolerance becomes vacuous; at DBL_MAX-scale ranges the oracle overflows to +inf and `reportAndCompareScalarImpl` auto-passes ANY candidate (utilities.hpp:450-454) — MEASURED for the existing frozen pilot spec (all_same [DBL_MAX,DBL_MAX], size 4096).
benchmarks.size_semantics: Element count per vector. TEST_SIZE is the common length N of BOTH x and y (cpu.cc:55: `std::vector<double> x(TEST_SIZE), y(TEST_SIZE)`), i.e. the number of index positions / pairs reduced. Total input data is 2*N doubles = 16 N bytes; the oracle's working set is 24 N bytes because it materialises a third vector. It is NOT a side length, not a total element count across both vectors, and no count is derived from it (no nnz, no density). One `size` fully determines the input shape.
benchmarks.complexity: Oracle: Theta(N) time, Theta(N) auxiliary space. baseline.hpp materialises a third vector z of N doubles (`z.resize(x.size())`, line 15 — zero-fills), runs one `std::transform` over N elements (lines 16-18) and one `std::reduce` over N elements (line 19). Two passes, memory-bandwidth bound; total footprint 24 B per index (x, y, z). MEASURED throughput ~1.4e8 elem/s in the warm regime (2,097,151 in 0.0150 s) degrading to ~5.8e7 elem/s at 1.68e7 and ~8.4e6 elem/s at 3.36e7 as the working set leaves memory-resident territory. The Theta(N) AUXILIARY allocation, not the Theta(N) arithmetic, is what ends the size range in the pipeline container.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
min_size = 0 because the empty sum is the mathematically defined neutral element and the oracle returns exactly that (measured). No condition is imposed by the operation itself.

The scale axis is derived from the two things that actually change with N for a bandwidth-bound elementwise-min + sum-reduction: (a) where the working set sits in the memory hierarchy, and (b) how much floating-point re-association error a correct parallel reduction may accumulate against the oracle's fixed sequential order. Divisibility is alternated deliberately across the three points so that no single assumption (SIMD width, chunk size, rank count) can satisfy all three.

SMALL = 1023 = 2^10 - 1. The driver's own default validation size is 1024 (cpu.cc:53); 1023 keeps that scale but removes divisibility by 2, 4, 8, 16 and by the pilot's 4 threads / 4 ranks (config.yaml:603-604), so every decomposition leaves a remainder (4 ranks -> 256/256/256/255) and every vectorised loop needs a scalar tail. x+y = 16 KiB, i.e. L1-resident: the reduction runs at latency, not bandwidth. Sizes 0, 1, 2, 7 — the sub-decomposition regime where a worker gets zero elements — are already the universal static base (config.yaml:562) and belong to the degenerate axis, so SMALL sits one step above them.

MEDIUM = 65,536 = 2^16. x+y = 1.0 MiB (1.5 MiB with the oracle's z): the largest round power of two whose whole working set still fits a typical L2/L3, so a 4-way decomposition is a real workload while bandwidth is not yet the story. It is the exactly-balanced counterpart to SMALL: divisible by every SIMD width, by 4 threads and 4 ranks, remainder zero everywhere — the aligned fast path a candidate may special-case.

LARGE = 2,097,151 = 2^21 - 1. x+y = 32 MiB, above the LLC of the target machines, so the operation runs in its true memory-bandwidth regime and the accumulation chain is 2^21 long. It is odd again, so the remainder path is exercised at a scale where a dropped tail element (~33.3 in expectation) is still 5 orders of magnitude above the 1e-4 epsilon and therefore detected. The value is capped here by the operation's OWN validation contract, not by the clock: at this size the measured worst-case divergence of a correct block-parallel summation from the oracle is 7.8e-6, a 12.9x margin under the 1e-4 absolute epsilon, whereas 2^22 leaves only 3.5x and 2^23 is exactly at the epsilon.

None of these three values was taken from, or checked against, any candidate or model output; they follow from the cache hierarchy, the divisibility structure of a parallel reduction, and measured floating-point re-association error.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no. The prompt (serial/omp/mpi, thesis/prompts/generation-prompts-thesis.json) states the operation completely and matches the oracle — `thesis/docs/benchmark-example-consistency.md:89` records benchmark 29 as "consistent / consistent". Sizes are chosen by the driver, never by the model, and the operation has no size precondition to communicate (unlike closest-pair or triangle-area, it is total on N >= 0). Adding a size sentence would only leak harness detail. The one restriction that IS needed does not belong in the prompt but in the SPEC GENERATOR: value ranges must stay in a magnitude regime where an absolute 1e-4 is a meaningful discriminator.
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: yes — a benchmark-specific TWO-VECTOR construction is required, because the current single-pattern-per-spec fill makes x and y IDENTICAL for every deterministic pattern, which turns min(x_i, y_i) into the identity and degenerates the benchmark into a plain sum. validate() applies the same ENHANCED_FILL to x and then to y (cpu.cc:64-65); deterministic patterns depend only on (size, lo, hi), so both vectors come out bit-identical. MEASURED at n=4096, positions where x != y: random 4096/4096, all_zeros 0, all_same 0, ascending 0, descending 0, alternating 0, extreme_values 0, duplicate_at 4096, sorted_except_one 0, spike_at 4095 — i.e. 7 of the 10 implemented patterns (and 7 of the 11 offered in config.yaml:576-579) produce sumOfMin == plainSum(x) exactly. Only the three rand()-consuming patterns (0 random, 7 duplicate_at, 9 spike_at) exercise the min at all. A construction that gives x and y different patterns, different ranges, or an offset/shift is needed for this benchmark specifically; the plain 1-D fill contract cannot express it.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
All of the following are MATHEMATICALLY DEFINED for this operation and were executed against the real oracle (scratch harness `degenerate.cpp`); none is a size floor.
- size 0 (empty pair set): sum over the empty set = 0. MEASURED oracle = 0. No guard needed, `std::reduce` on an empty range returns double{}.
- size 1: sum = min(x_0, y_0). MEASURED oracle = 2.5 for x=[3.5], y=[2.5].
- size 2: MEASURED oracle = 117.748, block split p=2 bit-identical.
- all values equal AND x == y (a tie at every index): min is unambiguous. MEASURED n=4096, all 7.0 -> oracle 28672, every block split p in {2,3,4,5,7,16} bit-identical. Probes that min() is applied per index rather than being skipped or double-counted.
- all zeros: sum = 0 exactly, all splits agree.
- x identical to y at every index: DEFINED, but semantically degenerate — min collapses to the identity and the task becomes a plain sum. Not an exotic case: it is what 7 of the 10 implemented fill patterns currently produce (see custom_input_construction_needed).
- extreme_values pattern (alternating DBL_LOWEST / DBL_MAX): MEASURED oracle = 0 at n=1024 (even) and DBL_LOWEST at n=1023 (odd) — both finite; block splits p in {2,3,4,5,7,16} all agreed within 1e-4 at both sizes. The a-priori overflow hazard (two DBL_LOWEST partials summing to -inf) did NOT materialise for these splits; it is split-dependent and was not exhaustively proven absent.
- overflow / non-finite regime (value range at DBL_MAX): MEASURED n=4096, all_same [DBL_MAX,DBL_MAX] -> oracle = +inf, and utilities.hpp:450-454 then auto-passes ANY candidate. This is exactly the shipped frozen pilot spec #3 for this benchmark (thesis/docs/pilot-001-corrected-numbers.md:245), which is therefore VACUOUS on two independent counts (x == y, and non-finite reference).

benchmarks.name: 30_scan_prefix_sum
benchmarks.input_form: One `std::vector<double> x` of length n (the only input), plus `std::vector<double> &output` that the driver has ALREADY pre-sized to n. The single relevant dimension is n = element count. Default value distribution: uniform in [-100.0, 100.0] via `fillRand` (cpu.cc:24 for the timed path, cpu.cc:57 for the validation path). There is exactly ONE fill site and it is 1-D, so `size` maps directly onto the vector length with no derived counts (no nnz, no side length, no point count). Output is elementwise-compared to the oracle.
benchmarks.min_size: 0 — no floor. The inclusive scan of an empty sequence is the empty sequence, and the oracle (`std::inclusive_scan` over `[begin, end)`) is well-defined on an empty range. The spec validator accepts `size >= 0` (specs.py:291) and the configured static base already ships size 0 (config.yaml:562, `static_base_sizes: [0, 1, 2, 7]`). Caveat established by execution, not assumption: at size 0 validate() compares two EMPTY vectors and therefore passes every candidate — see degenerate_cases; size 0 is valid but carries zero discriminating power.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — FORCED BY HARNESS. `stages.enhanced_tests.max_spec_size: 4096` (thesis/config/config.yaml:572), enforced in `validate_spec` (thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294: "size %s exceeds max_spec_size %s"). Not an operation limit: the operation itself supports far larger n (measured up to 1e8). Second, independent ceiling if that cap is ever raised: the ABSOLUTE 1e-6 tolerance, which a correct blocked parallel scan violates from n ~ 2.6e7 under the ascending/descending ramp patterns (measured), and from n ~ 4.2e6 at sizes near 2^22..2^25 (measured).
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE at the operation level. A prefix sum has no power-of-two requirement, no minimum element count, no ordering/uniqueness/structural precondition, no matrix validity condition. Any real-valued sequence of any length is in the domain. The only binding conditions are harness- and comparator-level: (1) `max_spec_size: 4096` (config.yaml:572, enforced specs.py:293-294) hard-rejects any spec size > 4096; (2) the driver compares with an ABSOLUTE epsilon 1e-6 (cpu.cc:70, predicate `std::abs(x-y) > epsilon` at utilities.hpp:409-416) against prefix sums whose magnitude GROWS with n and with the fill pattern's DC bias — this, not the runtime budget, is the real ceiling on n (measured below).
benchmarks.size_semantics: Element count of the single input vector x (and of the identically-sized output). `TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(2048)` at cpu.cc:47 sizes all three validation vectors directly (`std::vector<double> correct(TEST_SIZE), test(TEST_SIZE), input(TEST_SIZE);`, cpu.cc:49). Not a side length, not an nnz seed, nothing derived. Memory cost of a spec of size n inside validate() is exactly 3*n*8 bytes = 24 B/element (plus whatever the candidate allocates).
benchmarks.complexity: O(n) time — one floating-point addition and one store per element, with a strict serial dependency chain in the oracle. O(1) auxiliary space. Memory traffic 16 B per element (8 read + 8 write), so the operation is memory-bandwidth-bound once the working set leaves cache. Measured serial oracle throughput in the pipeline container: ~2.7e8 to 3.4e8 elements/s (0.035 s at n=8.4e6; 0.073 s at n=2.0e7; 0.371 s at n=1.0e8).
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
The operation has no structural preconditions, so the scale axis is driven purely by (a) the O(n) bandwidth-bound cost model, (b) the only structural degree of freedom a scan length possesses — how it splits across workers — and (c) the harness cap of 4096.

Because the cap forces the entire usable ladder into [0, 4096], the three points are chosen to step through the regimes that actually exist there, measured against the container CPU (i7-12700H: L1d 48 KiB/core, L2 1.25 MiB/core, L3 24 MiB) and the enhanced stage's fixed parallel launch width (omp_threads 4 / mpi_ranks 4, config.yaml `enhanced_launch`):

- SMALL = 17: just above 4x the launch width. Splitting 17 across 4 workers gives 5/4/4/4 — every worker receives >= 2 elements, so both halves of a blocked scan (the chunk-local scan AND the offset add) are exercised on every worker, while no worker is empty. 272 B working set. Prime, so the split is ragged for EVERY worker count > 1.
- MEDIUM = 1021: 16 KB working set, entirely L1d-resident (48 KiB), the latency-bound regime where the serial dependency chain dominates. Prime.
- LARGE = 4093: 65 KB working set — the first point that OVERFLOWS L1d and spills to L2, i.e. a genuine regime change rather than just a bigger number. It is also the largest prime <= max_spec_size, so it simultaneously exercises the harness cap boundary and guarantees a ragged split for every worker count.

Primes throughout are not decoration: a scan's tail chunk is the only place an off-by-one can hide, and a prime length makes the tail ragged for every decomposition, at every scale point. The three are not shared with another benchmark by convenience — they follow from THIS benchmark's 16 B/element traffic and from its 1-D `size`-equals-length mapping.

Had the cap not existed, the operation-derived ladder would be 1001 / 1,000,001 / 20,000,001 (L1-resident / past-L3 streaming / deep DRAM). That LARGE is bounded by memory (480 MB for validate's three vectors; measured OOM-kill region above ~1e8 elements in a 7.8 GB container with ~3.2 GB free) and by the absolute 1e-6 tolerance (measured drift 2.3e-8 under the driver's own random fill = 43x headroom; 1.8e-7 under the ascending ramp = 5.6x headroom; ramp drift crosses 1e-6 at n ~ 2.6e7). It is NOT bounded by the 10 s runtime budget, which is unreachable here.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no. The prompt is already unambiguous and matches the oracle exactly. Its worked example pins INCLUSIVE semantics beyond doubt — input [1, 7, 4, 6, 6, 2] -> output [1, 8, 12, 18, 24, 26], where output[0] = x[0] — and the oracle is `std::inclusive_scan` (baseline.hpp:13). The serial/omp/mpi variants differ only in the parallelism instruction; the mpi variant additionally pins the data placement ("Every rank has a complete copy of x. Store the result in output on rank 0."), which is exactly what the driver does (BCAST at cpu.cc:58, root-only compare at cpu.cc:70). No domain restriction is needed: the operation accepts every real-valued sequence of every length. Explicitly NOT recommended: a prompt sentence cannot fix the floating-point hazard described below, because no wording makes a parallel scan bit-reproduce a sequential one — that is a comparator decision, not a prompt decision.
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: no — the input is a single flat `std::vector<double>` of exactly `size` elements filled at one 1-D `ENHANCED_FILL` site (cpu.cc:57), with no derived counts, no structural preconditions and no auxiliary arrays; the generic pattern library in enhanced-fill.hpp covers this benchmark completely.

benchmarks.evidence_gap: One sub-finding is measured but UNEXPLAINED, and I did not fabricate a mechanism for it: the ascending/descending ramp drift is smooth and ~linear in n at round decimal sizes (5.2e-8 at 2e6 -> 1.19e-6 at 3e7, i.e. a few ULPs of the peak |S_i| = 25n), but blows up by 3-4 orders of magnitude at sizes near powers of two (6.94e-4 at n = 16,777,216; 3.28e-4 at 16,777,215; 2.53e-6 at 4,194,304) while dropping to EXACTLY 0 at n = 2^k + 1 (4,194,305 and 16,777,217, where the ramp step 200/(n-1) is exactly representable and every partial sum is exact). The exact-at-2^k+1 case is explained; the blow-up immediately adjacent to it is not. This does not affect the reported row — all three chosen sizes are far below the affected region and measured clean — but it means no simple monotone size cap can be claimed to make the ramp patterns safe at large n.
benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
All established by EXECUTING the driver's own validate() logic (oracle + `reportAndCompare(correct, test, 1e-6)`), not by reasoning.

DEFINED and non-discriminating:
- size 0 — empty scan of the empty sequence. Mathematically defined; the oracle writes nothing. Executed: validate() compares two empty vectors, so an identical candidate, an EXCLUSIVE-scan candidate and a skip-index-0 candidate ALL pass. Valid input, zero information. Already in `static_base_sizes`.
- all_zeros (pattern 1) and all_same (pattern 2) at the call-site range: all_same's midpoint of [-100, 100] is exactly 0.0, so BOTH patterns produce an all-zero input and an all-zero prefix sum (measured max|S_i| = 0.000e+00 at every size). Neither can distinguish inclusive from exclusive from reversed accumulation. Non-discriminating unless the spec overrides ENHANCED_FILL_RANGE_LO/HI.

DEFINED and high-value:
- size 1 — output[0] = x[0]. Executed: catches BOTH the exclusive-scan misreading and the "loop starts at i=1, output[0] left 0" bug. The single most discriminating degenerate size for this benchmark.
- size 2 — first size at which the dependency actually chains. Executed: both bug classes caught.
- alternating (pattern 5, -100/+100): prefix sums cycle -100, 0, -100, 0 (measured max|S_i| = 1.000e+02, drift 0). Discriminates inclusive vs exclusive; insensitive to reassociation.

DEFINED and, unusually for this suite, SAFE here:
- extreme_values (pattern 6): the reference stays FINITE at every size measured (17, 1021, 4093, 1e6+1, 2e7+1: nonfin_ref = 0 everywhere), because DBL_lowest + DBL_max = 0 exactly and the pattern alternates. Blocked-scan drift measured EXACTLY 0 for chunk counts P in {2,3,7,16,20,64,257,1024}. So the non-finite-reference hazard that the audit records for the reduce/geometry/sparse_la families does NOT fire for prefix sum.
- spike_at(k) (pattern 9, x[k] = DBL_MAX/2): reference finite; measured drift 0 to 2.7e-8 across all P at n = 2e7. Passes. Note however that after index k the prefix sums sit at ~9e307 where one ULP is ~2e292, so the 1e-6 ABSOLUTE tolerance is ~1e298 ULPs tighter than one ULP — past the spike the comparison is effectively an exact-bit-equality test, not a tolerance test. It happened to hold at every size and P measured, but it is testing something other than what the epsilon suggests.

Note: enhancedFillPattern returns early for n == 0 (enhanced-fill.hpp), and the k-patterns (7/8/9) are rejected below size 2 by specs.py:322 — so no degenerate size can produce a malformed input.

Nothing else is inside the timer — input generation, the `std::fill` of the output and the result-liveness check are all outside it.

Repetitions: 3 per size, median reported (LARGE = 20,000,001 additionally repeated as four independent 3-rep runs to separate host noise from signal).

Full timing ladder (median of 3, seconds): 17 -> below single-call clock resolution (<1e-6, reported as 0.000000); 1021 -> 0.000001; 2048 (driver default) -> 0.000004; 4093 -> 0.000004; 4096 -> 0.000007; 65,536 -> 0.000155; 1,000,001 -> 0.002773; 1,048,576 -> 0.002185; 8,388,608 (= DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE) -> 0.035151; 16,777,216 -> 0.098371; 20,000,001 -> 0.073; 33,554,432 -> 0.117027; 50,000,000 -> 0.132903 (1 rep); 100,000,000 -> 0.370943 (1 rep).

LARGE adjustment made to meet the budget: NONE, and the 10 s budget was never the binding constraint. At the measured ~2.7e8 elements/s a 10 s serial scan would need ~2.7e9 elements = ~22 GB for the input vector alone, versus 7.8 GB of container RAM; a 3-rep run at 6.7e7 elements was already OOM-killed (exit 137) during the sweep. The budget is therefore unreachable for this benchmark rather than inappropriate, and I did not silently substitute a different budget — I report the actual binding constraints instead: the harness cap (4096) for the operative row, and memory + the absolute 1e-6 tolerance (~2e7) for the uncapped variant.

Second measurement, numerical headroom (this is what actually bounds LARGE, so it was measured rather than assumed): a separate harness compares the oracle against the canonical blocked two-pass scan (P chunks: chunk-local inclusive scan, exclusive scan of chunk totals, offset add). This decomposition comes from the operation's parallel definition as stated in the omp/mpi prompts, NOT from any observed candidate — no candidate or model output was read for this row. Reported as max |oracle - blocked| against the driver's 1e-6.
  - At the chosen sizes, all ten implemented fill patterns, P = 20: worst drift 0.0 (n=17), 7.3e-12 (n=1021), 8.7e-11 (n=4093). At least 11,000x headroom.
  - Driver default random fill: 3.9e-12 (n=1001), 1.3e-9 (n=1e6+1), 2.3e-8 (n=2e7+1), 3.6e-8 (n=3.36e7) — smooth and safe (the prefix sums are a mean-zero random walk, so |S_i| only grows as sqrt(n)).
  - Robustness of the uncapped LARGE: at n = 20,000,001, drift re-measured for P in {2, 3, 7, 16, 20, 64, 257, 1024}; worst across ALL patterns and ALL P = 2.4e-7 (ascending), random fill 1.3e-8 to 3.1e-8. Not a single-P coincidence.

benchmarks.name: 31_scan_scan_with_min_function
benchmarks.input_form: One dense 1-D `std::vector<float> x` of length N, transformed IN PLACE (signature `void partialMinimums(std::vector<float> &x)`). Exactly one dimension: N = element count. No second array, no index array, no structural precondition. Values: uniform i.i.d. in [-100.0, 100.0] at both generator sites (perf path cpu.cc:27, validation path cpu.cc:59), drawn from unseeded `rand()` (utilities.hpp:144-159). Output must be the inclusive prefix minimum written back into x. MPI variant additionally: every rank starts with a full copy of x, the result is only required (and only checked) on rank 0.
benchmarks.min_size: 0 — there is NO mathematical size floor. The inclusive prefix minimum is a total operation on sequences of every length: N=0 is the empty transformation, N=1 is the identity. Verified by execution: the oracle returns cleanly on N=0 and N=1 (semantics probe, see measurement_detail). The driver imposes no floor either (cpu.cc:49-51 simply sizes three vectors to TEST_SIZE; enhanced-fill.hpp:177-179 returns early on n==0). Sizes 0/1/2 are therefore degenerate_cases, not a floor.
benchmarks.max_size: Not forced by the operation. Two harness-side ceilings, both far above LARGE: (1) HARD: `fillRand` iterates with an `int` counter — `for (int i = 0; i < x.size(); i += 1)` (utilities.hpp:146) — so any TEST_SIZE >= 2^31 breaks the input generator itself (signed overflow / UB) before the oracle ever runs. (2) BINDING IN PRACTICE: validate()'s 12*N-byte footprint (three TEST_SIZE float vectors, cpu.cc:51) against a measured container of 7775 MiB total / ~6.4 GiB free, i.e. ~2^28 as an absolute practical ceiling and much less under concurrent runs. A 2^28 attempt was started and did NOT complete (see measurement_detail) — I therefore report no number for it.
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE. No power-of-two requirement, no minimum element count, no sortedness, no positivity, no distinctness, no matrix/point-set validity. Every N >= 0 and every finite float vector is in domain. The ONE constraint is not a size condition but a VALUE-RANGE condition, and it is discovered from the oracle, not from the prompt: `correctPartialMinimums` seeds `std::inclusive_scan` with `std::numeric_limits<float>::max()` (baseline.hpp:18-20), so any input element that is +Inf (or NaN) is CLAMPED/ABSORBED by the sentinel and the oracle diverges from the plain running minimum. MEASURED: input [+Inf, 5, +Inf] -> oracle [3.40282e+38, 5, 5], naive running min [+Inf, 5, 5]; input [NaN, 5, -1] -> oracle [3.40282e+38, 5, -1], naive [NaN, NaN?/5, -1]. Consequence for the enhanced stage: enhanced specs for this benchmark must stay inside the FINITE float range. The stock patterns are safe (extreme_values gives FLT_LOWEST/FLT_MAX, spike_at gives FLT_MAX/2 — both measured to agree with the naive running min), but `explicit_values` (pattern 10) and any ENHANCED_FILL_LO/HI override pass doubles through `enhancedFromDouble<float>` (enhanced-fill.hpp:164-171), so a magnitude above ~3.4e38 silently becomes +Inf and creates an oracle/candidate divergence that is an artefact of the sentinel, not of the operation.
benchmarks.size_semantics: The size number is the ELEMENT COUNT N of the single float vector. Nothing is derived from it (no nnz, no side length, no point count). It maps 1:1 onto the validation size: `const size_t TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)` (cpu.cc:49), and ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(n) is `(ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE)` when the define is present (enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79). validate() allocates THREE vectors of TEST_SIZE floats (input, correct, test — cpu.cc:51), so the memory footprint of a size point is 12*N bytes. The separate perf-path size is DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE (cpu.cc:34), configured as serial 1<<22, omp/mpi/mpi+omp 1<<20, kokkos/cuda/hip 1<<22 (drivers/problem-sizes.json:281-289) — context only, it does not constrain the enhanced sizes.
benchmarks.complexity: Oracle: O(N) time, O(1) extra space — exactly max(N-1, 0) pairwise `std::min` applications plus one fold against the FLT_MAX init, one read and one write per element, no branches whose count depends on the data, no accumulation (min is an exact selection, so there is zero floating-point error growth with N). The operation is memory-bandwidth-bound: MEASURED throughput 2.6e8 elem/s at N=2^24 (64 MiB) and 2.2e8 elem/s at N=2^26 (256 MiB) versus effectively unbounded throughput while L1-resident, i.e. flat O(N) with a cache-hierarchy step, no super-linear term anywhere.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
SCALE AXIS, derived from the operation and its complexity only — no candidate code was read, and no size was chosen because some implementation switches strategy there.

The operation is an O(N) in-place inclusive scan under a min combiner: one read + one write per element, no data-dependent branch count, and — because min is an exact selection — no floating-point error growth with N. So the only thing size can vary is (a) where the working set sits in the memory hierarchy and (b) how a blocked/parallel decomposition of the scan partitions N. The three points target exactly those.

SMALL = 127. Prime, therefore no power-of-two block count and no SIMD width (4/8/16) divides it: every blocked decomposition of a scan — the standard local-scan / block-offset / re-apply structure — is forced to produce an uneven remainder block, which is where the boundary and offset bugs of a scan live. 508 B, trivially L1-resident, so the memory hierarchy contributes nothing and only the algorithmic structure is under test. Still clearly above the degenerate regime (0/1/2, which are the config's static base sizes and are handled on the degenerate axis), and small enough that the MISMATCH_REPORT_MAX=3 dump with the input values printed is humanly interpretable. Measured: 5 distinct prefix-min values, i.e. the output still has real structure.

MEDIUM = 262,144 = 2^18. 1 MiB per vector, 3 MiB for validate()'s three vectors: past a typical 1-2 MiB L2, still LLC-resident. N is now vastly larger than any thread count, so every block of a blocked scan is large and the block-offset combine step is exercised in its normal regime rather than its edge case. Measured 0.544 ms — three orders of magnitude above SMALL, one below LARGE, so the three points really are three regimes and not decoration.

LARGE = 16,777,216 = 2^24. 64 MiB per vector, ~192 MiB for validate(): far beyond any LLC, so the operation runs in the DRAM-streaming regime where its bandwidth bound is real (measured 2.6e8 elem/s versus effectively free while cache-resident). It is deliberately 4x the serial DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE (1<<22, problem-sizes.json:282), so the enhanced stage probes strictly beyond the size the performance driver already exercises — the held-out property. Measured 0.063 s, comfortably inside the 10 s budget with the memory ceiling (not the clock) as the real outer bound.

WHY NOT LARGER, stated as an operation property rather than convenience: for the prefix minimum under any i.i.d. fill, the number of positions at which the answer changes is the number of left-to-right minima, expected H_N ~ ln N. MEASURED on the driver's own fillRand: 12 distinct values at N=2^18 and only 18 at N=2^24 — 0.00011% of indices. Beyond a few thousand elements the correct output is a single constant almost everywhere, so growing N adds essentially ZERO discriminating information under a random fill while multiplying memory and wall time by 4 per doubling across MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS x patterns x samples. The discriminating axis for this benchmark is the FILL PATTERN, not N: descending makes every index a new record (maximal discrimination), ascending collapses the output to the constant x[0], alternating and sorted_except_one(k) place records at controlled positions, all_same removes them entirely. A domain table row for 31 that only moved N would be nearly powerless; the three sizes are the scale axis, and the pattern axis is where the correctness signal is.

DOMAIN (not size): N >= 0 with no further precondition; values finite floats. The only genuine domain restriction found is the oracle's FLT_MAX init sentinel absorbing +Inf/NaN (see special_conditions) — an oracle artefact that must be kept out of the specs' value ranges, not a property of the operation.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no — the prompt is unambiguous over the entire finite-float domain. It states the operation ("Replace the i-th element of the vector x with the minimum value from indices 0 through i"), gives two worked examples, and both were executed against the real oracle and match exactly ([8,6,-1,7,3,4,4] -> [8,6,-1,-1,-1,-1,-1]; [5,4,6,4,3,6,1,1] -> [5,4,4,4,3,3,1,1]). There is no empty-input return value to pin (the function is in-place and returns void), no tie-break convention (values, not indices), no accumulation convention. The single divergence (+Inf/NaN absorbed by the oracle's FLT_MAX init) is an oracle artefact and must be handled by restricting SPEC value ranges to the finite float range, not by adding a sentence to the prompt. If the spec generator is ever allowed to emit |value| > 3.4e38 for this benchmark, the honest fix is still spec-side; only if that is refused would the prompt need: "All elements of x are finite."
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: no — the input is a single flat float vector with no derived counts, no structural validity requirement and no second container, so the stock fillRand / ENHANCED_FILL path (cpu.cc:59) covers it and every pattern id 0-10 is applicable; the only spec-side constraint is the finite-float value range (see special_conditions), which is a range restriction, not a construction.
