benchmarks.name: 48_sparse_la_sparse_axpy
benchmarks.input_form: z = alpha*x + y, sparse-into-dense AXPY. Inputs: (a) scalar `double alpha` drawn uniform in [-1,1]; (b) `std::vector<Element> x` and `y` with `Element{size_t index; double value;}`, each of length nnz = floor(N * SPARSE_LA_SPARSITY) = floor(0.1*N), SORTED ascending by `index`, indices drawn uniformly WITH REPLACEMENT from [0,N) (duplicates always present), values uniform in [-1,1]; (c) `std::vector<double> z` DENSE of length exactly N, pre-zeroed. Relevant dimensions: N (dense index space = length of z) and nnz per sparse vector, which is NOT free — it is rigidly derived as floor(0.1*N). Output compared: the dense vector z (length N), elementwise, absolute tolerance 1e-4.
benchmarks.min_size: Mathematically the operation is defined for every N >= 0. For the SCALE axis the floor is N >= 10: below that nVals = floor(0.1*N) = 0, so both sparse vectors are EMPTY and the test is vacuous (z stays the zero vector and any candidate that touches nothing passes). N = 10 is the smallest N with exactly one entry per sparse vector. No power-of-two, divisibility, or other structural minimum exists.
benchmarks.max_size: No hard maximum from the operation. Practical ceiling from the harness/host, in this order: (1) memory — validate() allocates ~22.4*N bytes (two dense vectors of N doubles + Element/staging arrays), so N = 2^28 already needs ~6 GB and exceeds the container's 7 GB; (2) the index generator — fillRand for integral types is `rand() % N` and glibc rand() returns values in [0, 2^31-1], so for N > 2^31 the upper part of the index space can never be addressed (the input silently stops being uniform over [0,N)); (3) cpu.cc:111 uses an `int` loop counter over xIndices.size(), which overflows once nVals = 0.1*N exceeds 2^31, i.e. N > ~2.1e10. Only (1) binds in practice.
benchmarks.special_conditions: (1) SORTEDNESS (hard oracle precondition): x and y must be sorted ascending by `index` — the oracle is a two-pointer merge (baseline.hpp:18-30) and silently produces a wrong answer on unsorted input. The driver always sorts (cpu.cc:52-53, 115-116). The PROMPT never states this. (2) INDEX RANGE (hard, memory-safety): every index must satisfy index < N — the oracle writes `z[...]` unchecked at baseline.hpp:20,23,26,33,38 and z is never resized. index >= N is an out-of-bounds heap write inside the ORACLE. (3) z must have length exactly N and be zero-initialised: the oracle ACCUMULATES with `+=`, it does not assign or resize (cpu.cc:118-119 zero it). (4) nnz is not an independent knob: nVals = floor(0.1*N), with SPARSE_LA_SPARSITY = 0.1 (utilities.hpp:31). (5) Duplicate indices are ALWAYS present by construction (uniform draw with replacement) and the oracle commits to the COO "duplicates are summed" convention — see pending_fix. (6) No power-of-two, no rank-divisibility requirement (the MPI prompt gives every rank a full copy of x and y).
benchmarks.size_semantics: The size number is N = TEST_SIZE = the length of the DENSE output vector z, i.e. the size of the index space. It is NOT an element count of the sparse operands: nnz per sparse vector is DERIVED as nVals = floor(N * SPARSE_LA_SPARSITY) = floor(0.1*N) (cpu.cc:86, cpu.cc:62). So a spec size of N means: two sorted sparse vectors of floor(0.1*N) entries each, scattered into a dense array of N doubles. Total oracle work is Theta(0.2*N) scattered read-modify-writes into an 8*N-byte array.
benchmarks.complexity: Oracle correctSparseAxpy: Theta(|x| + |y|) time — one two-pointer merge pass, each step a scattered read-modify-write into the dense z. Under the driver's fixed tie |x| = |y| = floor(0.1*N) this is Theta(N) with a small constant; memory behaviour is a random scatter over an 8*N-byte array (DRAM-bound once 8*N exceeds the LLC). Space Theta(N) for z plus Theta(0.1*N) for the operands. Untimed driver overhead per validation attempt is Theta(N) (zeroing the two dense vectors) plus Theta(nnz log nnz) (the two sorts) and in practice DOMINATES the oracle by ~20x at LARGE.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
Derived only from the operation, its specified input distribution, its complexity and the budget — no candidate code was consulted.

min_size = 10 (scale axis): nnz = floor(0.1*N) reaches 1 only at N = 10. For N < 10 both operands are empty; that is a valid but vacuous input and belongs on the degenerate axis, not the scale axis. (The existing enhanced spec set for this benchmark is entirely in that vacuous range — all 20 specs have size <= 8 per the oracle audit — which is exactly the failure this row is meant to prevent.)

The operation has exactly two things that scale: the merge work (0.2*N steps) and the scatter target (an 8*N-byte dense array). Both are pinned to N, so the three points are chosen to place the dense output z in three qualitatively different levels of the memory hierarchy, with a secondary requirement on duplicate-index density (duplicates are the semantic core of this benchmark — the oracle sums them, and they are what makes a naive parallel scatter race).

Expected number of colliding index pairs inside one operand is C(nnz,2)/N ~ nnz^2/(2N) = 0.005*N — a property of the SPECIFIED generator (uniform draw with replacement from [0,N)), not of any candidate.

SMALL = 2048: the two requirements are (a) the whole working set in L1D, and (b) duplicates actually present. Working set is ~22.4*N bytes (16N for the two dense vectors + 3.2N for the Element arrays + 3.2N for the staging arrays); 22.4*2048 = 46 KB, of which the two dense vectors are 32 KB — L1/L2-resident, no DRAM effects, so this point tests merge logic (both tails, the equal-index branch) in isolation. Duplicate pairs expected = 0.005*2048 ~ 10, and nnz = 204 gives a rich interleaving of the two index sets. N = 2000 is the smallest N meeting (b); 2048 is the nearest power of two, chosen only so z lands on an exact cache-line/page multiple.

MEDIUM = 2^20: z = 8 MB, i.e. straddling the last-level cache of typical hardware (8-32 MB). This is the transition regime: the merge stream is still cheap but the scatter starts missing. nnz ~ 105k, ~5.2k expected duplicate collisions.

LARGE = 2^24: the smallest power of two whose dense output is unambiguously beyond ANY plausible LLC — z = 128 MB, 2x-16x larger than an 8-64 MB L3, so every scatter is a DRAM access and the operation is in its true memory-bound regime. 2^23 (z = 64 MB) is not safe: some server parts have a 64 MB+ L3 and the point would degenerate back into MEDIUM. nnz = 1.68M forces any parallel scheme to genuinely partition work; ~84k expected duplicate collisions make a racy scatter-add fail with near-certainty rather than by luck. Measured oracle cost 0.074 s = 0.7% of the 10 s budget; validate() peak RSS ~370 MB, which is the real ceiling on this benchmark's LARGE (see budget_adjustment).

Powers of two are a convenience of cache-boundary placement here, NOT a requirement of the operation — any N >= 10 is a legal size.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no — for the SIZE/SCALE domain. The size is invisible to the model (it is a compile define in the driver), every N >= 10 is a legal input, and no structural restriction (power of two, divisibility, minimum count) exists that a model would have to be told about. Two separate, NON-size prompt questions exist and are recorded elsewhere: (a) BL-15 option 1 would add the sentence "Indices may repeat; entries with the same index are summed." to all three entries (serial/omp/mpi) — that decision is open and is not this row's to make; (b) the prompt never states that x and y arrive sorted by index, although the oracle requires it and the driver always guarantees it. (b) needs no prompt change for validity (a sortedness-agnostic implementation is also correct), but it does mean any custom input construction MUST preserve sortedness.
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: yes — for three independent reasons. (1) SAFETY: the enhanced fill library applies ONE pattern to all four fill sites (two index sites + two value sites, benchmark_shapes.json: fill_sites = 4), and three of the offered patterns put indices outside [0,N) — measured: alternating(5) -> index == N, extreme_values(6) -> SIZE_MAX, spike_at(9) -> SIZE_MAX/2 — which makes the ORACLE write out of bounds. Spec generation for this benchmark must be restricted to {random, all_zeros, all_same, ascending, descending, duplicate_at, sorted_except_one}, and the mutation table (specs.py: "random"->"extreme_values", "alternating"->"extreme_values") must be blocked here too. ENHANCED_FILL_LO/HI overrides are likewise unsafe, since one range is applied to both the index sites and the value sites. (2) EXPRESSIVENESS: nnz is welded to floor(0.1*N), so the interesting structural cases — disjoint index sets, identical index sets, nnz = 1, a genuinely duplicate-free (well-formed) sparse vector — cannot be expressed by size + pattern at all. (3) The surgical escape hatch is closed: explicit_values is already disabled for this benchmark (4 fill sites, ambiguous value-to-vector mapping). Minimum contract for any custom construction: indices in [0,N), both operands sorted ascending, z of length exactly N and zeroed.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Mathematically DEFINED degenerate inputs for this operation (all verified not to crash the oracle, measured at N = 0,1,2,9,10,11):
- N = 0: x, y and z all empty; the oracle's three loops never execute; result is the empty vector. Defined, but reportAndCompare on two empty vectors returns true -> a vacuous PASS.
- N = 1..9: nVals = floor(0.1*N) = 0, so both operands are EMPTY while z has length N; result is the zero vector of length N. Defined, and again vacuous (a candidate that does nothing passes). This is where all 20 currently existing enhanced specs for this benchmark sit.
- N = 10: exactly one entry per operand — the minimal non-vacuous case; exercises either the equal-index branch or one strict-inequality branch plus one tail loop, in isolation.
- alpha = 0: z = scatter(y) only. Defined; isolates the y path.
- alpha = 1 (the prompt's own example): plain sparse merge.
- All values zero, or all values identical: z = 0 resp. a scaled indicator; defined.
- ALL INDICES IDENTICAL (fill pattern all_zeros -> every index 0; all_same -> every index N/2): every entry collides, z has a single nonzero equal to alpha*sum(x.value) + sum(y.value). Defined, in-range, and the sharpest available probe of the duplicate-summation convention (BL-15).
- Disjoint index sets (x and y share no index): exercises only the two strict-inequality branches and both tails; defined.
- Identical index sets: exercises only the equal-index branch; defined.
NOT degenerate but OUT OF DOMAIN (must never be generated): any index >= N. Measured: the generic fill patterns alternating(5), extreme_values(6) and spike_at(9) all produce such indices at the two index fill sites (at N=1024, nVals=102: pattern 5 -> 51 indices equal to exactly N; pattern 6 -> 51 indices = SIZE_MAX; pattern 9 -> 1 index = SIZE_MAX/2), which makes the ORACLE ITSELF perform an out-of-bounds heap write. explicit_values(10) would be equally unsafe but is already disabled for this benchmark in thesis/enhanced_tests/benchmark_shapes.json.
benchmarks.pending_fix:
YES — this row is PROVISIONAL. Two open items:

(1) BL-15 (class B blocker, thesis/docs/oracle-correctness-audit.md:403-...): the duplicate-index convention is undecided. The prompt says "sparse vectors" and shows unique indices; the driver always feeds duplicates; the oracle silently commits to COO summation (`z[...] +=`). The audit leaves three options open: option 1 = add a clarifying prompt sentence; option 2 = make the driver generate duplicate-free indices; option 3 = accept and document. IMPACT ON THIS ROW: under option 2 the collision statistic 0.005*N that co-justifies SMALL = 2048 disappears (nnz would drop below floor(0.1*N) after dedup), and SMALL would then rest on the cache-footprint argument alone — the three sizes themselves survive, but the SMALL justification must be re-stated. Options 1 and 3 leave this row unchanged.

(2) The existing enhanced spec set for this benchmark is vacuous (all 20 specs at size <= 8, where nVals = 0) and must be regenerated with sizes >= 10; this row supplies those sizes. That regeneration must simultaneously drop the index-unsafe fill patterns (5/6/9) — see custom_input_construction_needed.

benchmarks.name: 49_sparse_la_sparse_lu_decomp
benchmarks.input_form: A = unordered list of COO triples {size_t row, size_t column, double value} describing an N x N matrix; outputs L and U are DENSE N x N row-major double buffers of length N*N (L unit lower triangular, U upper triangular). Relevant dimensions: (a) N = side length of the square matrix — the single spec "size"; (b) nnz = number of triples, currently DERIVED as nnz = floor(SPARSE_LA_SPARSITY * N * N) = floor(0.1*N^2) (cpu.cc:100, utilities.hpp:29-32), indices drawn independently in [0, N-1] (cpu.cc:114-115), values in [-10,10] (cpu.cc:116). The oracle immediately densifies A into an N x N buffer (baseline.hpp:18-21), so nnz influences only which cells are non-zero, never the cost.
benchmarks.min_size: No size floor follows from the operation. N = 0 is defined (empty factorization; MEASURED: oracle produces nothing, comparator trivially passes) and N = 1 is defined for EVERY A (MEASURED: L=[1], U=[a00]; the division branch requires i>j and can never execute). The binding precondition is a FORM condition, not a size condition: A must admit an unpivoted LU, i.e. every leading principal minor of order 1..N-1 must be non-zero (baseline.hpp:33,35 divide by U[j*N+j] with no pivot search and no zero-pivot guard). Practical floor for a NON-VACUOUS scale point: N >= 4, because the current generator yields nVals = floor(0.1*N^2) = 0 for N <= 3 (MEASURED), i.e. the empty COO list = the zero matrix, which is out of domain for N >= 2.
benchmarks.max_size: 1024 under the 10 s oracle budget on this host — measured, not imposed by the harness (N=1280 -> 6.38 s still fits but offers no headroom, N=1536 -> 21.5 s and N=2048 -> 64.4 s both blow it). Memory is not the limit (24*N^2 bytes = 25 MB at N=1024, 100 MB at N=2048). No cap from drivers/problem-sizes.json, which only fixes the TIMING size (1<<9 = 512) and does not constrain the validate/enhanced size.
benchmarks.special_conditions: (1) DOMAIN (hard): all leading principal minors of orders 1..N-1 non-zero — otherwise the oracle divides by an exact zero and emits Inf/NaN. A itself may be singular (only minors up to N-1 are used as divisors); MEASURED: N=2 all-same c gives the valid factorization L=[[1,0],[1,1]], U=[[c,c],[0,0]] although A is rank 1. (2) The random-COO generator violates (1) essentially always: MEASURED 4032 of 8192 output entries non-finite at N=64, 1047552 of 2097152 at N=1024 — matching audit finding BL-16. (3) OUTPUT FORM: dense N x N row-major, unit diagonal in L, zeros outside each triangle — stated only in baseline.hpp:11, NOT in any of the three prompt entries, whose worked example prints L and U as COO triple lists. (4) DUPLICATE COO COORDINATES: overwrite, last entry in array order wins (baseline.hpp:20 uses `=`); MEASURED reproduction of BL-20: A={(0,0,2),(0,1,4),(1,0,1),(1,1,5),(1,1,-2)} -> L=[1,0,0.5,1], U=[2,4,0,-4], i.e. A[1][1] = -2. Family-inconsistent (46/47/48 sum). (5) No power-of-two or parity requirement. (6) Comparison epsilon 1e-3 on BOTH L and U (cpu.cc:140), MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS = 2 trials (cpu.cc:111, utilities.hpp:25-27) — so the oracle runs TWICE per validate().
benchmarks.size_semantics: The spec "size" is N, the SIDE LENGTH of the square matrix, not an element count. It is the value substituted for TEST_SIZE by -DENHANCED_TEST_SIZE (enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79, cpu.cc:99). Everything else is derived from it inside validate(): the three fill sites each have length nVals = floor(SPARSE_LA_SPARSITY * N * N) = floor(0.1*N^2) (cpu.cc:100), the index range is [0, N-1] (cpu.cc:114-115), and both result buffers have N*N doubles (cpu.cc:105-106). Consequence to keep in mind: nnz is quadratic in the size number, so doubling the spec size quadruples the number of triples and octuples the oracle's work; and for N <= 3 the truncation makes nVals exactly 0 (MEASURED), i.e. the input degenerates to the zero matrix. Under the proposed banded construction nnz would instead be N*(2k+1) - k*(k+1), linear in N (measured 124 at N=16, 1132 at N=128, 9196 at N=1024 for k=4).
benchmarks.small: N = 16 (matrix 16x16; working set 3*N^2 doubles = 6.1 KB, fully L1-resident). MEASURED oracle median 0.000008 s (3 reps, in-domain banded input).
benchmarks.medium: N = 128 (working set 393 KB, L2/L3 regime; the strided U[k*N+j] access with stride 1 KB starts to dominate). MEASURED oracle median 0.003830 s (3 reps, in-domain banded input).
benchmarks.large: N = 1024 (working set 25 MB, out of last-level cache, memory-bound). MEASURED oracle median 5.914901 s (3 reps, in-domain banded input) — within the 10 s budget.
benchmarks.complexity: Oracle: Theta(N^3) time, Theta(N^2) memory, INDEPENDENT of nnz. Exactly: densification O(nnz) + O(N^2) zero-init (baseline.hpp:18-21), then the triple loop (baseline.hpp:24-38) executes ~N^3/6 inner iterations in the U branch and ~N^3/6 in the L branch, i.e. ~N^3/3 total. Note the L branch performs a floating-point DIVISION by U[j*N+j] INSIDE the k-loop (baseline.hpp:35), so ~N^3/6 divisions — this oracle is measurably more expensive than a textbook Doolittle that hoists the division. Memory: fullA + L + U = 3*N^2 doubles = 24*N^2 bytes. The "sparse" character costs nothing and buys nothing.
benchmarks.domain_rationale: The operation is an unpivoted Doolittle LU with DENSE cost Theta(N^3) and a Theta(N^2) working set, so the only meaningful scale axis is N, and the only regimes that differ qualitatively are the levels of the memory hierarchy the working set 24*N^2 bytes lands in. The ladder is therefore anchored on that quantity, geometrically spaced by a factor 8 in N (factor 512 in nominal work): SMALL N=16 -> 6.1 KB, entirely L1-resident, so the measurement is the recurrence itself (elimination depth 16, update sums up to 15 terms, both the U-update at baseline.hpp:28-30 and the L-update at :34-36 run with many terms) and not memory; it is also >= 2k+1 for every plausible band width k <= 7, so the pending banded A = L*U construction is genuinely banded and hand-checkable there, and it is a quarter of the driver's own default validate size (64), hence a genuinely smaller regime rather than a relabelling. MEDIUM N=128 -> 393 KB, past L1/L2 into L3, where the strided access U[k*N+j] rather than the arithmetic sets the cost. LARGE N=1024 -> 25 MB, beyond any last-level cache, fully memory-bound, and the largest point of the doubling ladder that fits the 10 s oracle budget. min_size is not used as a floor: the adopted decision keeps 0 and 1 available, and both are mathematically defined here (measured), so they sit in degenerate_cases. No size is derived from any observed candidate code; the ladder follows from Theta(N^3)/Theta(N^2) plus the measured budget alone.

benchmarks.name: 50_stencil_xor_kernel
benchmarks.input_form: One square N x N grid of ints in row-major layout, passed as std::vector<int> of length N*N, plus an output grid of identical shape (cpu.cc:61). The driver's own generator fills it via fillRand(input, 0, 2), whose integral branch is rand() % (max-min) + min = rand() % 2, so the reference value domain is exactly {0,1} (utilities.hpp:143-152, cpu.cc:69). The oracle itself accepts arbitrary ints: only the exact value 1 counts as a live neighbour (baseline.hpp:22-25). Relevant dimension: a single number, the SIDE LENGTH N. Element count is N*N (thesis/enhanced_tests/benchmark_shapes.json:463, total_elements "n*n", elements_per_site ["n2"], fill_sites 1). Comparison is an exact integer != on ints - there is NO epsilon and no fequal/reportAndCompare helper involved (cpu.cc:85).
benchmarks.min_size: N >= 3 (side length). Mathematically the operation is defined for every N >= 0, but the harness forces 3: at N = 0 the driver HANGS (measured), and at N = 1 and N = 2 validation is VACUOUS - it compares zero cells and passes any candidate (measured). N = 3 is the smallest side length at which the graded window contains at least one cell.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 - forced by the harness: max_spec_size: 4096 in thesis/config/config.yaml:572, and validation rejects larger specs (thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294). NOT forced by the runtime budget: I measured N = 8192 at 3.808847 s (4-neighbour) / 5.866742 s (8-neighbour), both still inside the 10 s budget, so the config cap binds roughly 2x before the budget does.
benchmarks.special_conditions: None mathematically. N is any non-negative integer - no power-of-two, no parity, no minimum point count. The grid is square by construction (cpu.cc:61 allocates TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE for all three vectors), input.size() == output.size() == N*N, and values may be any int because the rule is a literal equality test against 1 (baseline.hpp:22-25), not a truthiness test. The one load-bearing condition is harness-side, not mathematical: validate() grades only the OPEN INTERIOR i,j in [1, N-2] (cpu.cc:83-84), so (a) the entire boundary ring is ungraded at every size, and (b) the graded window is empty unless N >= 3. Additional harness conditions: max_spec_size = 4096 caps N (thesis/config/config.yaml:572); explicit_values specs are capped on the ELEMENT count, so explicit grids are limited to N <= 8 (N*N <= 64, thesis/config/config.yaml:586, thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:343-353).
benchmarks.size_semantics: size = N = the SIDE LENGTH of the square grid, NOT the element count. ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE overrides TEST_SIZE at cpu.cc:59 (default 512), and that value is used both as the vector dimension TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:61) and as the row stride N passed to the oracle (cpu.cc:75). So a spec size of 4096 means 16,777,216 ints per grid and 192 MB across validate()'s three grids. benchmark_shapes.json:463 confirms total_elements = "n*n", which is also what drives the explicit_values element-count cap.
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(N^2) in the side length N, i.e. Theta(n) in the cell count n = N^2. Exactly 4 guarded neighbour reads and one store per cell today; exactly 8 after the pending 4-neighbour -> 8-neighbour fix. Memory Theta(N^2): the oracle touches 2 int grids, validate() holds 3 (input, correct, test) = 12*N^2 bytes. The kernel is memory-bandwidth-bound once the working set leaves the last-level cache - measured: 4096 cells in 0.000156 s vs 16.8M cells in 0.935806 s is 6,000x work for only 5,998x time at the small end but the per-cell cost rises from 38 ns/kcell to 56 ns/kcell between N = 64 and N = 4096, the DRAM-streaming signature.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
The scale axis for a 2D nearest-neighbour stencil is the side length N, and the only thing that changes with N (given that the neighbourhood is a fixed-size constant and the graded window is interior-only) is the MEMORY-HIERARCHY REGIME of the three N x N int grids validate() streams. That gives a candidate-independent three-point ladder at x8 in side length / x64 in area, anchored on the benchmark's own numbers:

SMALL = 64: 3 grids x 16 KB = 48 KB, fully L1/L2-resident. Pure indexing-correctness regime with zero memory effects; 62^2 = 3,844 interior cells are graded, far too many for a wrong neighbour set or a transposed i*N+j stride to survive by chance on a random binary grid. Comfortably above the N >= 3 floor, so it is a scale point and not a degenerate case.

MEDIUM = 512: the driver's OWN shipped TEST_SIZE (cpu.cc:59), so medium reproduces exactly the validation scale the un-enhanced suite already uses - a deliberate anchor, not a convenience number. 3 grids x 1 MB = 3 MB overflows L2 and lands in L3; 260,100 interior cells graded.

LARGE = 4096: 3 grids x 64 MB = 192 MB (measured peak RSS 195 MB), far beyond any LLC, so the oracle runs in the DRAM-streaming regime that dominates the operation at scale. It is simultaneously (a) the harness ceiling max_spec_size = 4096, and (b) exactly this benchmark's configured DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE (1<<12) in drivers/problem-sizes.json:453 - independent corroboration from the suite's own authors that this side length is the intended feasible top end for this operation.

Deliberately NOT reused from other rows: the ladder is in SIDE LENGTHS of a square grid whose cost is quadratic in the number, which is why the top point is 4096 and not the 2^20-ish numbers a 1-D Theta(n) benchmark would carry, and why it is not a power-of-two-only ladder like the FFT rows (nothing here needs a power of two - 64/512/4096 are powers of two only because the x8 geometric step starting from a cache-sized grid lands there).

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
MATHEMATICALLY DEFINED, HARNESS-BROKEN:
- N = 0 (empty grid): the operation is defined (empty output) and the oracle is safe (both loops have zero trip count). The DRIVER is not: cpu.cc:83 computes TEST_SIZE-1 in size_t, which underflows to 2^64-1, and the comparison loop walks out of bounds on zero-length vectors. MEASURED: the full serial driver at ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE=0 does not crash but HANGS - killed by a 30 s timeout, rc = 124, for both a correct and a do-nothing candidate. This size is in static_base_sizes (config.yaml:562), so it will be generated; it maps to "hang" -> baseline_incompatible and burns 30 s of wall clock per (sample, model).
- N = 1 (single cell, no neighbours): defined, output = {0}. MEASURED: VACUOUS PASS - a candidate that never reads input and just writes zeros returns "Validation: PASS", because the graded window [1, N-2] is empty.
- N = 2 (2x2, every cell has 2 orthogonal / 3 Moore neighbours): defined. MEASURED: VACUOUS PASS, same cause. Also in static_base_sizes.
- N = 3: the smallest non-vacuous size; exactly one cell (1,1) is graded. MEASURED: the do-nothing candidate correctly FAILS here.

DEFINED AND SAFE BUT WEAK (correct output is uniformly zero, so a "write zeros" candidate passes):
- all-zeros grid (pattern all_zeros): every count is 0.
- all-ones grid (pattern all_same at range (0,2) yields the midpoint 1): interior count 4, edge 3, corner 2 under the current rule - never exactly 1, so output is all zeros for N >= 3.
- alternating at range (0,2) -> values {0,2}, and extreme_values -> {INT_MIN, INT_MAX}: no cell equals 1 at all, so every count is 0 and the output is all zeros. These two are worth keeping only as ==1-vs-!=0 discriminators, not as scale tests.
- ascending/descending at range (0,2): integral ramp with span 2 cycles 0,1,2 - the only stock pattern that mixes a real 1 with a non-1 non-zero value, i.e. the sharpest stock probe of the literal ==1 rule.

DEFINED AND STRONG (the cases worth hand-building):
- single isolated 1 at the grid centre: the exact discriminator between the current 4-neighbour and the pending 8-neighbour rule (4 cells light up vs 8), and simultaneously a check of the ==1 rule. Fits explicit_values at N = 7 (49 <= 64).
- two orthogonally adjacent 1s, and two DIAGONALLY adjacent 1s: the diagonal pair is invisible to the 4-neighbour rule and decisive for the 8-neighbour one.
- a full row or column of 1s: exercises row-stride indexing.
NOTE: the entire boundary ring is ungraded at EVERY size (cpu.cc:83-84), so "all cells on the edge" style degenerate inputs cannot be graded at all - a wrap-around/periodic boundary implementation passes every size.

benchmarks.name: 51_stencil_edge_kernel
benchmarks.input_form: One `std::vector<int> imageIn` of exactly N*N elements, interpreted as an N x N grayscale image in ROW-MAJOR order, plus an output vector `imageOut` of the same N*N length and the scalar `size_t N`. The 3x3 edge kernel {{-1,-1,-1},{-1,8,-1},{-1,-1,-1}} is a compile-time constant declared by the PROMPT itself (not by baseline.hpp), so it is not an input. Relevant dimensions: N = side length (the only free parameter) and P = N*N = pixel count = fill-site element count. Driver fill site: `ENHANCED_FILL(input, 0, 255)` -> `fillRand(input, 0, 255)`, which via `rand() % (max-min) + min` actually draws from [0, 254] (255 is never produced) — measured. benchmark_shapes.json records this benchmark as one fill site, total_elements = n*n, explicit_values_supported = true.
benchmarks.min_size: N = 0. There is NO mathematical size floor: the oracle is total on every N >= 0 and requires no minimum neighbourhood. Valid form (the actual precondition) is a length invariant, not a size floor: imageIn.size() == imageOut.size() == N*N. Verified by execution: N = 0 returns an empty output, N = 1 returns clip(8*v), N = 2 returns four corner pixels — no crash, no undefined branch.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — HARNESS-FORCED, not operation-forced: thesis/config/config.yaml:572 `max_spec_size: 4096` ("validation rejects larger"). The operation itself has no upper limit (the oracle would stay correct until `int x = i + k` at baseline.hpp:28 overflows, i.e. N > 2^31, which is unreachable). The practical ceiling from the 10 s budget alone would be N ~= 18,700; the ceiling from host memory with 4 MPI ranks x 3 vectors is N ~= 18,100 on 15.7 GB. The config cap of 4096 binds first by a factor of ~4.6 in side length.
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE on N. Any N >= 0 is valid — explicitly NOT restricted to powers of two, not to even N, not to N >= 3 (the driver's own N = 1024 / 4096 are powers of two only by convention, and the oracle's loops `for i < N` / `for j < N` carry no such guard). The genuine precondition is on the VALUES, not on N: (a) semantically the values must be grayscale pixels in [0, 255] — the prompt says "grayscale image" and the clip to [0,255] presupposes it; (b) hard limit: the oracle accumulates into an `int sum` over 9 taps with coefficients in {-1, 8}, so |sum| <= 16*|v| and any |v| > INT_MAX/16 = 134,217,727 is signed-integer overflow (UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR) inside the ORACLE. Measured with UBSan: baseline.hpp:33 "signed integer overflow: -2147483648 * 8". Consequence: the enhanced fill patterns `extreme_values` (id 6, INT_MIN/INT_MAX) and `spike_at` (id 9, INT_MAX/2) and any spec value_range beyond ~+/-1.3e8 are OUT OF DOMAIN for this benchmark and must not be used.
benchmarks.size_semantics: The size number is the SIDE LENGTH N of a square image, not the element count. The fill site and both vectors carry N*N elements (cpu.cc:47-48, cpu.cc:65), so work and memory grow QUADRATICALLY in the spec's size number: a spec of size 4095 fills 16,769,025 values. This matters twice — for the explicit_values pattern, whose cap of 64 values binds on n*n (config.yaml:583-586), limiting explicit_values specs to N <= 8; and for memory, since every MPI rank holds a complete copy (the mpi prompt states "Every rank has a complete copy of imageIn").
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(9 * N^2) = Theta(N^2) in the side length, i.e. Theta(P) LINEAR in the pixel count. Fixed 3x3 kernel, 9 taps per output pixel, no data-dependent branching beyond the boundary test and the clip, no reduction, O(1) auxiliary memory, perfectly data-parallel (imageOut[i] depends only on imageIn, never on imageOut). Measured throughput on this host: 2.7e-8 s/pixel at -O3, i.e. the constant is small and flat from N = 1024 upward (memory-bandwidth bound).
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
min_size = 0 because a 2-D convolution with zero padding is total: an empty image has an empty convolution, and the oracle's loop bounds encode exactly that. No power-of-two or minimum-neighbourhood condition exists, so none is imposed.

The three scale points come from the memory hierarchy of a row-major 3x3 stencil and from the halo/interior ratio, which is the ONLY structural parameter this operation has. Boundary pixels = 4N-4, interior = (N-2)^2:
- SMALL N = 15: image = 900 B, entirely L1-resident, so the kernel is compute-bound. 56 of 225 pixels (24.9%) are boundary pixels — zero padding has FIRST-ORDER weight on the result, while all three pixel classes (4 corners, 52 non-corner edge, 169 interior) are present in quantity. This is the smallest scale at which the operation is fully exercised without being degenerate.
- MEDIUM N = 511: 1.044 MB per vector — past typical per-core L2 (0.5-2 MB), resident in L3. Boundary drops to 0.78%, so the interior sweep dominates and the 3-row working set (3*511*4 = 6 KB) is the only thing that stays cached. This is the regime where the loop body, not the halo, decides the result.
- LARGE N = 4095: in + out = 134 MB, several times any L3 — genuinely memory-bandwidth bound, boundary 0.098%. It is also the regime where a 4-rank MPI row decomposition has non-trivial halo rows.

All three are of the form 2^k - 1 (15, 511, 4095). That family follows from the operation's domain (defined for EVERY N, not only powers of two) combined with the fact that every size the driver itself ever uses is a power of two — validation TEST_SIZE = 1024, DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE = (1<<12). The general-N part of the domain is therefore completely untested by the existing harness, and a one-short-of-power-of-two side length guarantees a remainder row AND a remainder column for any power-of-two-aligned blocking, SIMD width or rank split, while keeping the three points cleanly log-spaced (15 -> 511 -> 4095, ~34x and ~8x in side length, ~1160x and ~64x in pixel count). This is derived from the operation and from the driver's own defaults, never from any candidate code.

LARGE was fixed by the harness cap, not by the 10 s budget — see budget_adjustment.

benchmarks.name: 52_stencil_1d_jacobi_3-point_stencil
benchmarks.input_form: One 1-D array of doubles, no structure. `input`: std::vector<double> of length N, values drawn i.i.d. uniform in [-100.0, 100.0]; `output`: std::vector<double> of the SAME length N, pre-zeroed by the driver. Relevant dimensions: exactly one, N. Operation: one out-of-place Jacobi sweep, output[i] = (input[i-1] + input[i] + input[i+1]) / 3 with out-of-range reads replaced by 0 (divisor held at 3, never renormalised). Signature: void jacobi1D(std::vector<double> const& input, std::vector<double>& output) — length is carried implicitly by input.size(), there is no separate N argument.
benchmarks.min_size: Three distinct floors, all verified by execution: (a) MATHEMATICAL: N >= 0. The operation is total — N=0 gives the empty output, N=1 gives input[0]/3. Oracle measured safe and correct at N=0,1,2,3 (N=0 -> [], in=[1] -> [0.3333333333], in=[1,2] -> [1,1], in=[1,2,3] -> [1, 2, 1.666666667]). (b) HARNESS floor N >= 1: at TEST_SIZE=0 the driver's compare loop `for (size_t i = 1; i < TEST_SIZE-1; i++)` (cpu.cc:76) underflows to SIZE_MAX and indexes empty vectors — AddressSanitizer reports SEGV at cpu.cc:77. (c) NON-VACUOUS-VALIDATION floor N >= 3: at N in {1,2} that loop compares zero cells, so validate() returns PASS for any submission (measured: a submission that writes -999999 at both boundaries PASSes at N=1 and N=2). Recommended operating floor for scale points: N >= 3.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — FORCED BY HARNESS. thesis/config/config.yaml:572 sets `max_spec_size: 4096`; thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294 rejects any spec with size > max_size ("size %s exceeds max_spec_size %s"). A second, far higher ceiling (N <= INT_MAX) follows from fillRand's `int i` counter at utilities.hpp:146 and never binds while (2) holds. The operation itself imposes no maximum.
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE from the operation. Any N, no power-of-two requirement, no minimum point count, no ordering, sign, distinctness, or matrix-form precondition; the kernel is a fixed radius-1 affine map applied at every index. All conditions that exist are harness-side: (1) N >= 3 for the interior-only comparison window [1, TEST_SIZE-2] (cpu.cc:76) to inspect any cell; (2) N <= 4096, hard-enforced by the enhanced-tests spec schema (config.yaml:572 `max_spec_size: 4096`, checked at specs.py:293-294); (3) N <= INT_MAX from fillRand's `int i` loop counter (utilities.hpp:146) — never binding under (2). Note (2) is a CURRENT-CONFIG cap, not a property of the operation.
benchmarks.size_semantics: The size number IS the element count N of the input and output vectors, directly and with nothing derived from it. cpu.cc:52 reads `const size_t TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024);` and cpu.cc:54 allocates `input(TEST_SIZE), correct(TEST_SIZE), test(TEST_SIZE)`; ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE overrides that default (enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79). Not a side length, not an nnz seed, no sparsity factor. Consequences: validator memory = 3 * 8 * N bytes; the model's own working set = 2 * 8 * N bytes; the oracle performs exactly N iterations. The default non-enhanced validation size is 1024. Separately and on a different axis, the timing/performance stage uses DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE = (1<<24) for serial/omp/mpi (problem-sizes.json:470) while the correctness stage builds with (1<<8) (thesis/evaluation/tools.py:44) — DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE only sizes the Context in init() (cpu.cc:36-37) and never affects validate().
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(N) — exactly N loop iterations (baseline.hpp:14), each 2 predicated adds + 1 add + 1 division, 2 loads + 1 store. No algorithmic phase transition in N; the cost model is purely linear-streaming. Working set 16N bytes (input+output), 24N bytes for the validator's three buffers (input, correct, test). Measured on the container (i7-12700H, g++ 13.3, -O3): ~4 ns/element while cache-resident (N=17: 72 ns/call = 4.2 ns/el; N=1024: 4.027 us = 3.93 ns/el; N=4096: 16.944 us = 4.14 ns/el) and 6.1 ns/element at N=2^24. The oracle is NOT vectorised — the two per-iteration boundary branches (`if (i > 0)`, `if (i < input.size()-1)`, baseline.hpp:16-21) sit inside the loop — so it is scalar/branch bound (~12 cycles/element) rather than bandwidth bound at these sizes.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
The operation is Theta(N) with a fixed 3-point radius-1 kernel, so the scale axis CANNOT be justified by complexity classes — there are none. Exactly two quantities vary with N for this operation, and both are derived from the operation itself, not from any observed code:

(A) The boundary fraction 2/N. The operation has exactly two structurally special indices (0 and N-1, where the prompt's "replace with 0" rule applies) and N-2 uniform interior indices. 2/N is the only dimensionless structural parameter of the problem.
(B) The working set 16N bytes (24N in the validator), i.e. where a single linear sweep sits in the memory hierarchy.

SMALL = 17. Boundary fraction 2/17 = 11.8%, i.e. the two special indices are a first-order share of the work — the regime where the boundary rule dominates. N >= 3 is required for the driver's window to compare anything (see min_size); 17 is comfortably above that while keeping 2/N large. 17 is odd and prime, so N is not a multiple of any SIMD lane count (2/4/8/16): a sweep of an arbitrary-length array always leaves a nonempty remainder, and at N=17 the single remainder element coincides with the right boundary — the maximal-stress combination of the operation's two structural special cases. Working set 272 B (408 B for three buffers): fully L1-resident, so nothing about memory is being measured here. This is chosen from the operation's structure (two special endpoints + a tail on an arbitrary-length sweep), never from any candidate's strategy.

MEDIUM = 1024. Boundary fraction 0.195% — the operation is effectively a pure interior sweep, the exact complement of SMALL. N is a power of two, fully aligned, tail-free: deliberately the structural complement of 17, so the SMALL/MEDIUM pair separates "tail + boundary structure" from "scale" instead of confounding them. Working set 16 KiB (24 KiB for three buffers): still inside L1d on the measurement host (48 KiB/core), so this is the pure in-cache streaming regime. It is additionally the benchmark's OWN committed non-enhanced validation size (cpu.cc:52, `ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)`), which makes it the calibration anchor between the correctness stage and the enhanced stage — a repo-sourced, candidate-independent reason.

LARGE = 4096. The largest size the enhanced-tests schema admits (config.yaml:572), hence the strongest available scale stress. It is also the only memory-hierarchy transition reachable inside the admissible range on this host: three buffers of 32 KiB = 96 KiB > L1d 48 KiB, while MEDIUM's 24 KiB still fits — so 1024 -> 4096 genuinely changes regime rather than only changing magnitude. Boundary fraction 0.049%.

The three points are therefore: boundary-dominated + tail (17), pure interior in-L1 (1024), interior out-of-L1 at the schema ceiling (4096). No two of them are "the same size reused".

WHAT THE OPERATION WOULD WANT IF THE CAP WERE LIFTED. For a memory-bound linear stencil the meaningful LARGE is the DRAM-bandwidth regime, which is unreachable below 4096 (the entire admissible band 0..4096 is 64 KiB and never leaves L2). If `max_spec_size` is raised, LARGE should become 2^24 = 16777216 (256 MiB working set, >10x the 24 MiB L3; also the repo's own configured DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE for serial/omp/mpi at problem-sizes.json:470, so feasibility is corroborated by the repo) and MEDIUM 2^18 = 262144 (4 MiB working set: out of the 1.25 MiB per-core L2, inside L3). Both were measured (see measurement_detail) and both sit far inside the 10 s budget.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no. The operation is total on every N >= 0 and every double value, so there is no domain to restrict. Explicit caveat: the prompt is complete only in real arithmetic. Under IEEE-754 it does not pin the ACCUMULATION ORDER — the oracle computes ((L + R) + C)/3 (baseline.hpp:16-22: left, then right, then centre) while the prompt's printed formula reads ((L + C) + R)/3 — and under the extreme_values fill the two differ by inf-vs-finite. Adding an order clause would be the WRONG repair and is explicitly rejected by the audit (oracle-correctness-audit.md:451: it "would make the benchmark measure FP associativity rather than the stencil"). The fix belongs in the spec/pattern policy or the validator, not in the prompt.
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: no — a flat std::vector<double> of length N filled in [-100,100] is exactly what the generic fill produces; no derived counts, no structural repair, no rejection sampling, and every enhanced-fill pattern (0-10) applies to the single fill site unchanged.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Degenerate inputs that are MATHEMATICALLY DEFINED for this operation (separate axis from small/medium/large):
- N = 0 (empty input): DEFINED — empty output. Oracle verified safe: `N=0 out=[]`. NOT USABLE as a spec: validate()'s compare loop underflows (cpu.cc:76) and reads out of bounds; ASan reports SEGV at cpu.cc:77; without ASan it reads heap garbage and returns FAIL for EVERY submission, including a prompt-exact correct one (measured). Already excluded in practice — the recorded gate marks all three size-0 specs "baseline_incompatible".
- N = 1: DEFINED — output[0] = input[0]/3 (both neighbours out of range -> 0, divisor stays 3). Measured: in=[1] -> [0.3333333333]. Usable at oracle level but VACUOUS at driver level (0 cells compared; a boundary-garbage submission PASSes).
- N = 2: DEFINED — output[0] = output[1] = (input[0]+input[1])/3. Measured: in=[1,2] -> [1,1]. Also VACUOUS at driver level.
- N = 3: DEFINED and the smallest N with a fully interior cell; the smallest N at which validate() compares anything at all (exactly 1 cell).
- all values equal / all zeros: DEFINED. all_zeros -> all zeros. all_same = v -> interior v, boundaries 2v/3. This is the case that discriminates "always divide by 3" from "normalise by the neighbour count" — and the interior-only window is blind to it at EVERY N (measured: a submission correct on the interior and -999999 at both boundaries PASSes at N = 1, 2, 3, 4, 17 and 1024).
- extreme_values (alternating -DBL_MAX / +DBL_MAX): DEFINED in R, NOT representable in IEEE double — the oracle's first partial sum overflows to +/-inf and the verdict inverts in both directions (BL-18). 6 of the 20 recorded specs for this benchmark use this pattern.
NOT degenerate for this operation (no special meaning, do not spend spec budget on them): duplicate values, sortedness, sign, distinctness — the kernel is a fixed local affine map and no input value is structurally special.
benchmarks.pending_fix:
YES — this row is PROVISIONAL on its degenerate axis. Two open, not-yet-implemented semantics decisions, both filed as open decision #73 in thesis/docs/oracle-correctness-audit.md:605:
(1) BL-18 (audit:442-451): extreme_values policy for oracles that perform a floating-point sum. The oracle accumulates ((L+R)+C)/3 while the prompt writes ((L+C)+R)/3; under fill pattern 6 the oracle overflows to +/-inf, the prompt-exact implementation stays finite and is FLAGGED WRONG, and a genuinely different operation (neighbours-only average) overflows to the same +/-inf, giving |inf-inf| = NaN, and `NaN > 1e-4` is false, so it is counted CORRECT. Four fix options are listed in the audit and none is chosen yet. Note that the in-flight NaN-aware hardening of the SHARED comparator (uncommitted working-tree change to drivers/cpp/utilities.hpp, adding mismatchIsFinite/fequal guards) does NOT reach this benchmark: 52's cpu.cc:77 uses a raw inline `std::abs(...) > 1e-4` predicate and calls no shared comparator.
(2) The interior-only validation window `i in [1, TEST_SIZE-2]` (cpu.cc:76): extend it to the full vector, or document it. If it is EXTENDED, N=1 and N=2 stop being vacuous, the stated boundary rule becomes enforceable, and TEST_SIZE=0 needs an explicit underflow guard before size 0 can ever be used — all of which changes what the degenerate band tests.
The SCALE axis (17 / 1024 / 4096) is NOT affected by either decision. A third, non-semantic dependency: LARGE is pinned to the current `max_spec_size: 4096`; if that config value is raised the row's LARGE (and MEDIUM) should be re-cut to 2^24 / 2^18 as set out in domain_rationale.

benchmarks.name: 53_stencil_2d_jacobi_5-point_stencil
benchmarks.input_form: One iteration of an out-of-place 5-point (von Neumann) Jacobi stencil on a square grid. Input: `std::vector<double> const& input` of exactly N*N elements, row-major, values drawn by fillRand uniformly from [-100.0, +100.0]; `std::vector<double>& output`, pre-sized to N*N by the driver and zero-filled before the call; `size_t N` = the SIDE LENGTH. output[i*N+j] = (up + down + left + right + centre)/5 with out-of-grid neighbours substituted by 0 and the divisor held fixed at 5. Relevant dimension: a SINGLE one, the side length N — the grid is square by construction, there is no independent row/column extent. Derived quantities: element count N^2; bytes per vector 8*N^2; the driver's validate() allocates THREE such vectors (input, correct, test) = 24*N^2 bytes.
benchmarks.min_size: Mathematically: 0. The operation is total on every N >= 0 and the oracle is clean there — EXECUTED: N=0 returns an empty output, N=1 returns exactly input[0]/5 (measured 13.607509 == in[0]/5), N=2 fine. Operationally the minimum DISCRIMINATING size is 3: the driver's validation window is i,j in [1, N-2], so N=0 -> segfault (size_t underflow, already gated), N=1 and N=2 -> ZERO cells compared (vacuous pass), N=3 -> exactly 1 cell compared. MEASURED cells-compared: N=1:0, N=2:0, N=3:1, N=7:25, N=16:196, N=127:15625, boundary cells compared: 0 at EVERY size. So: min_size = 3 for the scale axis; 0/1/2 belong to degenerate_cases, not to a size floor.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — FORCED BY THE HARNESS, not by the operation and not by the runtime budget: thesis/config/config.yaml:572 `max_spec_size: 4096`, enforced in thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294. The operation has no upper bound of its own. Extrapolating the measured 6.4 ns per cell at N=8192 (0.431 s median for 67.1 M cells), the 10 s serial budget would first bind near N ~ 4*10^4 — about 10x beyond the cap, and at that point the driver's three vectors would need ~37 GB. For this operation memory, not time, is the real ceiling; the config cap sits far below both.
benchmarks.special_conditions: No mathematical precondition at all: N is any non-negative integer — no power of two, no minimum point count, no matrix-validity or conditioning requirement, no sparsity parameter. The only structural requirement is input.size() == output.size() == N*N in row-major order, which the driver guarantees by construction. ONE harness-derived condition is adopted for this row: N must be ODD. Reason (derived, then measured): with row-major indexing the vertical neighbours of (i,j) are +/-N apart in the flat vector and the horizontal ones +/-1. Under the `extreme_values` fill pattern (index-parity alternating DBL_LOWEST/DBL_MAX, enhanced-fill.hpp:199-200 + :128-141) odd N makes all four neighbours have parity OPPOSITE to the centre, so all four carry the same extreme and every summation order yields the same +/-inf; even N makes the two vertical neighbours share the centre's parity, so DBL_MAX + DBL_LOWEST cancels exactly and the RESULT DEPENDS ON ASSOCIATION ORDER. EXECUTED against a mathematically identical, differently-associated implementation through the driver's own window and epsilon: N=3 PASS, N=4 FAIL, N=6 FAIL, N=7 PASS, N=127 PASS, N=128 FAIL, N=726 FAIL, N=727 PASS, N=4093 PASS, N=4096 FAIL. All three chosen scale points are odd primes and are therefore structurally immune to this false-FAIL. Note also (specs.py:325) that the k-patterns bound k by `size`, not by the n^2 element count, so spike_at/duplicate_at/sorted_except_one can only place their special element inside grid ROW 0 — the perturbation still reaches the validated interior through the cell below it, but the perturbed cell's own output is never compared.
benchmarks.size_semantics: The size number is the SIDE LENGTH N, never the element count. ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE overrides validate()'s TEST_SIZE (enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79, used at cpu.cc:55), and the driver then allocates three vectors of TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE doubles (cpu.cc:57) and calls both the oracle and the candidate with TEST_SIZE as N (cpu.cc:71, cpu.cc:74). thesis/enhanced_tests/benchmark_shapes.json:490 records this independently: fill_sites 1, elements_per_site ["n2"], total_elements "n*n". Consequences: element count = N^2, driver memory = 24*N^2 bytes, and explicit_values specs need N^2 values (so they are auto-rejected above N=8 by explicit_values_max_size 64, config.yaml:586).
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(N^2) time in the side length N (equivalently Theta(M) in the element count M = N^2) and Theta(N^2) memory. Per output cell: up to 5 loads, 4 branch-guarded, 4 adds, 1 divide, 1 store — a fixed constant, no recursion, no reduction tree, no size-dependent algorithmic regime change. Arithmetic intensity is ~1 flop per 8 bytes, so once the grid exceeds L3 the oracle is DRAM-bandwidth bound. Measured cost per cell was essentially flat across the whole admissible range (~2.6 ns/cell at N=127 up to ~6-9 ns/cell at N=4093-8192), i.e. runtime is a pure function of N^2 and never a discriminator between candidate strategies.
benchmarks.domain_rationale: The operation admits every N >= 0 and has NO algorithmic regime change with size — one pass, constant work per cell, no thresholds, no numerical conditioning, no power-of-two requirement. The only things that genuinely vary with N are (a) the boundary-to-interior ratio, which falls as 4/N, and (b) which level of the memory hierarchy holds the grid, because the two neighbour directions are qualitatively different in row-major layout: j+/-1 shares the centre's cache line, i+/-1 sits N*8 bytes away. The three scale points therefore span the three memory regimes, and are chosen as odd PRIMES for two independent reasons: odd makes extreme_values order-insensitive (proof + measurements in special_conditions), prime leaves a remainder under every row-block decomposition including the pipeline's fixed 4-thread / 4-rank launch (config.yaml:603-604), and none of the three coincides with a size the benchmark already uses (validate default 1024, DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE 4096, static_base_sizes 0/1/2/7). SMALL = 127: working set 3*127^2*8 = 0.4 MB, fully L2-resident, so the kernel is latency- rather than bandwidth-bound; boundary cells are 508 of 16,129 = 3.1 %, the largest boundary fraction of the three; the validated interior is 15,625 cells, so a systematic indexing error shows at many indices rather than at one. For scale, the benchmark's entire currently realised spec set tops out at size 8, where the interior is 36 cells. MEDIUM = 727: working set 12.1 MB, the geometric midpoint (sqrt(127*4093) = 721) rounded to the nearest prime, giving ~5.7x in N and ~32x in work per step; the footprint sits above typical L2 (0.5-2 MB) and inside typical L3 (16-32 MB), a partially cache-resident regime distinct from both neighbours. LARGE = 4093: working set 383 MB, more than 10x any L3, so the kernel streams from DRAM and the vertical neighbour lies 32,744 bytes (8 pages) away from the centre while the horizontal one shares its line — the regime in which a wrong blocking/tiling or a mis-sized index computation would surface. It is the largest prime <= max_spec_size (4096), i.e. the maximum separation the harness permits from the driver's own default TEST_SIZE of 1024. NOT reachable and therefore explicitly NOT covered: N^2 = 16.75 M still fits comfortably in int32, so the 32-bit index-overflow regime (N > 46,340) lies far beyond the config cap. The 10 s budget played no role in choosing LARGE — see budget_adjustment.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no. The prompt is already complete on the operation: it states the formula, the divisor 5, the row-major NxN layout and the boundary rule verbatim ("Replace with 0 when reading past the boundaries of `input`."), and thesis/docs/benchmark-example-consistency.md:113 records the worked example as consistent with the oracle. Nothing about the chosen sizes needs a prompt sentence. The actionable defect is the mirror image of a prompt gap and must be fixed on the VALIDATOR side, not in the prompt: the stated boundary rule is never checked (0 boundary cells compared at every size, measured), so adding more prompt text would not change any verdict.
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: no. There is exactly one fill site (cpu.cc:65, `ENHANCED_FILL(input, -100.0, 100.0)`, N^2 doubles), the container is a plain flat vector of doubles with no index/structure semantics, and benchmark_shapes.json:490 already models it generically as total_elements "n*n" with explicit_values_supported true. The generic ENHANCED_FILL machinery covers every offered pattern; what this benchmark needs is a pattern-SELECTION rule (odd N for extreme_values), not a benchmark-specific input builder.

benchmarks.name: 54_stencil_game_of_life
benchmarks.input_form: Two flat row-major `std::vector<int>` of length N*N representing an N x N grid (`input` const, `output` written), plus `size_t N`. Signature: `void gameOfLife(std::vector<int> const& input, std::vector<int> &output, size_t N)`. Relevant dimension: N = SIDE LENGTH (one number); element count = N^2. Value domain per prompt: exactly {0,1} (1 = alive, 0 = dead). Operation = ONE generation, Moore-8 neighbourhood, B3/S23, cells outside the grid contribute nothing (oracle convention). Driver generator: `fillRand(input, 0, 2)` -> `rand() % 2` in {0,1}, ~50% alive, unseeded deterministic rand(). Comparison in validate() is EXACT integer `!=` (no epsilon, no reportAndCompare* helper) and only over the strict interior i,j in [1, N-2].
benchmarks.min_size: Mathematically N = 0 (the empty grid is a well-defined input; the oracle's loops simply do not execute — verified by execution). Harness-safe minimum N = 1: at N = 0 the DRIVER's validate() computes `TEST_SIZE-1` on a size_t, wrapping to SIZE_MAX, and indexes zero-length vectors -> segfault (cpu.cc:89-90). Smallest N at which validation inspects anything at all = 3 (exactly 1 cell compared; measured: compared = 0 at N=1 and N=2, = 1 at N=3). There is NO size floor intrinsic to the operation — 0/1/2 belong in degenerate_cases, not in a floor.
benchmarks.max_size: 8192 on the current container (forced by the harness, not by the operation). Two reasons, both measured: (a) validate() allocates THREE N^2 int buffers = 12*N^2 bytes per rank; with the configured `enhanced_launch.mpi_ranks: 4` that is 4*12*N^2 bytes, so the 7 GB container caps N at ~12000, and at N=8192 it is 3.2 GB (fits, headroom). (b) A hard host memory cliff sits just above 8192: N=8192 -> 1.18 s median, N=12288 -> 60.3 s median (clean, 3 reps), N=16384 -> 65.7 s single call at 2.10 GB RSS for only two buffers. Anything above 8192 blows the 10 s budget on this machine.
benchmarks.special_conditions: (1) NO power-of-two requirement and no other structural condition on N: the oracle uses only `i*N + j` address arithmetic and `i>0 / i<N-1 / j>0 / j<N-1` guards (baseline.hpp:25-51) — every N >= 0 is a valid, in-domain input. (2) HARD value precondition: every cell must be in {0,1}. The prompt defines the domain exhaustively; the oracle mixes a `== 1` liveness test (baseline.hpp:52) with `sum += raw value` neighbour accumulation (lines 29-50), so outside {0,1} the two choices interact in a way the prompt never specifies, and INT_MIN/INT_MAX overflow the `int sum` (signed-overflow UB). (3) The generic fill patterns violate (2) at the call site's (0,2) range — MEASURED: ascending/descending -> `0 1 2 0 1 2 ...` (value 2 out of domain, because enhanced-fill.hpp:114-119 uses an INCLUSIVE ramp `position % (span+1)` while utilities.hpp:151 fillRand is HALF-OPEN `rand() % (max-min)`); alternating -> `0 2 0 2 ...`; extreme_values -> INT_MIN/INT_MAX; spike_at -> 1073741823. And there is no single value_range that fixes it: with range [0,1] the ramp/alternating patterns become {0,1} but `fillRand(x,0,1)` degenerates to `rand()%1 == 0` -> ALL DEAD (measured). In-domain patterns are therefore only: all_zeros; all_same with [0,2] (midpoint 1 -> all alive, measured); random/duplicate_at with [0,2); ascending/descending/alternating ONLY with [0,1]; explicit_values with 0/1 values. (4) Driver-side, not operation-side: N <= 2 makes validation vacuous and N = 0 segfaults the validator.
benchmarks.size_semantics: The spec size number is N, the SIDE LENGTH of the grid, NOT the element count. cpu.cc:65-67 allocates three vectors of TEST_SIZE*TEST_SIZE ints and cpu.cc:81/84 passes TEST_SIZE as N. So size s means s^2 cells and 3*s^2*4 bytes of driver allocation per rank. DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE (1<<12) = 4096 is likewise a side length (16.8M cells) and applies only to the perf path (cpu.cc:48), not to validation.
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(N^2) time — exactly N^2 cells, each with at most 8 guarded neighbour loads and a constant-size B3/S23 decision (baseline.hpp:24-68). In terms of the element count M = N^2 it is Theta(M), i.e. linear in the grid. Oracle auxiliary space O(1) (it writes into the caller's buffer); the driver allocates 3*N^2 ints in validate() (cpu.cc:67). Access pattern: radius-1 2-D stencil, streaming, working set 3 rows = 12*N bytes.
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
No size floor from the operation (min_size 0 mathematically, 1 for the harness) because a Game-of-Life generation is defined on any N x N grid including the empty one. The three scale points are derived from the two regimes that are intrinsic to a radius-1 2-D stencil with a dead-outside boundary — the boundary/interior balance and the memory hierarchy — never from candidate code.

SMALL = 7: the boundary-truncated cells number 4N-4 and the full-8-neighbour interior cells (N-2)^2. These are equal at N = 4+2*sqrt(2) ~= 6.83, so N = 7 is the FIRST side length at which full-stencil cells (25) outnumber truncated cells (24); at N = 6 it is 16 vs 20. That is the balance point of this operation, and the smallest scale at which both the uniform path and all eight truncation special cases (4 corners, 4 edges) are present in bulk. Deliberately not a power of two (proves N need not be one) and deliberately NOT 5 — 5 is the size of the worked example printed verbatim in all three prompts, so it is not held out.

MEDIUM = 1024: interior-dominated ((1022/1024)^2 = 99.6% of cells take the uniform 8-neighbour path) AND still cache-resident, so the operation runs compute-bound. The two timed buffers are 8 MiB, the last power of two below the container's 24 MiB L3 (N = 2048 -> 32 MiB straddles it). At ~10^6 interior cells a 50%-alive random fill hits even the rarest rule branch (sum < 2, p = 9/256) ~36 800 times, so the whole B3/S23 rule table is exercised with certainty.

LARGE = 8192: interior-dominated and decisively OUT of cache — 512 MiB of timed buffers = 21x the 24 MiB L3 — so this is the memory-bandwidth regime, the third and last regime the operation has. It is also the largest side length that keeps validate()'s three N^2 buffers inside the container under the configured mpi_ranks = 4 (3.2 GB of 7 GB) and stays inside the 10 s oracle budget (measured 1.18 s median, >= 6.7x headroom on the median, and the worst single observation ever seen — 5.73 s under deliberate container contention — is still inside).

The three points span 49 / 1.05e6 / 6.71e7 cells: boundary-balanced, cache-resident-interior, bandwidth-bound-interior. They are not shared with any other benchmark by convenience — 7 follows from 4N-4 vs (N-2)^2, 1024 from the L3 boundary, 8192 from the pipeline's 3-buffer x 4-rank memory envelope.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: yes: "Cells outside the grid are dead: they contribute 0 to a neighbour count, and the grid does not wrap around." — The value domain is ALREADY pinned by the existing prompt sentence "A cell is 1 if it is alive and 0 if it is dead", so no size or value sentence is needed. The BOUNDARY convention is not pinned anywhere in the prompt (verified: none of the serial/omp/mpi prompt texts mentions the grid edge, and the 5x5 worked example does not separate the possibilities), while the oracle silently commits to dead-outside. Today the omission is harmless because the validator excludes the border ring — I confirmed by execution that a toroidal implementation is accepted by an exact replica of the validate() window at N = 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 16 even though the full grids differ from N = 2 upward. The sentence becomes MANDATORY the moment the interior-only window is widened (audit finding #73, "should fix"); adding it now is harmless and removes an unstated requirement.
benchmarks.custom_input_construction_needed: yes — three independent reasons, all measured. (1) No generic fill pattern + value_range combination keeps the whole pattern set inside {0,1}: at the call site's (0,2) the ramp and alternating patterns emit the out-of-domain value 2 and extreme_values/spike_at emit INT_MIN/INT_MAX/INT_MAX/2 (UB in the oracle's `int sum`), while at [0,1] the random pattern collapses to all-dead (`rand()%1`). The construction must therefore pin values per pattern, not per benchmark. (2) The interesting inputs for one Game-of-Life generation are structural, not statistical — blinker, block, glider, all-alive block, checkerboard — which requires explicit_values; and explicit_values fills CYCLICALLY (enhanced-fill.hpp:216-219), so an N x N grid needs either N^2 values in row-major or a deliberate length-N row that repeats, an easily-misused property that a benchmark-specific builder should encapsulate. (3) The size is a side length, so any generic "size = element count" construction produces the wrong grid.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Mathematically DEFINED for one Game-of-Life generation (this is the degeneracy axis, independent of the 7/1024/8192 scale axis):
- N = 0, empty grid: DEFINED, output is the empty grid. Oracle is safe (executed; baseline.hpp:25-26 loops never run). But the DRIVER's validate() segfaults on the size_t underflow of `TEST_SIZE-1` (cpu.cc:89) — mathematically legal, harness-unsafe.
- N = 1: DEFINED. The single cell has zero neighbours, so it ALWAYS dies regardless of input (executed: [1] -> [0]). Validation window is empty -> unconditional PASS for any implementation.
- N = 2: DEFINED. All four cells are corners with 3 neighbours each: all-alive 2x2 is a still life (executed: 1111 -> 1111); a 2x2 with exactly three alive gives birth to the fourth. Validation window is empty -> unconditional PASS.
- N = 3: DEFINED, and the smallest grid with a true interior cell. All-alive 3x3 -> corners survive (3), edges and centre die (5 and 8): executed 111111111 -> 101000101. Exactly ONE cell is compared.
- All cells dead (all_zeros, any N): DEFINED, a fixed point — no birth is possible without 3 live neighbours (executed at N=7: alive = 0).
- All cells alive (all_same on [0,2] -> midpoint 1, any N): DEFINED — corners have 3 and survive, edge cells have 5 and die, interior cells have 8 and die. This is the classic boundary-convention discriminator, but the interior-only window hides it.
- Checkerboard / alternating on [0,1]: DEFINED.
NOT degenerate but OUT OF DOMAIN — must be excluded, not classified as degenerate: any cell value outside {0,1} (-1, 2, INT_MIN, INT_MAX, INT_MAX/2). These are not "edge cases of the operation"; the prompt does not define the operation there, and INT_MIN/INT_MAX overflow the oracle's `int sum` (UB).

Adjusted. First choice from a pure time-budget extrapolation of the Theta(N^2) ladder (4096 -> 0.313 s, so ~10 s at N ~ 23000) was N = 16384. MEASURED at 16384: 65.72 s for a single oracle call with 2.10 GB RSS for only two buffers — 6.6x over the 10 s budget. Stepping down, N = 12288 still measured 60.33 s median over 3 clean repetitions (min 50.1, max 150.2). The oracle does not scale that way algorithmically; this is a host memory cliff on a 7 GB container (12288 needs 1.21 GB of timed buffers, 16384 needs 2.15 GB). Independently, the pipeline's own memory envelope excludes both: validate() allocates THREE N^2 int buffers per rank and thesis/config/config.yaml sets `mpi_ranks: 4`, i.e. 48*N^2 bytes = 7.2 GB at 12288 and 12.9 GB at 16384, against a 7 GB container. ADJUSTED LARGE = 8192: 1.177 s median (>= 6.7x headroom), 805 MB per rank / 3.2 GB across 4 ranks — the largest power-of-two side that satisfies both walls.
Secondary check on the pipeline's own timeouts at LARGE = 8192 (not the assigned budget, reported for completeness): the -O1 baseline gate (baseline_selftest.py:56 RUN_TIMEOUT = 30) runs 2 trials x 2 oracle calls plus 2 fills of 67M elements, ~7-8 s measured-equivalent — comfortably inside 30 s; the 60 s model-run timeout has similar headroom. Neither wall was the binding constraint.

benchmarks.name: 55_transform_relu
benchmarks.input_form: One dense 1-D vector x of `double`, length n (`std::vector<double>`), transformed IN PLACE: x_i <- max(0, x_i). Exactly one dimension (n) and exactly one fill site; the driver fills x uniformly from [-50.0, 50.0]. No second operand, no shape/structure constraint, no index vectors. The three prompt variants share this input form; the mpi variant adds only a placement requirement on the OUTPUT ("every rank has a complete copy of x, the final result is stored on rank 0"), not on the input. Relevant dimension: n alone.
benchmarks.min_size: 0. There is no size floor. correctRelu on an empty vector is a well-defined no-op (std::transform with begin==end) and the comparator returns PASS for two empty vectors — both verified by execution. The elementwise map max(0,.) is total, so every n >= 0 is a mathematically valid input.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — forced by the harness, not by the operation. thesis/config/config.yaml:572 sets `max_spec_size: 4096` and thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294 rejects any spec with `size > max_size`. The operation itself has no upper bound; memory would be the next binding constraint (3 vectors of n doubles are live in validate()).
benchmarks.special_conditions: None. No power-of-two requirement, no minimum element count, no matrix/graph/geometry validity condition, no sortedness, no distinctness. The oracle max(0.0, v) is total on all doubles, so no value-domain precondition either. Two value-level caveats that are NOT size conditions but bound what a spec may inject: (a) a +Inf element makes the ORACLE output non-finite (max(0,+inf)=+inf), tripping the non-finite-REFERENCE contract in utilities.hpp; (b) a NaN element is silently mapped to 0.0 by std::max's argument ordering (a<b is false for NaN, so `a`=0.0 is returned) — a candidate written as `if (v<0) v=0;` keeps the NaN and is then graded FAIL by contract A1b case 2. Neither can arise from fillRand or from fill patterns 0-9 (extreme_values uses lowest()/max(), both finite); only explicit_values or a value_range containing inf could produce them.
benchmarks.size_semantics: The size number is the ELEMENT COUNT n of the single vector x. It is validate()'s TEST_SIZE (`ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)`, cpu.cc:51), overridden 1:1 by -DENHANCED_TEST_SIZE. thesis/enhanced_tests/benchmark_shapes.json:508-516 confirms `total_elements: "n"`, `elements_per_site: ["n"]`, `fill_sites: 1`, `explicit_values_supported: true` — so spec size == element count == number of explicit values needed (relevant because explicit_values_max_size is 64, capping THAT pattern at n<=64 while the other patterns run to 4096). No nnz, no side length, no derived count.
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(n) time, Theta(1) extra space — one compare-and-select per element, no dependencies; memory-bandwidth bound (measured 1.07 ns/element cache-resident, 2.50 ns/element out of cache).
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
The operation is a pure elementwise map f(v)=max(0,v) over a contiguous double vector: Theta(n), total on the whole value domain, zero preconditions, zero cross-element structure. Consequently the ONLY property that n can vary for this benchmark is (i) how many elements are processed and (ii) how n interacts with a DECOMPOSITION — SIMD lane count, OpenMP chunking, MPI block distribution — since all three parallelism models are in scope for this benchmark (serial/omp/mpi prompts exist). Decomposition remainder is the operation's only structural failure mode, and it is model-specified, not candidate-observed. The three scale points therefore alternate remainder-bearing / cleanly-divisible / remainder-bearing while climbing the scale axis:
- small = 7: the length of the worked example carried in all three prompt variants (the operation's own reference instance). Below one AVX-512 double vector (8 lanes), so a vectorized loop is nothing but its remainder; at the runner's fixed mpi_ranks = 4 (config.yaml:604) a block split is 2/2/2/1, i.e. uneven with fewer than 2 elements on the last rank. Whole array in L1.
- medium = 1024: the size the driver itself was authored to validate at (cpu.cc:51, ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)) — the reference scale of the benchmark. Power of two: exactly divisible by every SIMD width (2/4/8), by 4 OpenMP threads and by 4 MPI ranks. This is the CLEAN-decomposition control point: a candidate with broken remainder handling passes here, which is exactly why it must be flanked by the other two.
- large = 4093: the largest PRIME <= max_spec_size = 4096, i.e. the largest admissible scale that is simultaneously maximally indivisible (4093 = 4*1023 + 1 across 4 ranks, 4093 = 8*511 + 5 across AVX-512 lanes). At full scale every chunked serial/OMP/MPI decomposition again carries a remainder, and the MPI gather must reassemble unequal counts.
Span: 7 -> 1024 -> 4093, about 2.8 orders of magnitude, the maximum the harness ceiling permits.
On the runtime budget: the 10 s budget is NOT the binding constraint here and could not be, because the operation is Theta(n) with a ~1-2.5 ns/element constant. Extrapolating from the measured 2.50 ns/element at n = 6.7e7, a 10 s oracle call would need ~4e9 elements ~ 32 GB for one vector (validate() holds three). The harness cap of 4096 binds ~6 orders of magnitude earlier: LARGE = 4093 measures at 4.39 microseconds, i.e. 0.00004 % of the budget. This is reported, not silently re-budgeted — no alternative budget was substituted and LARGE was not raised past the harness-enforced limit.
Sizes are NOT shared with a sibling transform benchmark out of convenience: 7 follows from THIS prompt's example length, 1024 from THIS driver's TEST_SIZE default, 4093 from the prime-below-ceiling argument, which only makes sense because this operation's sole structural axis is divisibility.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no — the operation is total on every double and every n >= 0, so there is nothing to restrict. (Non-binding note for the spec stage rather than the prompt: specs for this benchmark should not inject +Inf or NaN via explicit_values / an infinite value_range, and should not use a value_range whose magnitudes fall below the absolute comparison epsilon 1e-6, since both make the verdict depend on grader conventions rather than on the stated semantics.)

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Mathematically defined and admissible (all verified by execution, none are size floors):
- n = 0 (empty vector): oracle is a no-op, comparator returns PASS. Non-trivial for omp/mpi candidates (chunk = n/nranks = 0, loop bounds, MPI_Gatherv with zero counts).
- n = 1: single element, no decomposition possible; every rank/thread but one is idle.
- all elements negative: output is the all-zero vector (the map collapses the whole input).
- all elements positive: output == input (identity); a candidate that does nothing at all passes this case, so it must never be the only case.
- all elements equal (all_same pattern): output is either the constant or 0 depending on its sign.
- all zeros: fixed point; also distinguishes -0.0 handling (oracle normalizes -0.0 to +0.0; a candidate keeping -0.0 still passes since |0.0-(-0.0)| = 0).
- exact boundary value 0.0 and values within 1e-6 of 0: the prompt's example contains 0.0; the comparison epsilon is ABSOLUTE 1e-6, so an input of magnitude < 1e-6 makes "zeroed" and "kept" indistinguishable to the grader — such value ranges should be avoided in specs, they weaken the test.
- extreme finite magnitudes (DBL_LOWEST / DBL_MAX, the extreme_values pattern): verified safe — map to 0.0 and DBL_MAX, both finite.
NOT admissible / must be avoided in specs: +Inf (makes the oracle's own output non-finite -> baseline_incompatible marker) and NaN (oracle converts it to 0.0 through std::max's argument ordering, so the verdict is decided by an oracle implementation convention the prompt never states). Both are reachable only via explicit_values or an infinite value_range, never via the driver's own fillRand.
