benchmarks.name: 56_transform_negate_odds
benchmarks.input_form: One dense 1-D `std::vector<int> x`, transformed IN PLACE. Exactly one dimension: n = x.size(). No second array, no matrix, no index/offset arrays, no derived counts. Driver's default value distribution: uniform integers in [1, 99] (fillRand(x, 1, 100) -> rand() % 99 + 1). The oracle itself is total on the whole of `int`: negation is applied only to odd values, whose magnitude is at most 2^31-1, so it never overflows, and INT_MIN is even and therefore takes the exact /2 branch. Output type = input type (vector<int>), compared with EXACT integer equality (no epsilon).
benchmarks.min_size: 0. The oracle is a single std::transform over [x.begin(), x.end()); for n = 0 that is a well-defined no-op, and reportAndCompareEq over two empty vectors is trivially true. There is NO positive size floor for this operation. (Measured: n = 0 and n = 1 both execute the oracle without error.)
benchmarks.max_size: none — no harness or operation limit. `ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE` is a plain compile define consumed as `size_t` (enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79) with no upper check, and the oracle has no size precondition. The only practical ceiling is memory: validate() holds 3 vectors of n ints (~12n bytes) per attempt, so the proposed LARGE costs ~50 MB.
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE. No power-of-two requirement, no divisibility requirement, no minimum point/element count, no structural validity condition (no matrix form, no sparsity, no sortedness). Every n >= 0 and every `int` value is in-domain, and the map is total: for odd i, |i| <= 2^31-1 so -i is representable; INT_MIN is even and takes the exact i/2 branch; for even i, i/2 is exact (no rounding, no truncation ambiguity, including for negatives). The only harness-side (not operation-side) condition: the enhanced k-patterns (duplicate_at / sorted_except_one / spike_at) require size >= 2 (enhanced-fill.hpp:21-24), which excludes only the degenerate sizes 0 and 1, not any of the three scale points.
benchmarks.size_semantics: The size number is the ELEMENT COUNT of the single vector: n = x.size() = TEST_SIZE in validate() (cpu.cc:49/53) and = DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE in init() (cpu.cc:31). It is not a side length, not an nnz, and nothing is derived from it. Memory footprint in validate() is ~12n bytes (input + correctResult + testResult), per attempt, MAX_VALIDATION_ATTEMPTS = 2.
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(n) time, Theta(1) extra space. One branch + one integer op per element, one int read and one int write per element -> memory-bandwidth bound above cache. Measured slope is linear: 1.6e-7 s @ n=31, 8.7e-5 s @ n=100003, 4.7e-3 s @ n=4194301, 1.41e-1 s @ n=67108859 -> ~1.1 ns/element at DRAM scale (~7 GB/s of touched int data).
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
The operation is a total, branch-per-element map on integers with no algorithmic phase change in n, so the scale axis cannot be justified by "the algorithm behaves differently above X". It must instead be justified by the regimes that change which CODE PATH a serial/OpenMP/MPI implementation of an elementwise map actually executes. Three such regimes exist, and one length property cuts across all of them.

Cross-cutting property: PRIME length. An elementwise map is parallelised by index partitioning (SIMD lanes, OpenMP chunks, MPI scatter/gather with p ranks and every rank holding a full copy per the mpi prompt). Its characteristic failure is a mishandled remainder: n/w elements covered, n mod w dropped or double-written. A prime n guarantees n mod w != 0 for every vector width w > 1 and every worker count p > 1 (p < n), so the tail path is forced at all three scale points. This follows from the operation's decomposition, not from any observed candidate; no candidate/model code was consulted.

SMALL = 31 (124 B). Sub-partition regime: fewer elements than one AVX-512 int vector (16) times a handful of workers, so any decomposition assuming at least one full chunk per worker degenerates, and the whole vector fits in ~2 cache lines. Prime, and below the driver's own default TEST_SIZE of 1024 (cpu.cc:49) by a factor ~33.

MEDIUM = 100003 (400 KB). Cache-resident regime: beyond L1 (32 KiB = 8192 ints) so chunking and prefetch are real, but still inside a typical L2/L3, so the loop is not yet DRAM-bound. Prime. ~100x above the driver's default validation size, i.e. a genuinely different scale point rather than a nudge.

LARGE = 4194301 (16.8 MB) = the largest prime below 2^22. Streaming regime: the working set exceeds a typical LLC, so the loop is memory-bandwidth bound, which is the regime the benchmark authors themselves configured for timing (problem-sizes.json: serial/omp/mpi = (1<<22) = 4194304). Choosing the largest prime just below that scale keeps the authors' own working scale while forcing the remainder path that the exact power of two hides.

Runtime budget: NON-BINDING here, and reported as such rather than silently replaced. The 10 s ceiling is respected with three orders of magnitude to spare (measured median 0.0047 s at LARGE). Extrapolating the measured 1.1 ns/element, saturating 10 s would need ~9e9 elements ~= 36 GB of int data — not constructible on this host and pointless for a differential-correctness stage. The budget is a ceiling, not a target, so LARGE was set from the memory-hierarchy regime plus the driver's own configured scale, and the measured headroom is stated openly.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
Mathematically DEFINED for this operation (all executable, all distinct from the scale axis):
- n = 0 (empty vector): std::transform over an empty range is a no-op; comparison of two empty vectors is trivially equal. MEASURED to run. Note k-patterns are skipped (enhanced-fill.hpp:177) and cannot be specified there.
- n = 1: single element, no partitioning possible; the classic "one element per worker / fewer elements than workers" case for omp and mpi.
- all values 0 (all_zeros): 0 is even, 0/2 = 0, so 0 is the ONLY fixed point of the map; the whole output equals the whole input. A candidate that negates on the wrong parity branch is invisible here, which is exactly why it is a degenerate rather than a discriminating input.
- all values equal and even (e.g. all 50): output is a uniform halving; the negate branch is never taken.
- all values equal and odd (e.g. all 49): output is a uniform negation; the halve branch is never taken. Together with the previous case this isolates the two branches.
- alternating extremes (extreme_values pattern): INT_MIN (even) -> -1073741824 exactly, INT_MAX (odd) -> -2147483647. Well defined, no UB, no overflow — worth stating because "negate" plus INT_MIN is the usual UB trap and it does NOT apply here.
- all values negative (reachable only via an ENHANCED_FILL_LO/HI override): parity of a negative integer is well defined, and the oracle's `i % 2 == 0` branch classifies -6 as even (-3) and -5 as odd (+5). This is the discriminating case against the common `i % 2 == 1` idiom, which in C++ is false for every negative odd int. It is a legitimate correctness probe, not a prompt ambiguity (see prompt_restriction_needed).
- (parallel only, not a property of the math) n smaller than the OpenMP thread count or the MPI rank count: 31 already exercises this for large rank counts.

benchmarks.name: 57_transform_inverse_offset
benchmarks.input_form: One 1-D `std::vector<double> x` (in-place). Single dimension: n = x.size(). The size parameter IS the element count (benchmark_shapes.json: fill_sites 1, elements_per_site ["n"], total_elements "n"). Values drawn uniformly from [-50.0, 50.0] at both the perf site (cpu.cc:26) and the validation site (cpu.cc:55). Operation: elementwise map x_i -> 1 - 1/x_i, no cross-element coupling, no ordering, no matrix structure.
benchmarks.min_size: 0. The operation is mathematically defined for the empty vector (the empty map = no-op) and for n = 1; there is NO size floor. MEASURED: oracle runs at n = 0 (out.size == 0), n = 1 and n = 2 without error. The benchmark's real precondition is on VALUES, not on n.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — FORCED BY HARNESS: thesis/config/config.yaml:572 `max_spec_size: 4096`, enforced in thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294 ("size %s exceeds max_spec_size %s"). Not an operation limit. The operation itself has no upper bound; the physical limit measured here is MEMORY, not time (see measurement_detail).
benchmarks.special_conditions: No power-of-two requirement, no sortedness, no minimum point count, no matrix form. The only precondition is the POLE of the map: x_i != 0 (and |x_i| >= ~5.56e-309 = 1/DBL_MAX, else 1/x overflows). MEASURED: x = 0 -> -inf, x = -0.0 -> +inf, x = 4.94e-324 -> -inf, x = 5.0e-309 -> -inf, x = DBL_MIN 2.225e-308 -> -4.494e+307 (finite), x = +/-DBL_MAX -> 1.0 (finite). Two consequences that constrain the size domain: (1) random fill can NEVER hit the pole — fillRand computes (rand()/(double)RAND_MAX)*100 - 50 and RAND_MAX = 2147483647 is ODD, so rand()/RAND_MAX == 0.5 is unreachable; the closest attainable values are +/-2.3283064365386963e-08 (MEASURED). (2) the enhanced ramp patterns DO hit the pole at ODD n: enhancedRampValue(-50,50,i,n) == 0.0 exactly iff i/(n-1) == 0.5, i.e. iff n is odd. MEASURED: ascending at n = 17/1023/4093/4095 -> exactly 1 pole hit; at n = 18/1024/4090/4096 -> 0 hits. Therefore all three scale points are chosen EVEN, which keeps ascending(3)/descending(4)/sorted_except_one(8) inside the domain. Independent of size, all_zeros(1) and all_same(2) are out of domain at the call site's range: enhancedMidValue(-50,50) = -50 + (50-(-50))/2 = 0.0 exactly, so all_same is bit-identical to all_zeros (MEASURED: 18/18, 1024/1024, 4090/4090 elements at the pole for both).
benchmarks.size_semantics: Element count of the single 1-D double vector. size == n == number of doubles == number of divisions performed. Not a side length, not a derived nnz. validate() allocates three vectors of this length (input, correctResult, testResult) -> memory footprint = 24 * n bytes.
benchmarks.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space. Exactly one double division and one subtraction per element (baseline.hpp:11, `std::transform` with lambda `1.0 - 1.0/x`), fully vectorizable, no data dependence between elements. MEASURED throughput at -O3: ~2.6-2.7 ns/element once the array exceeds cache (2.63 ns/elem at n = 2^24, 2.73 ns/elem at n = 2^26).
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
Derived only from the operation, its domain and the budget — no candidate code was inspected.

min_size = 0: an elementwise map is total over vectors of any length including the empty one; nothing in oracle or driver imposes a floor (baseline.hpp:11 is a bare std::transform over begin/end).

The scale axis for a pure O(n) elementwise map has exactly three structural regimes, and nothing else — there is no reduction tree, no recursion, no ordering:
(a) sub-vector-length / tail-only regime, where a SIMD or chunked implementation runs mostly remainder code and every worker gets a very small slice;
(b) a clean, evenly-divisible regime where the main vectorized body dominates and partitioning is exact;
(c) the largest admissible regime with a non-trivial remainder, so the main body, the SIMD tail and an uneven worker split are all exercised at once.

Parity is a DOMAIN constraint here, not a taste: the fill range [-50,50] is symmetric about the pole x = 0, and the harness's linear ramps land exactly on 0 iff n is odd (measured). Odd scale points would silently convert every ramp-pattern spec into a baseline_incompatible run. All three points are therefore even.

small = 18 = 2*8 + 2: the smallest size giving TWO complete AVX-512 doubles vectors (width 8) plus a non-empty scalar tail, hence 18 mod 4 = 2 and 18 mod 8 = 2 -> a tail for every common SIMD width; over the harness's 4 workers (config.yaml:603-604 omp_threads 4 / mpi_ranks 4) it splits 5/5/4/4 — uneven but with every worker non-empty, which is the tail-only regime (a) without collapsing into the degenerate n < workers case. Deliberately distinct from the static base sizes [0,1,2,7] (config.yaml:562), which already cover n < 4 and n = 7.

medium = 1024: the benchmark's OWN default validation size (cpu.cc:50 `ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)`), i.e. the scale the unenhanced correctness stage validates at, so the enhanced ladder stays anchored to it. 2^10 is divisible by 2, 4, 8 and by 4 workers -> the clean regime (b): no SIMD tail, exact partition. This is the control point against which the two remainder points are read.

large = 4090: the largest n <= max_spec_size (4096, harness-forced) that is even AND == 2 (mod 8). Even keeps the symmetric ramps off the pole; 2 (mod 8) forces a non-empty tail for SSE2/AVX2/AVX-512 widths simultaneously; 4090 = 4*1022 + 2 splits 1023/1023/1022/1022 over 4 workers -> regime (c) at the top of the admissible range, with ~511 full AVX-512 iterations before the tail. 4096 was rejected because it repeats medium's clean-divisibility character and adds no new structure.

Note on the cache regime: at n <= 4096 the vector is <= 32 KB and never leaves L1/L2, so the memory-bandwidth regime is UNREACHABLE under the harness cap. If the cap is raised, the memory-bound scale point anchored on measurement is n = 2^26 = 67,108,864 (0.183 s oracle, 512 MB/vector, 1.5 GB for validate()'s three vectors) — still 55x inside the 10 s budget.
benchmarks.prompt_restriction_needed: no. DEFINED for this operation (belong in the degenerate axis, NOT in a size floor):
- n = 0 (empty vector): defined, no-op. MEASURED: oracle returns, out.size() == 0.
- n = 1: defined (single element), MEASURED: in 34.018772 -> out 0.970604.
- n = 2: defined. Already in static_base_sizes.

Defined.

- any x_i == 0.0 or -0.0 -> -inf / +inf. MEASURED.

benchmarks.name: 58_transform_squaring
benchmarks.input_form: Single 1-D container: `std::vector<int> x` of length n; the operation is the in-place elementwise map x[i] <- x[i]*x[i]. Exactly one fill site, `elements_per_site: ["n"]`, `total_elements: "n"`, `explicit_values_supported: true` (thesis/enhanced_tests/benchmark_shapes.json, key "transform/58_transform_squaring"). Relevant dimension: n = number of int elements. Values come from `ENHANCED_FILL(input, -50, 50)` which without ENHANCED_* defines is `fillRand(input, -50, 50)`; for integral DType fillRand computes `rand() % (max - min) + min`, i.e. uniform integers in [-50, 49] (drivers/cpp/utilities.hpp:151, working tree). No second input, no derived counts, no structure (no matrix, no index arrays, no point sets). Comparison is EXACT integer equality via `reportAndCompareEq(correctResult, testResult, input)` — no epsilon exists for this benchmark (drivers/cpp/benchmarks/transform/58_transform_squaring/cpu.cc:68; helper at drivers/cpp/utilities.hpp:437).
benchmarks.min_size: 0 — there is no floor. The operation is total on every n >= 0: the oracle is `for (size_t i = 0; i < x.size(); i++) x[i] = x[i]*x[i];` (baseline.hpp:11-13), which is a well-defined empty loop at n = 0 and returns the empty vector. Measured: n=0 and n=1 both run cleanly through the oracle harness. 0/1/2/7 are already in `static_base_sizes` (thesis/config/config.yaml:562), so the harness itself treats 0 as a legal size.
benchmarks.max_size: 4096 — FORCED BY THE HARNESS, not by the operation. `max_spec_size: 4096` (thesis/config/config.yaml:572) is enforced in `validate_spec`: `if size > max_size: return False, "size %s exceeds max_spec_size %s"` (thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:293-294), and the spec-generation prompt states the schema as `"size": <int, 0..4096>` (thesis/enhanced_tests/generate_test_specs.py:185, 194). The operation itself imposes no upper bound; on this host memory capacity would bind long before arithmetic (see budget_adjustment).
benchmarks.special_conditions: NO structural condition on n: any n >= 0 is valid — no power of two, no minimum element count, no matrix/point-set form, no divisibility requirement. There is exactly ONE precondition, and it is on the VALUES, not on n: every element must satisfy |x_i| <= 46340, so that x_i*x_i is representable in a 32-bit signed int (measured: 46340^2 = 2147395600 <= INT_MAX; 46341^2 = 2147488281 > INT_MAX). Beyond that bound the ORACLE ITSELF commits signed-integer overflow, which is UB in C++ — the "expected" value is then a GCC/x86 wrap artifact rather than a mathematically defined result. Measured in-container (GCC 13.3, -O3, pipeline flags): extreme_values (pattern 6) gives INT_MIN -> 0 and INT_MAX -> 1; spike_at (pattern 9) gives (INT_MAX/2 = 1073741823) -> -2147483647; the exact boundary gives 46340 -> 2147395600 (correct) and 46341 -> -2147479015 (wrapped). Consequence for spec generation: patterns `extreme_values` and `spike_at` must NOT be used for this benchmark, and any `value_range` must stay inside [-46340, 46340]. Both patterns are currently offered globally (thesis/config/config.yaml:576-579) and `validate_spec` has no per-benchmark value check (thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:288-300ff) — see pending_fix. The default call-site range [-50, 49] is safe by a factor of ~927 in magnitude.
benchmarks.size_semantics: size == n == the element count of the single std::vector<int>. It is neither a side length nor a seed for a derived count (no nnz, no n*n). In validate() the size is `const size_t TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024);` (cpu.cc:50), i.e. the spec's `size` becomes -DENHANCED_TEST_SIZE and directly replaces 1024 (drivers/cpp/enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79, thesis/enhanced_tests/specs.py:403). explicit_values therefore needs exactly n values. DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE (serial/omp/mpi = (1<<22), drivers/problem-sizes.json:524-527) sizes only the TIMING context (`ctx->x.resize(DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE)`, cpu.cc:32) and is a separate axis that the enhanced stage builds at (1<<4); it does not interact with the spec size.
benchmarks.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra space — one integer multiply and one store per element, no inter-element dependence. A pure streaming elementwise map; asymptotically and practically memory-bandwidth-bound once the working set leaves cache (measured ~1.61 ns/element at n = 6.7e7, i.e. ~5 GB/s of read+write traffic).
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
Derived only from the operation, its domain, its complexity and the pipeline's launch geometry — no candidate code was read or consulted.

(1) The operation is a pure elementwise map with zero inter-element dependence. Therefore the ONLY thing that can vary with n is how an implementation PARTITIONS the index range. Two partition granularities exist in this pipeline: SIMD lane width (4/8/16 ints for SSE/AVX2/AVX-512) and the enhanced stage's fixed launch geometry `omp_threads: 4` / `mpi_ranks: 4` (thesis/config/config.yaml enhanced_launch, lines 601-605). The scale axis must therefore cover: below the partition width, indivisible by it, and exactly divisible by it.

(2) SMALL = 5. Strictly ABOVE the 4-way launch width but not a multiple of it (4-way split = 2+1+1+1, remainder 1: the classic `n/size` truncation bug), and strictly BELOW every SIMD width (4/8/16), so a vectorized loop is all-remainder and no full vector iteration ever executes. It is not already covered by `static_base_sizes` {0,1,2,7} (config.yaml:562), and it is exactly the length of the example given in the problem statement itself ([5, 1, 2, -4, 8] — thesis/prompts/generation-prompts-thesis.json, all three parallelism models), so it is anchored in the specification rather than in any implementation. Working set 3*5*4 B = 60 B.

(3) MEDIUM = 257 = 2^8 + 1, prime. n mod 4 = 1 (uneven 4-way split 65+64+64+64 -> rank/thread imbalance and remainder handling), n mod 8 = n mod 16 = 1 -> exactly ONE element remains after the last full vector chunk. This is the canonical "one past the last full block" boundary for a map and is derived purely from the lane/worker arithmetic. Working set 3*257*4 B ~ 3 KB, fully L1-resident.

(4) LARGE = 4096 = 2^12. It is the harness maximum (max_spec_size) and, at the same time, the clean divisible counterpart to MEDIUM: divisible by 4 ranks, by 4 threads and by every SIMD width, so the fully vectorized / fully parallel path runs with NO tail at all. It is also the only admissible point where validate()'s working set (3 vectors: input, correctResult, testResult = 3*4096*4 B = 48 KB, cpu.cc:54/59/63) exceeds a typical 32 KB L1 and reaches L2 — i.e. the only point in [0, 4096] where the map is not purely L1-resident.

(5) The three points span three orders of magnitude inside the admissible range and cover both partition regimes (indivisible/tail-dominated vs. divisible/tail-free) plus the sub-worker-width regime. They are deliberately NOT the same triple another benchmark would get: 5 follows from the 4-rank launch and the prompt's own example, 257 from int SIMD widths, 4096 from the harness cap plus the L1 boundary for a 3-buffer int workload — all specific to a 1-D int elementwise map.

(6) The 10 s runtime budget plays no role in the choice here because it is non-binding by ~6 orders of magnitude (see budget_adjustment); the binding constraint is the harness cap.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
DEFINED (belong on the degenerate axis, all safe to use):
- n = 0: empty vector in, empty vector out; oracle loop executes zero times (baseline.hpp:11). Measured OK. Already in static_base_sizes.
- n = 1: single element squared. Already in static_base_sizes.
- all_zeros (pattern 1): defined; 0 is a FIXED POINT of squaring (0^2 = 0), so an implementation that writes nothing at all still passes — low discriminating power, must never be the only case.
- all_same (pattern 2) at the DEFAULT range: `enhancedMidValue(-50, 50)` = -50 + 100/2 = 0 (drivers/cpp/enhanced-fill.hpp:144-150, 187-188), so all_same COLLAPSES to all_zeros for this benchmark unless an explicit value_range is given. Worth knowing: two offered patterns produce the identical input here.
- all elements = +/-1: fixed points (1^2 = 1, (-1)^2 = 1) — same weakness as all_zeros; only the -1 case tests sign handling.
- alternating (pattern 5) at the default range: values -50, +50, ... — maximal sign coverage; +50 lies outside fillRand's own [-50, 49] but well inside the safe value domain.
- ascending/descending (patterns 3/4) integral ramp: `lo + position % (span+1)` with span = 100 -> values cycle through [-50, 50] (enhanced-fill.hpp:114-119) — safe.
- all values negative: the one real semantic trap of this operation (every output must be non-negative for |x| <= 46340); ordinary rather than degenerate, but it is what makes non-trivial cases discriminating.

NOT DEFINED (outside the domain — do NOT treat as degenerate-but-valid):
- extreme_values (pattern 6) and spike_at (pattern 9), and any value_range with |v| > 46340: signed-integer overflow inside the ORACLE itself, i.e. UB. Measured expected values are wrap artifacts (INT_MIN^2 -> 0, INT_MAX^2 -> 1, (INT_MAX/2)^2 -> -2147483647). Such a spec does not test "square every element"; it tests whether candidate and oracle happen to wrap the same way under the same compiler.

benchmarks.name: 59_transform_map_function
benchmarks.input_form: One dense integer vector `x` (`std::vector<int>`, n elements) plus one pre-sized boolean output bitset `mask` (`std::vector<bool>`, n elements). The operation is a pure elementwise map f: Z -> {false,true}, f(v) = isPowerOfTwo(v) = (v > 0) && !(v & (v-1)); mask[i] = f(x[i]). Exactly ONE relevant dimension: n = element count of x (mask has the same n). Driver value domain: uniform integers in [1, 1024] (cpu.cc:59 `ENHANCED_FILL(input, 1, 1025)` -> utilities.hpp:151 `rand() % (max-min) + min`). Comparison is EXACT equality on bool, no epsilon (cpu.cc:72 `reportAndCompareEq`, utilities.hpp:437).
benchmarks.min_size: 0 (no mathematical floor: a map over an empty index set is the empty map). Every n >= 0 is a valid input; n = 0 is exercised safely end-to-end (see degenerate_cases). No structural precondition of any kind.
benchmarks.max_size: Not forced by the operation (the map is defined for every n). Two ceilings imposed elsewhere: (1) HARD, correctness: the oracle's loop counter is `int` -- baseline.hpp:20 `for (int i = 0; i < x.size(); i++)` -- and so is fillRand's (utilities.hpp:146), so n > INT_MAX = 2,147,483,647 is signed-overflow UB in the REFERENCE itself. Unreachable in practice (8.6 GB for x alone). (2) PRACTICAL, measured on the pipeline host (7,775 MB container): the oracle is stable up to a ~277 MB single-process footprint (n = 2^26, median 0.441 s over 5 reps) and falls off a memory-pressure cliff at ~554 MB (n = 2^27, median 5.752 s with a 19.554 s outlier over 3 reps -- that one WOULD breach the 10 s budget). With mpi_ranks = 4 each holding a full copy of x, keep n <~ 3e7.
benchmarks.special_conditions: NONE from the operation: n need not be a power of two, need not be even, and the values are unconstrained (any `int`, including 0 and negatives, is in the domain of isPowerOfTwo). The only two size properties that carry DISCRIMINATING power come from the output type + the fixed harness launch, not from the math: (1) the random-fill mask is non-vacuous only if E[#true] = n * 11/1024 is comfortably above 1, i.e. n >= ~1000; (2) because the output is `std::vector<bool>` (64 elements packed per machine word), n must be chosen so that n / 4 is NOT a multiple of 64 (config.yaml:603-604 fixes omp_threads = 4 and mpi_ranks = 4), otherwise every static-schedule worker boundary lands exactly on a word boundary and the dominant defect class for this benchmark -- concurrent read-modify-write on a shared bitset word -- is structurally masked. All three chosen sizes satisfy both.
benchmarks.size_semantics: n = number of ELEMENTS in the vector x (and, identically, in the output bitset mask). Not a side length, not a derived nnz. The domain-table sizes are VALIDATION sizes: they are injected through `-DENHANCED_TEST_SIZE=<n>` which overrides `const size_t TEST_SIZE = ENHANCED_TEST_SIZE_DEFAULT(1024)` (cpu.cc:54, enhanced-fill.hpp:75-79). They are independent of DRIVER_PROBLEM_SIZE (problem-sizes.json:533-541: serial/omp/mpi = (1<<21)), which only sizes the timing Context (cpu.cc:35-36) and which the enhanced stage builds at (1<<4).
benchmarks.complexity: Theta(n) time -- exactly n loop iterations, each one compare + one bitwise AND + one bit write (baseline.hpp:19-26). Theta(n) input space (4n bytes) and Theta(n/8) output space (packed bitset). No reduction, no dependence between elements. Memory-bandwidth / bitset-RMW bound at scale: measured 5.4 ns per element single-threaded at n = 25e6 (GCC 13.3, -O3, NO_INLINE forces the oracle out of line at O3).
benchmarks.domain_rationale:
Derived only from the operation, its domain, its complexity and the runtime budget -- no candidate code was consulted.

FLOOR (statistical, operation-derived). The driver fills x uniformly over the 1024 integers [1, 1024] (cpu.cc:59 + utilities.hpp:144-152). Exactly 11 of those are powers of two (2^0..2^10), so p(true) = 11/1024 = 0.010742. P(the whole mask is false) = (1-p)^n: n=128 -> 25%, n=256 -> 6.3%, n=512 -> 0.4%, n=1000 -> 2.2e-5. Below ~1000 a non-negligible share of random draws yields an all-false mask, which a "write false everywhere" implementation passes -- the test is vacuous. n = 1000 is therefore the smallest scale at which the random-fill test reliably separates the two output classes. Measured confirmation: n=1000 produced 9-15 true entries per draw; n=25e6 produced 268,395-269,325 vs the predicted 268,555.

SMALL = 1000. The statistical floor, and simultaneously the cache-resident regime: 4 KB input + 125 B mask -> entirely inside L1d (48 KB/core on the pipeline host, i7-12700H). Isolates loop/index correctness from any memory effect. 1000/4 = 250, 250 mod 64 = 58 -> worker boundaries fall inside bitset words. Measured oracle: 4 us.

MEDIUM = 1,000,000. The out-of-L1/L2, still-in-L3 regime: 4 MB input + 125 KB mask vs 1.25 MB L2 per core and 24 MB shared L3. This is the intermediate scale neither endpoint covers, and it is the cheapest size at which a partitioned implementation must already handle thousands of interior word boundaries (mask spans 15,625 64-bit words). 1e6/4 = 250,000, 250000 mod 64 = 16 -> boundaries mid-word. Measured oracle: 0.0036 s.

LARGE = 25,000,000. Three constraints intersect. (a) DRAM-streaming regime: the input alone must clear the 24 MB L3 by a wide margin -> 4n >= ~96 MB -> n >= 2.4e7. At 25e6 the working set is 100 MB input + 3.1 MB mask = 103 MB = 4.3x L3, so the Theta(n) map is unambiguously bandwidth-bound rather than cache-resident. (b) No NEW class of defect becomes reachable above this scale: the only size-triggered failure modes left are int-index overflow (n > 2^31) and MPI int count/displacement overflow (n > 2^31 per rank), both requiring >= 8.6 GB for x alone and therefore unreachable on any machine this pipeline runs on -- so growing LARGE further buys nothing but cost. (c) Memory: the MPI prompt states every rank holds a COMPLETE copy of x, and config.yaml:604 fixes mpi_ranks = 4, so the aggregate footprint is 4 x (4n + 2*n/8) = 425 MB at n = 25e6, comfortably inside the 7.775 GB container, and each rank's 106 MB stays well below the measured single-process stability limit (see budget_adjustment). 25e6/4 = 6,250,000, 6250000 mod 64 = 16 -> boundaries mid-word.

NOTE ON THE 10 s BUDGET. It is satisfied with a 74x margin and is NOT the binding constraint for this benchmark; memory is. At the measured 5.4 ns/element, reaching 10 s would need n ~ 1.85e9, i.e. 7.4 GB for x alone (times 4 under mpi_ranks=4) -- larger than the whole container. This is reported rather than silently replaced by a different budget: the budget is an upper bound, it holds, and the actual ceiling is stated separately in max_size. There is also no accuracy ceiling (exact bool equality, no epsilon), so nothing except memory limits LARGE from above.

The ladder is 1e3 -> 1e6 -> 2.5e7 (1000x then 25x); the three points are L1-resident / L3-resident / DRAM-streaming. It is not shared with any sibling transform benchmark by convenience -- the floor of 1000 follows from this benchmark's specific 11/1024 power-of-two density in its specific fill range, and the non-multiple-of-256 rule follows from its specific `std::vector<bool>` output type. A `float`-output transform of the same shape would get neither constraint.

benchmarks.degenerate_cases:
All of the following are MATHEMATICALLY DEFINED for this operation and belong on the degenerate axis, not the scale axis:
- n = 0 (empty vector): defined, mask is empty. Safe end to end -- enhanced-fill.hpp:177-179 early-returns on n == 0, fillRand loops zero times, the oracle loops zero times, and the comparator returns true for two empty vectors (utilities.hpp:344-357 size check passes, total == 0). VERIFIED by measurement (harness ran n = 0 cleanly).
- n = 1: defined. But under the driver's random fill P(that element is a power of two) = 11/1024 ~ 1%, so the mask is almost surely all-false and the test is VACUOUS unless combined with a deterministic pattern (all_zeros, explicit_values). VERIFIED by measurement (n = 1 ran cleanly, 0 true entries).
- all values 0 (`all_zeros`, enhanced-fill.hpp:185): defined, f(0) = false. THE highest-value degenerate input for this benchmark: `!(x & (x-1))` alone evaluates to true for x = 0, so only the `x > 0` guard produces the correct false. A dropped guard is invisible under the driver's default fill range [1,1024], which never emits 0.
- all values equal (`all_same`, enhanced-fill.hpp:188): midpoint of [1,1025] = 513, not a power of two -> all-false mask. Defined but vacuous on its own.
- extreme values (`extreme_values`, enhanced-fill.hpp:200): INT_MIN / INT_MAX alternating. Both defined and both false. INT_MIN is the second high-value discriminator: an implementation without the `x > 0` guard computes INT_MIN & (INT_MIN-1), which under two's-complement wrap is 0 -> wrongly true. The REFERENCE is safe here because `&&` short-circuits, so the oracle never evaluates `x-1` at INT_MIN (no UB in the baseline).
- negative values in general: defined, always false.
- ascending/descending ramp (enhanced-fill.hpp:191/194, integral branch: value = 1 + (i mod 1025)): defined, cycles through every power of two 1..1024 -> a dense, deterministic 11-per-1025 true pattern. Useful as the non-random positive control.
No degenerate case here is out of domain -- unlike the fft/geometry/linear-algebra families, this operation has no undefined inputs at all.

Adjusted DOWN to 25,000,000 (measured median 0.136 s). The adjustment was NOT forced by the 10 s time budget -- 2^26 met it with a 22x margin -- but by two other constraints: (a) memory, since the MPI prompt gives every rank a complete copy of x and config.yaml:604 fixes mpi_ranks = 4, so 2^26 means a 1.14 GB aggregate footprint plus the candidate's own buffers, versus 425 MB at 25e6; and (b) the `std::vector<bool>` word-alignment criterion -- 2^26/4 = 16,777,216 is an exact multiple of 64, so every static-schedule worker boundary would land on a bitset word boundary and mask the dominant defect class, whereas 25,000,000/4 = 6,250,000 leaves remainder 16 mod 64. Separately excluded as over budget: n = 2^27 = 134,217,728, measured median 5.752 s over 3 reps with a 19.554 s outlier (554 MB footprint, memory-pressure cliff) -- that size is unstable and breaches 10 s on a loaded host.
